articles.title: Astros To Add Aaron Bates, J.P. Martinez To Coaching Staff
body: The Astros are hiring J.P. Martinez as their pitching coach and Aaron Bates as hitting coach, as first reported by Chandler Rome and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. Brian McTaggart of MLB.com reports that Triple-A manager Mickey Storey is also being promoted to the big league staff in an undetermined role.

Houston fired pitching coach Josh Miller this afternoon, a few weeks after announcing that he’d return to the staff. There hasn’t been any official word on 2026 hitting coach Victor Rodríguez, who was also expected back at the beginning of the offseason. Bates’ hiring might suggest they’re going in a different direction, though they could theoretically use a co-hitting coach setup if they want to keep Rodríguez on staff.

Bates departed the Dodgers’ organization a couple weeks ago after failing to come to terms on a new contract. He reportedly interviewed for the Yankees’ hitting coach vacancy. He’ll instead end up in Houston, where he’ll join Brad Ausmus’ staff. The 42-year-old Bates had spent the previous 12 seasons in Los Angeles.

The Dodgers have had one of the best offenses in the league over the last few years. Their entire coaching staff has had plenty of impact talent with which to work, of course. Bates will now get to coach unanimous AL MVP Yordan Alvarez, who carried an otherwise inconsistent lineup. Houston led the majors with 226 home runs but ranked 13th in scoring. They were 18th in batting average and 19th in on-base percentage, ranking middle of the pack in both strikeouts and walks.

articles.title: Royals Sign Caleb Thielbar
body: The Royals announced that they have signed left-hander Caleb Thielbar to a one-year deal. It’s reportedly a $3.25MM guarantee for the ISE Baseball client. Kansas City had an open 40-man roster spot and didn’t need to make a corresponding move.

Thielbar, 40 in January, is a veteran southpaw reliever. It took him a while to get established in the big leagues but he has been a fairly steady performer this decade. Thielbar made his debut back in 2013 but still had fewer than 100 big league innings by the end of 2015. He was then stuck in the minors for several years, not appearing in the majors from 2016 to 2019.

He returned to the show with the Twins in 2020 and hasn’t looked back. Over the past seven seasons, he has thrown 329 1/3 innings with a 3.66 earned run average, split between the Twins and Cubs. He has struck out 28.2% of batters faced in that time while limiting walks to a 7.9% pace. He racked up eight saves and 86 holds in that span. His fastball usually sits around 93 miles per hour while he also throws a slider and curveball.

Last offseason, Thielbar signed a $4.5MM deal with the Cubs. His ERA unfortunately spiked to 4.86 with Chicago this year, though still with good peripherals. His 28.3% strikeout rate was well above league average and right around his usual pace. His 8.5% walk rate was right around average and his typical lane. What led to more runs was a spike in homers. He allowed 11 home runs, a rate of 16.4% per fly ball. His previous career high was eight homers. His career home-run-to-flyball rate is 9.3%. League average is usually around 11%.

articles.title: Nationals To Sign Luis Curvelo To Minor League Deal
body: The Nationals have agreed to sign right-hander Luis Curvelo to a minor league deal, reports Kiley McDaniel of ESPN. The Ballengee Group client receives an invite to big league camp in spring training.

Curvelo, 26, pitched for the Rangers in the two most recent big league seasons. Over those two campaigns, he logged a combined 29 1/3 innings but allowed 23 earned runs, giving him an unpleasant 7.06 ERA. He was designated for assignment in August and cleared waivers. He became a free agent at season’s end.

The Nats are presumably overlooking Curvelo’s numbers in that small sample of big league work. The stuff is intriguing, as both his four-seamer and sinker have averaged over 95 miles per hour in his career thus far. He has also thrown a splitter, slider and changeup.

His results in the minors have generally been good, though he struggled in the Pacific Coast League. Initially a Mariners prospect, he tossed 226 2/3 innings on the farm from 2021 to 2024, topping out at the Double-A level. In that span, he had a 3.61 ERA. His 8.5% walk rate was around average while his 29.3% strikeout rate was very strong.

He became a minor league free agent after 2024 and signed with the Rangers going into 2025. As mentioned, his big league results thus far have not been good. He also tossed 81 1/3 innings for Triple-A Round Rock over the past two seasons with a 5.09 ERA, 21.9% strikeout rate and 10.8% walk rate.

articles.title: MLB Offers To Raise Minimum Salary To $1MM In Latest Cap Proposal
body: Major League Baseball made its latest proposal on core economics on Monday. The league offered to raise the minimum salary to $1MM for all players, a modest increase over their previous proposal of a $900K minimum for those with less than two years of service time (links via Bob Nightengale of USA TODAY, Alden González of ESPN, and Ronald Blum of The Associated Press). Of course, that’s yet again conditioned on the Players Association agreeing to a salary cap/floor system.

Under MLB’s proposal, pre-arbitration players who accrue a full year of service time and spent less than half the season on the injured list would receive an additional $100K. It’d be a $220K rise over this year’s $780K minimum salary. MLB also offered a 5% signing bonus for arbitration-eligible players who sign without a hearing, plus a $500K bonus for one veteran player per season who signs a one-year contract for $10MM or less.

As long as the sides remain divided on the overarching cap vs. luxury tax framework, all of their proposals amount to talking past one another. To that end, the MLBPA accepted the league’s previous offer for equal distribution of local media revenues — but conditional on the absence of the cap. Any “agreements” at this point are essentially meaningless.

articles.title: Guardians Sign Jairo Iriarte To Minor League Deal
body: The Guardians announced Monday that they’ve signed right-hander Jairo Iriarte to a minor league contract. He’s been invited to major league spring training. Iriarte is represented by Klutch Sports.

Iriarte, 25 next month, is a former top prospect in both the Padres and White Sox systems. He’s one of four players who went from San Diego to Chicago — alongside Drew Thorpe, Samuel Zavala and Steven Wilson — in the 2024 trade sending Dylan Cease to the Friars.

Iriarte only has six big league innings under his belt. Those came as a member of the 2024 ChiSox, and he held opponents to one run in that time. At that point, the South Siders were still intent on developing Iriarte as a starter. He pitched 126 Double-A frames in 2024, his age-22 season, posting a 3.71 ERA in that span. An audition in the White Sox’ big league rotation didn’t appear to be that far off.

The 2025 season, however, was a disaster. Iriarte spent the majority of the season in Triple-A, logging a 7.24 ERA in 46 innings. The Sox sent him to extended spring training for a reset after a tough five starts to begin the season. He returned in late May as a reliever but didn’t find better results. The Sox passed him through waivers unclaimed last February.

articles.title: Latest Details On Tarik Skubal Bidding
body: The Mets landed their top target on Sunday evening, agreeing to a nine-year contract with Tarik Skubal. The deal, which is pending a physical, comes with a record-setting $450MM guarantee that allowed New York to win the bidding over other suitors like the Blue Jays and Padres.

Skubal’s contract contains a $45MM signing bonus and $30MM in deferred money, so the net present value is slightly below the baseline $450MM figure. Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reports that the final NPV calculation is expected to be around $437-438MM. That still puts it more than $100MM clear of the previous record deal for a pitcher, Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325MM contract. Skubal and Gerrit Cole were the only other pitchers to command nine-plus years in recent history.

It’s the fourth-largest guarantee in league history — behind those secured by Juan Soto, Shohei Ohtani and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Ohtani’s contract is behind Guerrero’s $500MM extension in terms of net present value because of the deferrals, valued by MLB just shy of $461MM for luxury tax purposes and around $437.8MM by the Players Association.

As one would expect, the Mets didn’t open the bidding at $450MM. Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic reported that their first official proposal late last week was at $350MM. According to Bob Nightengale of USA TODAY, that initial offer was on a seven-year term. Jon Heyman of The New York Post writes that the Mets made their first offer on Friday, so the sides quickly progressed to reach the agreement around 48 hours later.

articles.title: Yankees To Sign Brent Suter
body: The Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have reportedly agreed to a one-year deal with a club option for 2028. It’s a $4MM guarantee for the Diamond Sports Management client in the form of a $3.75MM salary next year then a $250K buyout on the option, which is valued at $3.5MM. The Yanks have a couple of 40-man vacancies and won’t need to make a corresponding move.

Suter, 37, is a soft-tossing veteran lefty who has carved out a lengthy career by minimizing damage. His four-seamer has sat in the 86-88 miles-per-hour range for most of his career, well south of average in this era. His sinker is usually a bit faster but still averages under 90 mph. He also threw a slider and changeup last year.

As you might expect for that velocity, he doesn’t miss a ton of bats. Suter has a 20% strikeout rate in his career and was at 20.7% in 2026. This year’s league average rate was 22.1%. But Suter’s 6.2% walk rate in his career and his 6.6% pace in 2026 are both a couple of ticks better than par. His 44.6% ground ball rate for his career is also a good figure and he was up to 49.8% this year.

Statcast is generally impressed by Suter’s ability to keep hitters off balance. His 31% hard-hit rate this year was in the 94th percentile of qualified pitchers. He allowed an average exit velocity of 86.6 mph in 2026, putting him in the 92nd percentile. His 6.7% barrel rate was in the 65th percentile. Though Suter doesn’t blow opponents away, his control and knack for inducing soft contact have allowed him to throw 688 1/3 big league innings with a 3.54 earned run average.

articles.title: Blue Jays Offered Tarik Skubal Nine-Year Deal In $420MM Range
body: November 23: Jon Heyman of The New York Post reports that Toronto’s offer checked in at $420MM over nine years.

November 22: The Mets outpaced the market in signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450MM agreement earlier today, setting a new record as the largest contract ever given to a pitcher. The Dodgers, Padres, and Blue Jays were the other suitors known to be in on Skubal, and The Athletic’s Mitch Bannon reports that Toronto also offered Skubal a nine-year pact worth a little more than $400MM.

The Jays’ offer adds some context to the bidding process, and how Skubal’s final price tag ended up at $450MM. MLB Network’s Jim Duquette wrote on Friday that the Mets’ “initial” offer to Skubal was also nine years and around $400MM, essentially in line with Toronto’s number. Adding another $50MM or so put the Mets clearly in front, and it was enough to get Skubal to put pen to paper.

As ESPN’s Alden Gonzalez wrote earlier today, the Dodgers didn’t end up making Skubal a formal offer, though Los Angeles was willing to make a long-term offer, contrary to past reports that the Dodgers were looking for a shorter-term deal that would’ve paid Skubal a higher average annual value. There hasn’t been any word on what San Diego might’ve had on the table for Skubal, but according to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale, the Padres “had no interest in making an offer in that stratosphere.”

articles.title: The Best Fits For Teruaki Sato
body: MLBTR continues to give subscribers detailed looks at the markets for top free agents. In this edition, we look at Teruaki Sato, who is almost certainly going to sign very shortly. His 45-day posting window technically goes into the middle of December but a lockout is expected to begin on December 2. Since the posting window will not be paused for the lockout, Sato and other players posted by NPB teams should reach agreements in the next week or so.

The team that grabs Sato will be betting on the bat. The lefty swinger hit 40 home runs for the Hanshin Tigers in 2025 and 39 this year. His slash line in 2026 was.306/.383/.609, which translated to a 196 wRC+.

His defensive fit is more of a question. He has mostly been a third baseman thus far, with a decent amount of corner outfield work also mixed in. His defense at the hot corner isn’t considered strong but some evaluators think he can be developed into a viable third baseman. Others think he should just be moved to the outfield or first base right away. The 30 MLB teams will have varying opinions about the best path forward but, in theory, he could fit with just about any club with a need in a corner or the designated hitter spot.

Turning back to the bat, though the power is real, there are also yellow flags. Somewhat akin to Munetaka Murakami last offseason, there are questions about the approach. Both players hit a lot of home runs in Japan but with lots of strikeouts. The overall quality of pitching in MLB is higher than that of NPB, so hitters usually strike out more when moving from Japan to North America.

articles.title: Trade Rumors Front Office Subscriber Chat Transcript
body: Skubal off the board. Just over one week left on the lockout clock. Going to be a hectic few days! We’ll talk all things hot stove starting at 2pm CT, but feel free to send questions my way ahead of time! As we get underway, Jeff Passan reporting the Yankees are signing Brent Suter for a year and $4MM Would expect quite a few more transactions in the next eight days! Ha Let’s begin BhamBrave
If a free agent signs a deal before the lockout that includes a signing bonus, does he get it before the lockout? Steve Adams

Depends. Some bonuses are paid up front. Others are spread across several years and stipulated to be paid out on specific dates. Regardless, signing bonus money will go to the player in the event games are missed. Joe

Steve Cohen has pretty much thumbed his nose at a salary cap. If they do get one in the new CBA, how do you think they’ll handle the Mets being over it with no real way to drop below anytime soon? Steve Adams

articles.title: Pitching Coach Josh Miller Will Not Return To Astros In 2027
body: The Astros previously announced that pitching coach Josh Miller would be back for the 2027 season, but it seems there’s been a change of plans. Brian McTaggart of MLB.com reports that Miller will not be back next year, ostensibly ending a 16-year run with the organization.

Notably, the announcement regarding Miller’s return was made prior to the hiring of Brad Ausmus as Houston’s new skipper. Whether that played into things or whether Miller had a change of heart for other reasons remains unclear. Either way, the ‘Stros find themselves in the market for a new pitching coach. The Astros also have a few prominent vacancies on the staff, including a third base coach, bullpen coach and assistant hitting and pitching coaches.

Miller, 48 in February, was a minor league pitcher and spent time pitching professionally in Taiwan as well. He’s been Houston’s major league pitching coach for the past six seasons and spent the two prior years as their bullpen coach. Before that, he worked as a scout and minor league coach/coordinator within the system. Miller was Houston’s bullpen coach under former pitching coach Brent Strom, who returned to the organization as a “pitching consultant” a few months back, but it seems that relationship won’t keep him around on Ausmus’ big league staff.

articles.title: Tanner Rainey Signs With NPB’s Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters
body: Former Tigers reliever Tanner Rainey is heading to Japan. The righty has agreed to a deal with the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters, per a team announcement.

Rainey appeared in six games with Detroit this past season. He allowed three earned runs over seven innings and had more walks (8) than strikeouts (6). The veteran righty spent the majority of the year with Triple-A Toledo. He recorded a solid 3.40 ERA and picked up five saves in 45 appearances out of the Mud Hens’ bullpen.

The 33-year-old Rainey has pitched for four teams across parts of nine MLB seasons. The majority of his time in the majors came with the Nationals. He joined Washington in December 2018 in a trade that sent right-hander Tanner Roark to the Reds.

The Tanner-for-Tanner swap worked out well for the Nationals, at least initially. Rainey was a steady member of the bullpen for multiple seasons. He stepped up as the club’s closer in 2022, recording a dozen saves and a respectable 3.30 ERA. Rainey went down midway through that season with an elbow injury that ultimately required Tommy John surgery. He missed the majority of the 2023 campaign and has struggled to perform in the majors since then.

Rainey’s fastball was down to 94 mph in his final year with the Nationals, but he’s regained some of his lost velocity recently. He sat at 96.8 mph with the heater in his brief time with the Tigers this year. That’s his best mark since 2022. Rainey also added a curveball to his arsenal this season. He’s been a two-pitch guy for most of his career, so the addition of the curve is notable.

articles.title: Nationals Sign Jared Simpson, Marc Church To Minor League Deals
body: The Nationals announced a pair of minor league signings on Monday. Left-hander Jared Simpson is back in the organization. Right-hander Marc Church is joining the club after departing from the Rangers. Both deals include invitations to MLB Spring Training.

Washington did not tender a contract to Simpson by Friday’s deadline. He hit free agency, along with right-hander Josiah Gray and left-hander Carson Palmquist. Simpson’s time on the open market lasted a weekend. He’s back with the only team he’s known as a professional.

Simpson debuted with the Nationals in September. He tossed three perfect innings out of the bullpen in the first appearance of his career. Simpson delivered another perfect frame in his second outing, but the wheels came off from there. The lefty allowed five earned runs while recording one out across his final two games with the team.

The 26-year-old Simpson was one of several versatile arms Washington trotted out in a hybrid role. He made three relief outings and one appearance as an opener. Simpson had made 10 starts and 34 relief appearances in the minors before his call-up. He’s typically missed bats at a strong clip, but has had trouble throwing strikes. That flaw was evident in his brief MLB stint, as he walked seven in 4 1/3 innings. Simpson could fill multiple roles on a Washington pitching staff with few sure things heading into 2027.

articles.title: Blue Jays Interested In Trevor Rogers, Freddy Peralta
body: After coming up short in the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, the Blue Jays are moving on to the remaining top names on the starting pitching market. Toronto is interested in Trevor Rogers and Freddy Peralta, reports Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet.

Peralta and Rogers can be added to the ever-expanding list of targets for the Blue Jays, which also includes Michael King and Kaima Taira. The club hasn’t made any additions yet, but it’s not due to lack of effort. Their pitch to Skubal was reportedly nine years and over $400MM. Toronto made an offer to righty Jonathan Loaisiga before he signed with the Yankees. An acquisition of some form seems likely given the Blue Jays’ willingness to spend and frequent connections to free agents.

Rogers received a qualifying offer from the Orioles, so he comes with draft pick compensation attached. That didn’t stop him from ranking No. 2 on our Top 50 Free Agents list. After Skubal, he’s the prize of the available starting pitchers. Rogers should command nine figures this winter.

The 29-year-old Rogers is coming off a decent season in Baltimore. He posted a 4.03 ERA with modest strikeout numbers and a strong 5.6% walk rate. Perhaps more importantly, Rogers made 30 starts for the first time as a big leaguer. He tossed a career-high 169 2/3 innings.

articles.title: Dodgers, Robert Stephenson Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Dodgers and right-handed reliever Robert Stephenson are in agreement on a minor league contract, per Katie Woo and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. The Apex Baseball client missed all of the 2026 campaign due to elbow surgery and had a 2027 club option declined by the Angels earlier this offseason.

Stephenson, 34 in February, had been with the Halos on a three-year, $33MM deal that’ll prove to be one of the more substantial free agent missteps from any team in recent years. The right-hander enjoyed a dominant 2023 run with the Rays, parlaying that dominance into a three-year contract that would’ve seemed unthinkable a few months prior.

The deal blew up in the Angels’ face not because Stephenson performed poorly but because he was barely able to perform at all. Stephenson opened the 2024 season on the injured list after suffering an injury during spring training. It was eventually revealed to be a UCL tear that required Tommy John surgery and cost him the entirety of the 2024 campaign. Stephenson returned in May of 2025 but was back on the shelf less than a week later due to a biceps injury. He returned in late August and pitched well down the stretch but wound up totaling only 10 innings in year two of his contract.

Those are the only 10 innings thrown by Stephenson in an Angels uniform. He experienced renewed arm discomfort this past spring, and in early April then-manager Kurt Suzuki announced that Stephenson had undergone a second UCL repair — this time with an accompanying flexor repair. Stephenson didn’t pitch all season and is likely to be sidelined into next summer.

articles.title: Mets To Sign Paul Goldschmidt
body: 9:23am: Goldschmidt will sign a one-year, $8MM contract, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. Since the Mets are perennial luxury payors who are well into the top tier of penalty, they’d be in line for a 110% tax on that sum under the existing luxury-tax system. Goldschmidt will cost them $16.8MM overall. That number could potentially climb higher, as Joel Sherman of the New York Post adds that the deal contains $2MM of incentives.
8:57am: The Mets and free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt are in agreement on a deal, reports Robert Murray of FanSided. Goldschmidt is a client of Excel Sports Management.

It’s a quick follow-up to yesterday’s record deal for two-time American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. While the 39-year-old Goldschmidt certainly isn’t the marquee addition he would’ve been during his NL MVP-winning prime, the future Hall of Famer remains a productive role player who can handle at least a platoon timeshare at first base.

Goldschmidt was one of the top bats on the market in terms of production versus left-handed pitching, and the four-time Gold Glove winner still grades as a strong defender at first base, even if the limited role he now occupies in the late stages of his career means he’s unlikely to log enough innings to have a chance at a fifth.

Goldschmidt also spent the 2026 season in New York — but in pinstripes over in the Bronx. He appeared in 105 games and totaled 380 plate appearances, hitting.252/.343/.452 with 18 homers, 13 doubles, a triple, a 7.6% walk rate and a 22.6% strikeout rate.

articles.title: Mets To Sign Tarik Skubal
body: The Mets have made another blockbuster addition, as the club has signed two-time AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450MM contract. The deal is a straight nine-year pact with no opt-outs and a full no-trade clause. Skubal will get the first $45MM of his deal as a signing bonus, and $30MM of the southpaw’s future salary will be deferred. The contract will become official once Skubal passes a physical. Skubal is represented by the Boras Corporation.

As many expected heading into the offseason, Skubal has landed the largest contract ever given to a pitcher, with his $450MM payday far exceeding the $325MM Yoshinobu Yamamoto received from the Dodgers (over a 12-year term) in December 2023. Skubal’s contract is the fourth largest guaranteed salary given to any player, topped only by Juan Soto’s $765MM from the Mets two years ago, the $700MM Shohei Ohtani received from the Dodgers, and Vladimir Guerrero’s $500MM extension with the Blue Jays. Depending on how the deferrals are calculated, Skubal for now has the third-highest average annual value ever, behind Kyle Tucker and Soto.

MLB Trade Rumors naturally ranked Skubal in the top spot on our list of the offseason’s top 50 free agents, and his $450MM deal is even further north of our nine-year, $425MM projection. Steve Adams and Darragh McDonald each predicted Skubal would sign with the Mets, which was a logical choice given both New York’s severe need for starting pitching, and the fact that the Mets are one of the few teams willing and able to meet Skubal’s huge asking price.

articles.title: Astros, Blue Jays, Padres Interested In Randy Arozarena
body: The Astros, Blue Jays, and Padres are among the teams “monitoring” Randy Arozarena’s market, according to reporter Francys Romero. This trio of clubs joins the Orioles, Phillies, and Yankees as teams linked to the free agent outfielder to date.

Arozarena hits the open market in advance of his age-32 season, and on the heels of a fantastic 2026 that saw the outfielder hit.281/.381/.484 with 26 homers over 670 plate appearance for the Mariners. The three slash category numbers and Arozrena’s 151 wRC+ were all career bests, and he also stole 26 bases in 34 attempts. This performance earned Arozarena an eighth-place finish in AL MVP voting, as well as a Silver Slugger Award and his third career All-Star nod.

As noted in our breakdown of Arozarena in MLBTR’s top 50 free agent rankings, his bat speed fell off sharply in 2026. Between that troubling number, the decent amount of swing-and-miss in his game, and his defensive limitations as a left field-only player, Arozarena has his share of flaws, beyond the fact that he has generally been more of a solid player than the superstar he appeared to be in 2026.

Still, this didn’t keep Arozarena from landing the fifth spot in our top 50, and he was projected to sign a four-year, $100MM contract. This is significantly lower than the six-year, $150MM deal Arozarena and agent Scott Boras are reportedly hoping to land, though aiming high is a natural part of the negotiation process.

articles.title: Rockies Hire Scott Servais For Front Office Role
body: Scott Servais has joined the Rockies as the team’s new senior director of baseball operations, according to Dennis Lin and Will Sammon of The Athletic. Servais has been a special assistant in the Padres organization for the past two seasons, coming off a nine-year run as the Mariners’ manager.

This isn’t Servais’ first stint in Colorado, as he played in 33 games for the Rox back in 2000 and also 39 games for the Rockies’ Triple-A club in 2002 (Servais’ final season as a player). Current Rockies GM Josh Byrnes was the team’s assistant general manager during Servais’ playing days in Denver, and Servais will now join Byrnes in the front office under president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta.

Servais posted a 680-642 record as Seattle’s skipper, though with just one playoff appearance to show for his eight-plus seasons. The Mariners had a modest 64-64 record when Servais was fired in August 2024, and after catching on in San Diego, Servais re-emerged as a popular interview candidate during last winter’s managerial carousel. The Padres, Orioles, and Twins all had interest in Servais last offseason but ended up making other hires.

The specifics of Servais’ position aren’t yet known, but his hire represents the latest change to Colorado’s front office since DePodesta was hired a little over a year ago. Beyond trying to get the Rockies on track via a proper rebuild, DePodesta has also been tasked with modernizing a baseball ops department that was seen as behind on the times.

articles.title: Tigers To Sign Luis Gil
body: The Tigers are adding free agent righty Luis Gil on a one-year deal, reports Jeff Passan of ESPN. The pact is worth $2.3MM, with another $2MM available in incentives.

Gil was non-tendered by the Yankees on Friday. We had him projected to earn $2.3MM in arbitration. He’ll land that exact figure from Detroit. The performance bonuses haven’t been reported, but they will likely be tied to availability. Injuries have limited Gil to 20 appearances over the past two seasons.

The Tigers have made headlines this offseason for multiple pitching moves. The club got free agency rolling by adding closer Emilio Pagan in early November. Detroit also locked down young right-hander Troy Melton on a six-year extension. Bringing in Gil isn’t at the level of those moves, but it’s still an intriguing one. The 2024 AL Rookie of the Year is currently healthy and could contribute in multiple areas.

Injuries have been the story for Gil. He missed most of the 2025 campaign with a lat strain. It was shoulder inflammation that shelved him this past season. Before his breakout performance in 2024, he missed all of 2023 while recovering from elbow surgery. Gil has made just 56 appearances since debuting with the Yankees in 2021.

articles.title: Red Sox Interested In Luis Gil
body: Right-hander Luis Gil was non-tendered by the Yankees on Friday, making him a free agent. One of his suitors on the open market is a former AL East rival. The Red Sox are interested in Gil, reports Tim Healey of the Boston Globe.
MLBTR had Gil projected to earn $2.3MM in arbitration. After back-to-back seasons marred by injuries, the Yankees decided to cut him loose. Gil will be in search of a fresh start this winter.

The 29-year-old Gil seemed like a sturdy member of New York’s rotation two years ago. He put together 29 starts of a 3.50 ERA and a 26.8% strikeout rate in 2024. Gil earned AL Rookie of the Year honors for the performance.

Gil’s ascension as a mid-rotation starter came to a screeching halt in 2025. He suffered a lat strain in the spring that cost him the first four months of the season. Gil returned in the second half and made 11 starts to close the year. He had an underwhelming 16.8% strikeout rate and a hefty 13.5% walk rate.

The 2026 campaign went similarly for Gil. He missed a significant chunk of the season with shoulder inflammation. Gil was up and down with the big-league club, totaling 27 1/3 innings over nine appearances. He had more walks (18) than strikeouts (17).

articles.title: Jonathan Loaisiga Had Offers From Mets, Blue Jays
body: Right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga signed with the Yankees on Friday, bringing him back to New York after a season in Arizona. Loaisiga had other suitors, though, including another AL East squad and the other New York club.

Bob Nightengale of USA Today reports that Loaisiga had offers on the table from the Mets and Blue Jays. It’s unclear if those deals matched or exceeded the two-year, $18MM pact Loaisiga ultimately received from the Yankees.

Loaisiga had to take a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks last winter after multiple years of injuries and poor performance in the Bronx. It ended up being a huge win for Arizona, as Loaisiga emerged as one of the most important pieces in the bullpen. The veteran righty posted a 2.42 ERA with 10 holds and three saves as a member of the high-leverage group.

It’s no surprise Loaisiga attracted offers from multiple teams. Not only did he pitch well, but his fastball was up a tick in 2026. He seemed to be past the arm issues that plagued his final years with the Yankees. Loaisiga generated soft contact at an elite clip while keeping the ball on the ground at one of the highest rates in the league. It’s a repeatable approach, though the strikeouts are lower than a typical late-inning arm.

The Mets have multiple spots to fill in the bullpen after shipping out Luke Weaver and A.J. Minter at the trade deadline. Kodai Senga, who finished the year as the team’s closer, seems headed back toward a spot in the rotation. The Mets have some question marks behind Devin Williams, who is no sure bet himself.

articles.title: Cardinals, Alec Burleson Have Mutual Interest In Extension
body: First baseman Alec Burleson is coming off a two-year run of excellent hitting for the Cardinals. It’s not surprising that other teams have shown interest in trading for him, and even less of a surprise that St. Louis quickly turned away that trade interest. On the contrary, the Cardinals may want Burleson at first base for the long haul. Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports that the two parties have mutual interest in an extension. Burleson had previously expressed openness to a long-term deal.

Burleson was the Cardinals’ compensatory round draft pick in 2020, the No. 70 overall selection. He debuted in 2022 and played sparsely, then put up an 89 wRC+ in 347 plate appearances in 2023. He took a step forward the following year. Burleson hit 21 home runs and slashed.269/.314/.420 in 595 plate appearances, good for a 106 wRC+. He didn’t walk much but impressively struck out just 12.8% of the time.

The 2025 season was Burleson’s true breakout. He batted.290/.343/.459 with a 124 wRC+ in 139 games, missing only ten days late in the season for right wrist inflammation. Burleson upped his average exit velocity from 89.7 mph to 91.0 mph in 2025 and also gained 17 points in isolated power. This year, he had a nearly identical 125 wRC+, along with a career-best 8.2% walk rate and an 18.1% strikeout rate that’s still better than average. He also became a full-time first baseman after previously splitting time between the outfield, DH, and the cold corner.

articles.title: Padres, Mariners, Phillies Interested In Jarren Duran
body: The Red Sox are known to be actively shopping outfielder Jarren Duran since the recent GM Meetings. Duran appears to be drawing interest from a few clubs, with Chris Cotillo and Sean McAdam of MassLive naming the Padres, Mariners, and Phillies as clubs who have done due diligence on him. That brings the number of confirmed suitors for Duran to four, including the Cubs, whose interest was previously reported. Cotillo and McAdam also list the Diamondbacks, Angels, and Astros as speculative fits.

If there ever was a change-of-scenery candidate, it’s Duran. He hit well in a half season’s worth of plate appearances in 2023, then broke out fully with an excellent 2024. That year, Duran slashed.285/.342/.492 with 21 home runs, 34 steals, and a 132 wRC+. He usually strikes out more than average but did so at a career-low 21.8% clip in 2024, which is essentially league average. He also played exceptional defense. Duran split time between center field and left and earned a combined +23 Defensive Runs Saved and +10 Outs Above Average. He earned his first All-Star nod and finished eighth in AL MVP voting for his effort.

articles.title: Mets Extend A.J. Ewing
body: The Mets and outfielder A.J. Ewing have agreed to an eight-year contract extension, SNY’s Chelsea Janes reports. The deal also contains a club option for a ninth season (the 2035 campaign), and The Athletic’s Will Sammon reports that the option year is worth $25MM. Sammon also says the extension will pay Ewing $95MM in guaranteed money. Ewing is represented by ACES.

Ewing’s deal is the eighth-largest guarantee given to a player with less than a year of big league service time, as well as the eighth-largest in terms of average annual value. It’s a huge commitment to a 22-year-old who just made his MLB debut back in May, and it marks the first true long-term commitment extension for the Mets since David Stearns became president of baseball operations in October 2023. Catcher Luis Torrens inked a two-year, $11.5MM extension last May, but Ewing’s deal represents a new frontier for the franchise’s investment in young talent.

Locking up young players to early-career extensions was a common tactic for Stearns when he ran the Brewers’ front office, and gaining cost certainty over a promising player is a logical move for both larger-market and smaller-market teams alike. The Mets have now covered all of Ewing’s pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible years, and at least two of his free agent years.

articles.title: Giants Expected To Re-Sign Victor Bericoto
body: The Giants did not tender a contract to outfielder Victor Bericoto by Friday’s deadline, making him a free agent. The sides might not be splitting up for long, though. Alex Pavlovic of NBC Sports Bay Area reports that Bericoto will likely rejoin the organization on a minor league deal.

Bericoto has yet to reach arbitration, so his non-tender wasn’t a cost-cutting move. It was likely more about clearing a 40-man roster spot. Re-signing Bericoto to a minors agreement will allow the club to keep him in the organization as a depth option.

The 24-year-old Bericoto debuted with the Giants this past season. He slashed.241/.267/.420 with five homers and a stolen base in 41 games in the majors. Injuries led to a disjointed year, as Bericoto missed a month with an oblique strain and three weeks with a knee injury.

Bericoto spent most of his time in the corner outfield spots. He was a slight negative by Defensive Runs Saved. He also played nine innings at first base. San Francisco has Bryce Eldridge and Rafael Devers to handle first, so Bericoto’s future with the club is likely in the outfield.

The Giants signed Bericoto as an international free agent out of Venezuela in 2018. He’s hit at just about every minor league level, including a 125 wRC+ across three levels in 2025. Bericoto was perfectly league average at Triple-A this past year. He hit.288 with six homers and a 100 wRC+ in 54 games with Sacramento.

articles.title: Hiromi Itoh Reportedly Visited Chicago
body: Free agent right-hander Hiromi Itoh was in Chicago on Friday, reported Jesse Rogers and Jorge Castillo of ESPN. The report didn’t specify whether he visited the Cubs, White Sox, or both. The White Sox are known to be interested in Itoh. The Cubs haven’t been publicly connected to him, but they are in need of pitching.

The rumblings regarding Itoh haven’t been as prevalent as with his two NPB cohorts. Third baseman Teruaki Sato has been linked to more than a half dozen teams. Several clubs have been connected to right-hander Kaima Taira, including both the White Sox and Cubs. Outside of the White Sox and Giants, there haven’t been many clubs directly tied to Itoh. That doesn’t mean he isn’t generating the same level of buzz, though he is a bit older than Taira and doesn’t bring the same level of velocity.

The 29-year-old Itoh has been a reliable option for the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters since 2021. He’s put together a sub-3.00 ERA in four of his six NPB seasons. Itoh took home the Sawamura Award in 2025, which is Japan’s equivalent of the Cy Young Award. He ranked 36th on our Top 50 Free Agents list.

The White Sox have been one of the most active teams on the pitching front this offseason, both in terms of additions and subtractions. They landed Dustin May on a healthy three-year, $52.5MM deal. The club announced plans to move closer Grant Taylor into the rotation. The White Sox sent out Davis Martin and Luis Castillo in a trade with the Rockies.

articles.title: Blue Jays’ Nathan Lukes Receiving Trade Interest
body: Blue Jays outfielder Nathan Lukes has been getting some trade interest, the Toronto Star’s Gregor Chisholm reported earlier this week. Lukes has spent the last two seasons as a regular in the Jays’ outfield, and he is projected to earn $2.1MM in the first of four trips through the arbitration process as a Super Two player.

Despite this long-term control, Lukes turned 32 last July, and might not be in Toronto’s plans as anything more than a part-timer. Lukes opened some eyes with some strong numbers over 91 plate appearances in 2024, and over the last two seasons has hit.266/.325/.397 with 22 home runs over 888 PA (with most of that production coming against right-handed pitching). This translates to a 103 wRC+, and Lukes has been worth 4.0 fWAR in 2025-26 due to both his hitting and his glovework at all three outfield positions.

Addison Barger’s injury-marred season opened up a lot of playing time for Lukes in right field, and he ended up being a Gold Glove finalist after posting +11 Defensive Runs Saved and +2 Outs Above Average over 786 2/3 innings in the position. Lukes is better suited for corner outfield duty, and while he can handle center field in a pinch, rookie Brett Bateman emerged as another left-handed hitter who can provide a higher level of defense up the middle.

articles.title: AL East Notes: Gray, Red Sox, Fortes, Orioles, Rays
body: Sonny Gray signed a two-year, $55MM deal with the Twins earlier this week, with the 37-year-old landing a very nice payday on the heels of a strong 2026 campaign with the Red Sox. Despite Gray’s success in Boston, he told reporters (including MassLive.com’s Chris Cotillo) earlier this week that a new contract “never really came up” in what seemed to be limited discussions with Sox officials.

“I think the times we did have any type of conversations, it never really got close, it felt like, which is completely okay. As far as a reunion, it felt like it was never gaining any traction,” Gray said.

Gray reiterated how much he enjoyed his time in Boston, so there seem to be no hard feelings as the two sides part ways. While Gray’s production is theoretically difficult to replace, the Sox feel like they have a ready-made solution as Garrett Crochet returns from an injury-marred 2026 campaign. Gray, meanwhile, will now return to his old stomping grounds in Minnesota to help bolster a Twins staff that also includes Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley, and Pablo Lopez in his return from an internal brace procedure.
More notes from around the AL East…

articles.title: Manfred: Angels’ Sale Expected To Be Finalized In Early January
body: News broke on September 1 that Arte Moreno would be selling the Angels to Stan Kroenke, with the team’s announcement stating that the deal was “expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.” MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred added some specificity when speaking to the Associated Press and other reporters on Wednesday, saying that “we expect a closing just after the first of the year.”

This tentative four-month timeline fits with other recent franchise transfers, as the league needs time to fully explore and vet the many details that go into such a high-level sale. There is no doubt the other 29 owners will ultimately approve Kroenke’s purchase, and there was some thought that the league could try to expedite the process by the owners’ meetings that took place this past week. Instead, the Angels’ sale will follow a pretty standard path that should see Kroenke take charge in early January.

Given how the lockout will begin at the end of the day on December 1, the timing of the sale has gotten the Los Angeles offseason off to an unusual start. The club isn’t able to find a new full-time general manager/president of baseball operations until the sale is finalized, as interim GM John Mozeliak said at the start of November. Mozeliak remains in charge of the day-to-day business, including some preliminary interviews with potential GM candidates.

articles.title: Red Sox Had Interest In Corey Seager, CJ Abrams At Trade Deadline
body: The Red Sox were linked to such high-profile shortstops as Elly De La Cruz, Zach Neto, and Otto Lopez in the lead-up to last summer’s trade deadline, and MassLive.com’s Sean McAdam reports that the Sox were also interested in the Rangers’ Corey Seager and the Nationals’ CJ Abrams. This wasn’t the first time that Boston had looked into a Seager deal, as the Red Sox reportedly talked with the Rangers last offseason.

Despite this past interest, it doesn’t appear as though either player is necessarily on Boston’s radar this winter. One of the reasons is a lack of prospect capital, as McAdam notes that the Red Sox dug deep into their stockpile of young talent to swing other trades in advance of the deadline. Beyond the prospect package dealt to the Orioles to land Adley Rutschman, the Sox also moved former top prospect Marcelo Mayer to the Giants, and Connelly Early was dealt to Washington in a one-for-one swap for Curtis Mead.

Though Mead suffered a broken wrist in his first game in a Red Sox uniform, he is still lined up for a potential starting job at second base next season. With Mead penciled into the keystone, the Sox may feel they have a less pressing need in the middle infield than last summer. In terms of the shortstop position specifically, Trevor Story is entering the final year of his contract and is looking to rebound from another injury-marred season, and top prospect Franklin Arias is seemingly on the verge of his Major League debut.

articles.title: Giants Reportedly “Open To” Hearing Offers For Logan Webb
body: Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey flatly denied the possibility of a Logan Webb trade heading into last summer’s deadline, and even as recently as a week ago, Webb still seemed to be off the table in all trade discussions. However, the club’s stance now seems to have at least somewhat shifted, as FanSided’s Robert Murray writes that San Francisco is “open to listening to offers for Webb.”

There is no indication that any trade could be close, or that the Giants are doing anything but their due diligence in listening to what other teams might be willing to give up for the three-time All-Star. It costs Posey nothing to listen, and learning that a rival club is willing to part with a particular player or two could open a door to other trade discussions without Webb involved. Given how adding starting pitching is a priority for the Giants this winter, moving Webb would create a sizable hole at the top of the rotation, so it may be fair to say that a Webb trade is still pretty unlikely.

That said, this same need for pitching might relate to why Webb might be even somewhat of a trade candidate. Trading Webb would remove a hefty salary (he is owed $47MM over the next two seasons) from San Francisco’s books, and the Giants would almost certainly demand at least one controllable young starter back as part of any Webb trade package. Between acquiring such a young starter and using Webb’s salary to sign a more established arm, the Giants would essentially be turning Webb into two pitchers that could bolster the rotation in 2027 and beyond.

articles.title: White Sox Getting Trade Interest In Sean Sullivan
body: Sean Sullivan has only been a member of the White Sox for two days, yet the left-hander could conceivably find himself on the move again. The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon report that “multiple teams” stepped up with offers for Sullivan in the aftermath of the four-player trade that brought Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz to the Sox, with Luis Castillo and Davis Martin sent to the Rockies in return.

Moving Castillo’s $22.75MM salary was certainly Chicago’s chief goal in this trade, with Martin attached as a way of enticing the Rockies to pay full freight in absorbing Castillo’s contract. Acquiring a controllable arm like Martin and even a veteran like Castillo (who had a very solid career track record before his disastrous 2026 campaign) was a worthwhile investment for a Rockies team desperate to add pitching in any way possible, while for the White Sox, dealing Castillo perhaps clears payroll space for further moves this offseason.

Seen through this lens, Sullivan and a long-term type of prospect like Veliz could be viewed just as throw-ins for the trade, and the White Sox might well be open to flipping Sullivan in another deal. That said, Sullivan is also 24 years old, a former second-round draft pick (in 2023), and he just made his MLB debut this past season. While it’s fair to assume Sullivan is far from untouchable if the right offer came around, the White Sox might have interest in seeing what the left-hander can do away from the hitter-friendly environments of both Coors Field and the Rockies’ Triple-A affiliate in Albuquerque.

articles.title: Marlins Haven’t Yet Had Extension Talks With Sandy Alcantara
body: The Marlins have not yet approached Sandy Alcantara to discuss a contract extension, reports the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson. Alcantara, 31, is coming off a solid rebound campaign and saw his $21MM club option picked up at the end of last month. The team has no plans to trade him, and there’s mutual interest in getting an extension done, even if talks haven’t officially started yet.

It’s in both parties’ best interest to start negotiations sooner rather than later. The league is inevitably going to lock out the players after the CBA expires on December 1. That will put a freeze on all offseason activity until MLB and the Players Association can reach a new deal. If the lockout takes as long as it did five years ago, then Spring Training will be delayed and potentially abbreviated. Most players prefer not to continue extension talks during the regular season, so that leaves a week and a half until the lockout and the duration of Spring Training to complete a new Alcantara extension before the unofficial deadline.

Alcantara has a 3.69 earned run average in 1,289 1/3 career innings. All but 8 1/3 of those have been with the Marlins. From 2019-22, Alcantara established himself as an old-school workhorse, leading all qualified starters with 673 2/3 innings pitched. He ranked 13th-best in both ERA (3.07) and ground ball rate (50.4%) in that span as well. Alcantara peaked with a 10.2 fWAR stretch from 2021-22. In the latter season, he had a stellar 2.28 ERA and 207 strikeouts in 32 starts, unanimously winning the NL Cy Young award.

articles.title: Latest On Freddy Peralta
body: After finishing strong with the Rays this season, right-hander Freddy Peralta is one of the top available starting pitchers this side of Tarik Skubal. Unsurprisingly, Peralta is drawing interest from multiple teams, with Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic listing Peralta’s current suitors as the White Sox, Padres, Cubs, Blue Jays, and two unknown teams. The Padres and Blue Jays’ interest was previously reported. Rosenthal and Sammon also note that the Rays remain “seriously engaged” on Peralta.

MLBTR lists Peralta at No. 3 on our Top 50 Free Agents list and projects a five-year, $110MM deal. That’s a testament to the righty’s earlier track record with the Brewers and how he rebounded after the Mets traded him to the Rays at this year’s deadline. From 2021-25, Peralta pitched to a 3.30 earned run average for the Brewers with an above-average 29.6% strikeout rate. His 14.8 fWAR in that span tied for 18th among qualified starters.

With Peralta entering his walk year, the Brewers traded him and Tobias Myers to the Mets for a pair of prospects in January. Peralta wasn’t his usual self in 22 starts for New York. His strikeout rate fell to 22.1% after sitting in the 27-31% range from 2022-25. His ERA jumped to 4.99, albeit with a more palatable 3.86 expected ERA. Peralta’s velocity, walk rate, and ground ball numbers were in line with career norms, but the run prevention simply wasn’t there.

articles.title: Twins, Dodgers Swap Royce Lewis For Bobby Miller
body: The Twins and Dodgers lined up on a trade of formerly elite prospects, announcing on Friday that infielder Royce Lewis is headed to L.A. in exchange for right-hander Bobby Miller. Minnesota also adds young catcher Francisco Espinoza in the deal. Since both Lewis and Miller were on their respective clubs’ 40-man roster (and Espinoza is not), neither team’s 40-man roster count will change.

Lewis, 27, was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 draft and at one point ranked among the game’s very best prospects. He climbed through the Twins’ system as a shortstop but largely settled in at third base. At various points early on in his career, the righty-swinging slugger looked primed for stardom. Lewis was an absolute monster during the Twins’ playoff push in 2023, hitting.309/.372/.548 with 15 homers in 239 plate appearances that were scattered around multiple IL stints. He went 5-for-22 with four home runs, including a grand slam, during Minnesota’s ALDS run that year.

Unfortunately, that injury caveat has been far, far too prominent a concern in Lewis’ career. He’s amassed nearly five full years of major league service time but has only 1517 plate appearances. Lewis has twice torn the ACL in his right knee, and he’s been on the major league injured list a whopping 11 times due almost entirely to various leg injuries — most of them hamstring and quadriceps strains of varying degrees.

articles.title: Tigers, Troy Melton Agree To Six-Year Extension
body: The Tigers are locking right-hander Troy Melton into their rotation for the foreseeable future. The two parties have agreed to a six-year, $46.5MM contract extension. The deal includes a club option for 2033 and can max out at $80MM if the option is exercised and the pitcher hits all his performance bonuses. Melton would have reached free agency after the 2031 season, so the extension gives Detroit an extra two years’ worth of control over him. Melton is a client of Paragon Sports International.

The 25-year-old Melton earns a nice payday after a breakout season for Detroit. After starting the year on the 60-day IL for elbow inflammation, he made his season debut on May 24 and started 20 games the rest of the way. The righty held opponents to a 2.76 earned run average with a 20.0% strikeout rate and a 7.9% walk rate that checked in better than average. Melton also induced grounders at a 42.9% clip and generally kept the ball in the park.

Melton’s first 16 starts were particularly sharp. He carried a 1.86 ERA through the end of August and averaged just over six innings per start with a 7.3% walk rate. He fell off a bit once the calendar flipped to September. In four starts that month, Melton allowed 15 earned runs in 17 1/3 innings along with 22 hits and nine walks. In hindsight, some of that fall-off can be chalked up to forearm tightness, which caused Melton to end the year on the 15-day IL. He had no structural damage and is expected to have a normal offseason.

articles.title: Athletics Outright Hayden Juenger
body: The Athletics announced that reliever Hayden Juenger cleared waivers on Friday afternoon. He was outrighted to Triple-A Las Vegas and will remain in the organization without carrying a spot on the 40-man roster.

Juenger was a sixth-round selection by the Blue Jays in 2021. Toronto called him up in late May and got him into two games. They designated him for assignment a few weeks later and traded him to the A’s for minor league catcher Owen Carapellotti. Juenger was up and down from Triple-A three times the rest of the way. He allowed 13 runs across 14 innings for the A’s, surrendering 22 hits and six walks while striking out just six of 71 batters faced.

While it wasn’t a great debut showing at the MLB level, Juenger had a decent season in Triple-A. He pitched quite well for Toronto’s affiliate early in the year before scuffling in the much more hitter-friendly Pacific Coast League. Juenger finished the year with a combined 3.83 earned run average across 42 2/3 Triple-A frames. He struck out 20.8% of opponents against a 9% walk rate.

The A’s squeezed Juenger and Yunior Tur off the roster at Tuesday’s Rule 5 protection deadline. They acquired reliever Yaqui Rivera from Baltimore and added catcher Cole Conn to their 40-man roster. Tur landed with the Mets via waivers this afternoon. This is the first career outright assignment for Juenger, who’ll presumably receive a non-roster invite to big league camp and try to pitch his way back into Mark Kotsay’s bullpen.

articles.title: Mets Have Received Trade Interest In Mark Vientos
body: The Mets tendered Mark Vientos an arbitration contract this afternoon. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects him for a $2.4MM salary in his first year of eligibility. The decision came as a moderate surprise, as Vientos is out of minor league options and coming off a second consecutive poor season.

Although New York didn’t want to completely cut bait on Vientos, there’s no guarantee he remains on the roster into 2027. Will Sammon of The Athletic reports that the Mets have gotten trade calls on the first baseman, though no deal is believed to be imminent.

Tendering Vientos a contract merely ensures they can continue those conversations for the next couple weeks and again after the lockout. If Vientos and the Mets agree to a deal without an arbitration hearing, his salary would be fully guaranteed. If they can’t come to terms and go to a hearing, the Mets could release him for 30 or 45 days termination pay during Spring Training if they don’t feel he has a place on the roster.

Vientos looked like a potential offensive star a couple years ago. He slugged 27 home runs with a.266/.322/.516 slash line in only 111 regular season games in 2024. Vientos was one of the Mets’ best players in the postseason that year, batting.327 with a team-leading five longballs in 58 October plate appearances.

articles.title: Tigers Seeking Additional Relievers After Pagán Signing
body: The Tigers made the first move on the free agent market by signing righty reliever Emilio Pagán to a one-year, $11.5MM deal. If president of baseball operations Scott Harris has his way, there will be more bullpen additions incoming. When asked on Tuesday if he expected to add more relievers on big league deals, Harris told The Athletic’s Cody Stavenhagen and others, “We do. … As soon as I get off this call, I’m going to be hard at work at trying to find ways to get better…” He later added, “My job is to fill our ‘pen with talented arms and let A.J. decide how to deploy them,” in reference to the Pagán signing.

Earlier this month, Detroit picked up their $10MM option on swingman Drew Anderson and declined a $12MM option on Kenley Jansen in favor of a $2MM buyout. Anderson will compete for a rotation spot. The subtraction of Jansen left the Tigers in need of a closer, though Pagán is now in line for that role. The club was reportedly interested in Raisel Iglesias even after the Pagán deal. He wouldn’t be cheap, though. MLBTR expects Iglesias to earn $17MM on a one-year deal.

Detroit is currently projected for a $149.2MM cash payroll in 2027, as documented in MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker (courtesy of contributor Ethan Hullihen). That goes up to around $160MM with the addition of Pagán. The non-tenders of Jake Miller, Trey Sweeney, and Matt Vierling this afternoon will save about $5.3MM. Right-hander Troy Melton’s 2027 salary isn’t yet known; his six-year extension may give him a modest bump over the minimum salary for 2027, once that’s sorted out in the new CBA.

articles.title: Nationals Trade Braxton Roxby To Cubs
body: The Nationals and Cubs announced a trade that sends reliever Braxton Roxby from Washington to Chicago in exchange for cash considerations. The Nats had designated Roxby for assignment on Tuesday. Chicago’s roster count sits at 37.

Roxby has bounced around a little bit since the end of the season. The Nats claimed him off waivers from the Giants on October 29. (Washington had higher waiver priority than the Cubs because they had the worse record.) He only stuck on the Nats’ roster for a few weeks, getting squeezed out when they added three prospects to keep them out of the Rule 5 draft.

The 27-year-old Roxby made his first four big league appearances with San Francisco this year. He worked 5 1/3 innings of two-run ball, allowing six hits and a couple walks while recording three strikeouts. He threw his breaking pitches more than 60% of the time in that limited sample, also mixing in a four-seam fastball and a sinker in the 93-94 mph range. Roxby spent the majority of the season in Triple-A, pitching to a 3.78 earned run average with a 23% strikeout rate and 10% walk percentage across 64 1/3 innings.

Roxby has a full slate of minor league options remaining. The Cubs can shuttle him between Wrigley Field and Triple-A Iowa for the foreseeable future if they keep him on the 40-man roster. They had a handful of vacancies this early in the winter but are surely going to add multiple starting pitchers, which could force them to make some 40-man cuts after the lockout.

articles.title: Red Sox Trade Johan Oviedo To Diamondbacks
body: The Diamondbacks announced the acquisition of right-hander Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for relief prospect Luke Dotson and a player to be named later or cash considerations. Arizona’s 40-man roster tally sits at 38.

Oviedo adds some depth to an Arizona rotation that lost Michael Soroka and Zac Gallen to free agency. The 6’6″ righty is coming off a lost season, as he only made one big league appearance. He allowed four runs across 3 2/3 innings and departed early with a flexor strain. It wound up ending his season aside from one Triple-A rehab start in the middle of September.

It’s obviously not the way the Red Sox envisioned his tenure when they acquired Oviedo from Pittsburgh for outfielder Jhostynxon Garcia last offseason. Oviedo has flashed back-end ability but hasn’t put together a healthy season since 2023. He underwent Tommy John surgery and missed the’24 campaign, then suffered a lat strain in Spring Training 2025. That limited him to nine starts late in the year, in which he pitched to a 3.57 ERA with an above-average strikeout rate (24.7%) and far too many walks.

The D-Backs will hope for Oviedo’s stuff to rebound with a healthy offseason. He sat at 95.5 mph after the lat injury in 2025. That was down to 93 mph in his lone appearance in Boston. He also features a curveball and slider but hasn’t developed a trustworthy changeup to this point. That’s contributed to an underwhelming strikeout and walk profile versus left-handed batters.

articles.title: Rays Acquire Christian Koss
body: The Giants announced that they have traded infielder Christian Koss to the Rays in exchange for right-hander Cole Stokes. Koss was designated for assignment by San Francisco earlier this week. The Rays had 40-man space and don’t need to make a corresponding move.

Koss, 28, came to San Francisco in a minor trade in 2024. He made the Giants out of camp the following year and batted.264/.309/.368 in 191 plate appearances. Koss rarely walked and struck out a bit more than average, and the resulting 92 wRC+ implied he was 8% worse less productive than the average hitter. Defensively, he spent most of his time at second base, earning +8 Defensive Runs Saved in 339 innings there. He also played a handful of innings at third base and shortstop and missed one month with a left hamstring strain.

The 2026 season was a struggle for Koss on multiple fronts. He only put up a 58 wRC+ in 221 plate appearances as his batting line fell to.217/.257/.305. Both his strikeout and walk rates trended in the wrong direction, and Koss simply did not hit the ball with much authority, as evidenced by his meager 84.1 mph average exit velocity.

Koss played more shortstop and third base this year and was passable at both spots, but the total lack of hitting kept him a replacement-level player. It also didn’t help that he missed the month of June with a fractured left wrist and still didn’t hit well upon returning in July. The Giants ultimately cut him loose on Tuesday as part of a series of moves to protect Rule 5 eligible pitching prospects.

articles.title: White Sox Trade Jordan Leasure To Phillies
body: The White Sox have traded reliever Jordan Leasure to the Phillies for minor league pitcher Christian Coppola, according to announcements from both clubs. Philadelphia immediately agreed to a deal with Leasure to avoid arbitration.

Leasure was designated for assignment earlier in the week when Chicago signed Dustin May. He’s a couple months removed from undergoing UCL surgery that’ll likely cost him all of 2027. The Phils need to carry him on their offseason 40-man roster but can place him on the 60-day injured list at the beginning of Spring Training.

The 28-year-old Leasure had a productive 2025 season. He tossed 64 1/3 innings of 3.92 ERA ball and led White Sox relievers with 80 strikeouts. He worked his way into leverage spots and picked up seven saves. Leasure wasn’t nearly as effective this year, allowing 14 runs across 18 2/3 innings and spending a couple weeks on optional assignment to Triple-A. He’s likely making around the league minimum salary — MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz had projected him at $1MM — and has three additional years of arbitration control.

Philadelphia takes a reclamation flier, parting with their 12th round pick from this year’s draft. Coppola, who stands 6’5″, is a local product whom the Phils nabbed out of St. Joseph’s University. He hasn’t pitched professionally but recorded 69 strikeouts across 37 1/3 innings against small-school competition as a senior. Baseball America rated him the #326 player in this year’s draft, praising the movement he generates on his sweeping slider.

articles.title: Mets Claim Gus Varland
body: The Mets have claimed right-handed reliever Gus Varland off waivers from the NL East rival Nationals, Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic reports. The Nats designated Varland for assignment on Tuesday.

Unlike his brother, Blue Jays All-Star closer Louis Varland, Gus Varland has struggled to keep runs off the board in the majors. Since debuting in 2023, he has put up a 5.54 ERA over a combined 79 2/3 innings with the Brewers, Dodgers, White Sox and Nationals. Both right- and left-handed hitters have given Varland difficulty. While relying on a fastball-slider mix, he has yielded an.845 OPS against righties and a.939 mark versus lefties.

Over a career-high 33 frames with Washington in 2026, Varland posted a 6.55 ERA with discouraging underlying numbers. While metrics such as FIP (5.28), xFIP (4.90) and SIERA (4.37) suggest he deserved a better fate, he still checked in below average in those categories. Despite averaging a little north of 95 mph on his fastball, Varland struck out just 20.6% of hitters this past season. While the 30-year-old’s 9.7% walk rate hovered around average, his 28.6 ground-ball percentage ranked 309th among 328 relievers who tossed at least 20 innings.

Varland is out of minor league options, which will make it more difficult for him to stick with the Mets. For now, though, he’s part of the mix in a bullpen that figures to undergo notable changes this offseason. The Mets agreed to a three-year, $12MM deal with lefty Darwinzon Hernández on Thursday, and he probably won’t be the last free agent they add to a relief corps headlined by closer Devin Williams.

articles.title: 2026 Non-Tenders: National League
body: There is one day a year where a team can send a player directly to free agency without exposing the player to waivers. For players who do not have a guaranteed contract for next season, their club had to decide by 4pm Central today whether or not to tender the player a contract for 2027. This applies to players who have qualified for arbitration and those who do not yet have enough service time for arbitration. It does not apply to players who have already signed, whether that’s via a free agent deal, extension or some other contract.

Teams and players do not need to agree on a salary today, though some will. For those who do not have figures locked in by the end of today, the next steps will likely be interrupted this offseason. Normally, there’s a deadline in January where teams and players without agreements have to file salary figures for arbitration purposes. The hearings then take place in February. If there’s a lockout ongoing at those times this offseason, the process will be interrupted. With the 2021-22 lockout, the filing deadline was after the lockout was lifted in March and then hearings took place during the season.

For the players listed here, that’s all moot. Each has been cut from his roster spot and is now a free agent, eligible to sign with any club. For the American League non-tenders, please see this post. Projected salary figures are from MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz.

articles.title: Players Avoiding Arbitration Prior To The 2026 Non-Tender Deadline
body: The deadline for teams to tender contracts to arbitration-eligible players is this afternoon at 4pm CT. Throughout the day, we’ll see a handful of arb-eligible players agree to terms with their clubs to avoid a hearing.

These so-called “pre-tender deals” usually, although not always, involve players who were borderline non-tender candidates. Rather than run the risk of being cut loose, they can look to sign in the lead-up to the deadline. Those salaries often come in a little below projections, since these players tend to have less leverage because of the uncertainty about whether they’ll be offered a contract at all.

Under the 2022-26 collective bargaining agreement, players who sign to avoid an arbitration hearing are guaranteed full termination pay. That’s a change from prior CBAs, when teams could release an arb-eligible player before the season began and would only owe a prorated portion of the contract. This was done to incentivize teams and players to get deals done without going to a hearing.

All salary projections in this post come via MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz. This post will be updated throughout the day as deals are announced and/or reported. Deals are listed alphabetically by team name.

articles.title: 2026 Non-Tenders: American League
body: The deadline to tender a contract to arbitration-eligible players was 4pm CT this afternoon. Below is a comprehensive list of players on American League teams who have been non-tendered today. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected 2027 salaries for all arbitration-eligible players last month. Non-tendered players immediately enter free agency without needing to pass through waivers and can then be signed by any of the league’s 30 teams.

articles.title: Yankees Non-Tender Fernando Cruz, Luis Gil
body: The Yankees announced they’ve non-tendered reliever Fernando Cruz and former Rookie of the Year Luis Gil. Both pitchers had been projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz for $2.3MM salaries. Those are New York’s only non-tenders this year.

Cruz was Aaron Boone’s top right-handed setup man for the majority of the season. He fired 54 2/3 innings of 3.13 ERA ball, striking out 28.6% of batters faced. Cruz collected 19 holds in front of closer David Bednar and was slated to enter the postseason as a key leverage piece. That changed in August, as the 36-year-old sustained a partial tear of the UCL in his throwing elbow. It ended his season and raises the possibility of surgery.

The health outlook is clouded enough that the Yankees elected to move on despite Cruz’s fairly modest projected salary. They evidently didn’t want to risk a couple million dollars with the possibility that he’ll require an operation that costs him all of next season. Cruz has between four and five years of service time and will be eligible for arbitration again after 2027, barring a change to the service structure in the collective bargaining agreement.

articles.title: Mariners Non-Tender Luke Raley
body: The Mariners have non-tendered outfielder/first baseman Luke Raley, according to Robert Murray of FanSided. Raley is now a free agent.

The 32-year-old Raley entered the offseason on track to make his second of three potential trips through arbitration. MLBTR’s Matt Swartz projected a $3.1MM salary for Raley, but the Mariners are cutting him loose after he endured his second straight injury-shortened campaign. Raley underwent season-ending flexor surgery in August, though he expects to be ready whenever Spring Training gets underway in 2027.

Raley, who debuted with the Dodgers in 2021, established himself as a viable major league hitter in 2023 with the Rays. While logging the extreme majority of his 406 plate appearances against right-handed pitchers that year, the lefty slashed.249/.333/.490 with 19 home runs and 14 stolen bases. Raley’s output was 29% better than league average, per wRC+, but it wasn’t enough to stick in Tampa Bay. The Rays traded him to the Mariners for infielder José Caballero in January 2024.

articles.title: Rockies Acquire Chase Lee, Designate Jimmy Herget For Assignment
body: The Rockies have traded for Blue Jays right-hander Chase Lee, per a team announcement. Cash is heading back to Toronto in the deal. Colorado is designating right-hander Jimmy Herget for assignment to clear a roster spot.

Lee was squeezed off the roster yesterday when the Blue Jays claimed infielder Christian Cairo off waivers from the Dodgers. The Rockies swooped in with a trade before he was put on waivers. It’s the second straight day with a pitching acquisition for Colorado. The club swung a trade with the White Sox for righties Davis Martin and Luis Castillo last night.

It’s now back-to-back offseasons on the move for Lee. The Tigers traded him to the Blue Jays for lefty Johan Simon last winter. Lee had multiple stints in Toronto this season, all of them brief. He posted a 6.52 ERA across eight appearances. Lee walked eight and struck out five in his 9 2/3 frames with the Blue Jays.

While the MLB results were discouraging, Lee had a strong campaign at Triple-A Buffalo. He delivered 43 appearances of a 2.01 ERA. The 28-year-old got ground balls at a solid 47.9% clip and kept his walk rate under 10%. Lee picked up five saves out of the Bisons’ bullpen.

It seems fitting that Lee, a fellow sidearmer, replaces Herget in Colorado. The low-slot veteran has been a regular in the Rockies’ bullpen for the past two seasons. Herget was excellent in 2025, posting a mid-2.00s ERA as a multi-inning option. He couldn’t replicate that output this season. Herget scuffled to a 5.70 ERA in 51 appearances. His walk rate, which is typically a strength, ballooned to 11.0%.

articles.title: Padres Sign Cal Stevenson To Minor League Deal
body: The Padres have signed outfielder Cal Stevenson to a minor league deal, according to his transactions log at MiLB.com. Stevenson, who last appeared in the Majors in 2025 with the Phillies, will ride out the offseason with Triple-A El Paso.

Stevenson, 30, was a tenth-round draft pick by the Blue Jays back in 2018. He spent time in four clubs’ minor league systems before eventually debuting with the Athletics in 2022. Over 118 plate appearances from 2022-25, Stevenson has a line of.178/.276/.238 with a 26.3% strikeout rate, 11.9% walk rate, and a 52 wRC+. Defensively, he’s been worth -2 Defensive Runs Saved and +2 by Outs Above Average and Fielding Run Value.

Stevenson did not appear in the Majors this year, instead spending it with the Tigers’ top affiliate in Toledo. In 330 plate appearances for the Mud Hens, the journeyman slashed.264/.410/.456 with a 137 wRC+ and a well-above-average walk rate of 19.4%. A.353 average on balls in play certainly helped Stevenson out. He outperformed his expected batting average by 49 points and his expected slugging percentage by more than 100.

Plate discipline and speed are a couple factors working in Stevenson’s favor. The lowest walk rate he’s posted in the upper minors was 13.5% for the Athletics’ top affiliate in 2022. Dating back to 2023, he’s stolen 77 bases at Triple-A. The walks and steals make Stevenson an okay depth piece, though obviously he’s yet to translate that into major league production.

articles.title: Padres, Gavin Sheets Agree To Three-Year Deal
body: The Padres and first baseman Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11MM contract, reports Robert Murray of FanSided. ESPN’s Jeff Passan adds that Sheets will get a $500K signing bonus and $2.5MM salary for the upcoming season. The 2028 and 2029 seasons are player options valued at $4MM apiece.

Sheets, a client of Covenant Sports Group, was projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz to receive a $6.5MM salary in his final trip through arbitration. This new arrangement guarantees him some extra money while also providing multiple chances to test free agency if he performs at a high level.

The extension is a three-year deal in name only. If Sheets performs well this coming season, he’ll almost certainly opt out and test free agency in search of a larger deal. Presumably, there’s a buyout on the player options that’d further boost Sheets’ earnings if he takes one of his opt-out opportunities. The deal spares the Padres on Sheets’ luxury tax hit by presenting a somewhat artificially low annual value while affording both player and team some protection in the event that Sheets suffers an injury or simply performs poorly this coming season.

articles.title: Red Sox To Sign Duke Ellis To Minor League Deal
body: Outfielder Duke Ellis has agreed to a minor league contract with the Red Sox, as first reported by Francys Romero. Ari Alexander of 7News Boston adds the terms of the deal. It’s a split contract for Ellis, who is represented by The Movement Baseball. For the time he spends in the majors, he will either make $1MM or a salary $70K higher than the 2027 MLB minimum, whichever is greater.

Ellis, 29 in January, signed with the White Sox as an undrafted free agent in 2020. Four years later, he got the call to Chicago for his MLB debut. Shortly thereafter, he was designated for assignment and bounced from the White Sox to the Mets to the Mariners to the Yankees in quick succession. It was with the Yankees that he got another crack at big league playing time in September. He also made the roster for the ALDS. Altogether, he appeared in 11 regular games (and one playoff game) with the White Sox and Yankees in 2024, often as a pinch-runner or defensive replacement. Although he only managed one hit in five trips to the plate, he stole five bases and played all three outfield positions.

articles.title: Athletics Sign Brian Serven, Wilkin Ramos To Minor League Deals
body: The A’s have reunited with catcher Brian Serven on a minor league deal, according to his transactions page at MiLB.com. He returns to their Triple-A affiliate in Las Vegas after electing free agency in lieu of an outright assignment a few weeks ago. The A’s also signed right-hander Wilkin Ramos to a minor league deal a few days ago and assigned him to Las Vegas, per his transactions tracker.

Serven, 31, signed his first minor league deal with the A’s in December 2025 after electing free agency out of the Tigers organization the month before. The A’s selected him onto the big league roster on July 4, then optioned and recalled him twice in the next few weeks. Serven tallied just 85 plate appearances on the season. In that small sample, he batted.175/.224/.375 with a meager 55 wRC+, although he chipped in five home runs.

Serven had better results with Las Vegas. He took 262 plate appearances there and slashed.308/.401/.538 with a 125 wRC+, including an 11.8% walk rate that’s more than double the 5.7% mark of Serven’s big league career.
