In the last few years, Serven has alternated between good and below-average output at the top level of the Rockies, Blue Jays, Tigers, and Athletics’ systems. He has just a 45 wRC+ in 384 big league plate appearances dating back to 2022.

The defensive metrics on Serven are mildly intriguing. He has been worth +8 Defensive Runs Saved behind the plate in his career. He drew decent marks for his framing early on, and this year, Statcast considered him an above-average blocker.

articles.title: Cardinals To Non-Tender Nolan Gorman
body: The Cardinals will not tender infielder Nolan Gorman a contract before the 4 p.m. CT deadline on Friday, Joel Sherman of the New York Post reports. Gorman will hit free agency once the move becomes official.

Although the Cardinals could have controlled Gorman via arbitration through 2028, they will move on early after his production nosedived over the past three years. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected a $3.4MM salary in 2027 for Gorman, but the Cardinals deemed it too rich for a player they demoted to the minors for a large chunk of last season. With Gorman’s stock down, the Cardinals came up short in their attempts to find a trade partner for the 26-year-old.

Gorman’s tenure with the Cardinals will come to an end eight years after they chose him 19th overall in the 2018 draft. Thanks in part to his prodigious power, Gorman was considered a top-end prospect when he debuted in St. Louis in May 2022. There were questions about Gorman’s high strikeout totals then, though, and the lefty hitter has done nothing to allay those concerns since. In 1,883 plate appearances with the Cardinals, Gorman logged a 33.8% strikeout rate. Only six qualified hitters have fared worse in that category since 2022. While Gorman has drawn walks at a respectable 10.4% clip in the bigs, it hasn’t been enough to overcome his swing-and-miss issues. He’ll leave St. Louis with a below-average.212/.295/.402 line (94 wRC+) and 83 home runs.

articles.title: Orioles Re-Sign Luis Vázquez On Minor League Deal
body: The Orioles re-signed infielder Luis Vázquez to a minor league contract and invited him to major league spring training, reports Jorge Castillo of ESPN.

Vázquez, 27, has played in each of the past three major league seasons, the past two in Baltimore. He only played one game this past season, granted, but Vázquez appeared in 36 games for the 2025 O’s and has totaled 48 big league appearance between brief stints in Baltimore and with the Cubs. He’s primarily been used as a defensive replacement, however, evidenced by a tiny tally of just 67 major league plate appearances. Vázquez has slashed just.145/.194/.210 in that time.

Though he obviously hasn’t played much in the majors, Vázquez has played in parts of six Triple-A seasons. He’s stepped to the plate 1041 times at the top minor league level and recorded a.247/.327/.400 batting line while logging significant innings at shortstop, second base and third base (in addition to extremely brief cameos at first base and in the outfield corners). The righty-swinging Vázquez has above-average speed and is considered a solid defender across multiple infield positions.

There’s no immediate path to the majors for Vázquez in Baltimore, but the Orioles are clearly fond of having him on hand as a depth option. The O’s traded for Vázquez after the Cubs designated him for assignment in Jan. 2025, and though they’ve passed him through waivers a couple times, they’ve continued to hang onto him and use him as a depth piece. He’ll be back in a similar depth role next season.

articles.title: Rangers To Sign Dylan File To Minors Deal
body: The Rangers are expected to add right-hander Dylan File on a minor league deal, per Robert Murray of FanSided. The agreement includes an invitation to MLB Spring Training. File spent last season with the Tigers’ Triple-A affiliate.

The 30-year-old File has posted back-to-back strong workloads in the minors. He’s topped 130 innings in each of the past two seasons. The results have been less than ideal. File recorded a 5.28 ERA in 28 appearances with Toledo in 2026. He returned to minor league free agency at the end of the season.

Milwaukee took File with a late-round pick in the 2017 draft. He was a prospect of note for a time in the organization and even spent time on the 40-man roster. File ultimately fell short of reaching the big leagues in Milwaukee. He was released at the end of the 2022 campaign and has bounced around since then. File spent time in the minors with Arizona and Seattle before signing with Detroit. He also pitched briefly in the KBO with the Doosan Bears.

File showed a diverse arsenal this past season with the Mud Hens. He used six different pitches at least 9.9% of the time. File led with a low-90s four-seamer and sinker. He threw two breaking balls, a slider and a curveball. File also used a cutter and changeup. The repertoire didn’t generate many strikeouts, but File also kept the walks down. Homers were an issue. File permitted 1.51 home runs per nine innings.

articles.title: Mets Claim Yunior Tur
body: The Mets have claimed right-hander Yunior Tur off waivers from the Athletics, reports Francys Romero of BeisbolFR. The A’s designated Tur for assignment earlier this week. The Mets technically opened today with 39 guys on the 40-man roster but they agreed to a deal with lefty Darwinzon Hernández yesterday. If Tur takes the final 40-man spot, they will have to make a corresponding move to make the Hernández deal official.

Tur, 27, was originally an international signing out of Cuba. He got to make his major league debut this year and it did not go well. Tur logged 12 2/3 innings for the A’s and allowed 23 earned runs, giving him an ERA of 16.34.

Despite those numbers, there are reasons for the Mets to be intrigued. The arsenal is certainly appealing, as Tur has averaged about 95-96 miles per hour in his Triple-A and big league career. He has also thrown a cutter, splitter and slider.

Tur can miss bats but also misses the strike zone. In 2025, working primarily as a starter, he tossed 125 2/3 innings across three different levels with a 3.29 ERA. He struck out 24.5% of batters faced but also gave out walks at a high clip of 11.3%. The A’s had him mostly working in relief in 2026. He threw 61 1/3 innings at the Triple-A level. His strikeout rate ticked up to 27.6% but he also gave out walks at a 14.7% pace. He ended up with a 5.87 ERA at that level.

articles.title: Nationals Sign Omar Cruz To Minor League Deal
body: The Nationals announced this week that they have signed left-hander Omar Cruz to a minor league deal. He also receives an invite to major league camp in spring training.

Cruz, 28 in January, has a very limited track record in the big leagues. He made two appearances for the Padres in 2025, allowing two earned runs in 3 2/3 innings. He was non-tendered after that season and then re-signed with the Friars via a minor league deal. He didn’t get called up in 2026 and became a minor league free agent at season’s end.

The Nats naturally looked beyond that tiny sample of work to focus on Cruz’s work in the minors, which has broadly featured good amount of strikeouts but also a hefty number of walks. Over the past three years, Cruz has thrown 202 1/3 innings on the farm with a 4.49 earned run average. He punched out 28.9% of batters faced in that time but also gave out walks at a 12% clip. His four-seamer averaged around 92 miles per hour this year while he also threw a curveball and changeup.

The bullpen in Washington was clearly a weakness in 2026. The club’s relievers had a collective 4.99 ERA this year. Only the Royals and Athletics were worse. The Nats will surely make some moves between now and Opening Day but currently project to have Erik Tolman, Will Dion, Reiver Sanmartin and Philip Abner in the lefty relief mix. If Cruz can earn a roster spot, he still has options remaining.

articles.title: Twins To Non-Tender Trevor Larnach
body: The Twins are not expected to tender a contract to outfielder Trevor Larnach before the 4 p.m. CT deadline on Friday, Dan Hayes of The Athletic reports. Larnach will reach free agency once the move becomes official.

This is the second significant non-tender news of the day for Minnesota, which will also move on from right-hander Bailey Ober. Both Larnach and Ober have been Twins staples for several years, but the team will part ways with the pair in lieu of giving them raises in arbitration. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected a $6.3MM salary for Larnach in 2027, which would have been his third and final year of arbitration with the club. The Twins will go in another direction just days after Larnach underwent arthroscopic wrist surgery, though he is expected to be ready whenever Spring Training starts.

Larnach, who will turn 30 in February, has been a member of the Twins since they took him 20th overall in the 2018 draft. He topped out as Baseball America’s 39th-best prospect in 2021, the year he made his major league debut. Larnach yo-yoed between the majors and minors until 2024, when he played his first of three straight seasons of at least 112 games. Dating back to then, the lefty-swinging Larnach has taken a team-high 1,400 trips to the plate and slashed a solid.259/.336/.422 with a 20.9% strikeout rate, a 9.9% walk rate and 45 home runs. However, Larnach has struggled against same-handed pitchers, who have limited him to a miserable.209/.273/.310 line during his career. Just six of his 65 lifetime homers have come off southpaws.

articles.title: Cubs Claim Joey Bart
body: Joey Bart is headed north. The Cubs have claimed the catcher off waivers from their crosstown rivals, according to Robert Murray of FanSided. The White Sox designated him for assignment earlier this week.

Once heralded as Buster Posey’s heir apparent, Bart never quite figured things out during his four seasons with San Francisco. From 2020-23, he played exactly 162 games, hitting.219 with a.623 OPS and a 77 wRC+. Yet, almost instantly after the Giants traded him to the Pirates in 2024, the change of scenery paid off. Bart played 80 games that year, hitting.265 with a.799 OPS and a 120 wRC+. Among catchers with at least 200 plate appearances, his wOBA and xwOBA both ranked in the top 10. His defense was still subpar, but not so much as to make him a liability, especially when he was hitting so well.

That breakout performance earned Bart a $1.75MM salary from the Pirates in his first year of arbitration eligibility. He followed it up with another solid year in 2025. The backstop upped his walk rate and posted the highest on-base percentage of his career. He also set a new career high in plate appearances. However, that additional playing time meant he was exposed to right-handed pitching more often. While he still punished left-handers, he struggled when he didn’t have the platoon advantage. As a result, his overall offensive numbers were mediocre, though still above-average for a catcher: a.696 OPS and a 100 wRC+.

articles.title: Giants Sign Erick Mejia To Minor League Deal
body: Earlier this week, the Giants signed right-hander Erick Mejia to a minor league contract (h/t Francys Romero). The 32-year-old is trying to make a comeback as a pitcher after last appearing in the majors as a position player in 2020.

Mejia signed with the Mariners as an international free agent in 2012. Initially a shortstop, he would soon start to bounce around the diamond, just as he bounced between teams. From 2012-24, he played every position except catcher in the Mariners, Dodgers, Royals, and Nationals organizations. As a utility player, Mejia briefly made the majors with Kansas City in 2019 and’20, appearing in 17 total games. He hit.167 with a.466 OPS.

In 2024, Mejia threw an inning of relief in a blowout game at Triple-A. He turned enough heads with his performance that he and the Nationals decided to move him to the mound full-time the following year. At 30 years old, he returned to Single-A to start things over. By the end of the season, he was back at Triple-A. All told, he threw 49 innings across three minor league levels. His 58 strikeouts were impressive, though he struggled with his command. Nonetheless, despite his 4.59 ERA and 15.9% walk rate, it wasn’t hard to see promise in his five-pitch arsenal, which included a mid-90s four-seam fastball.

articles.title: Cashman: Teams Calling About Jasson Dominguez
body: Yankees general manager Brian Cashman told reporters on Thursday that rival clubs are reaching out about outfielder Jasson Dominguez. Injuries and defensive challenges limited Dominguez to 57 games with New York last season, but he’s apparently drawing interest on the trade market.

“Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball,” Cashman said, relayed by Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. “I think he’s got like an 1.100 OPS right now, and he’s looking really good. And I think the entire industry is noticing that based on, you know, the phone calls I’m getting.”

Cashman came in slightly high on Dominguez’s OPS with Aguilas, but not by much. He’s posted a 1.069 mark over 12 games of Dominican Winter League action. He has seven extra-base hits and 13 RBI. A dozen games of winter ball is probably not enough to spur trade interest alone, but teams certainly have other reasons to be interested in Dominguez given his pedigree.

“The Martian” was one of the most hyped prospects of the past decade. It’s yet to result in consistent production in the majors. Dominguez has now played in parts of four MLB seasons, though that’s only amounted to 751 plate appearances. His longest stretch as a big-league regular came in 2025. Dominguez hit 10 homers and stole 23 bases as a slightly above-league-average bat across 123 games.

articles.title: Twins To Non-Tender Bailey Ober
body: The Twins are expected to non-tender right-hander Bailey Ober today, reports Darren Wolfson of 5 Eyewitness News and SKOR North Radio. He’ll immediately become a free agent when the move becomes official.

Ober, 31, has been a mainstay in Minnesota’s rotation over the past four years and has seen big league action in each of the past six. He’s been a largely steady performer, totaling 748 2/3 innings of 4.15 ERA ball with a 22.7% strikeout rate and 5.5% walk rate in his career overall. The past two seasons, however, have seen Ober’s results back up against a notable velocity dip.

The towering 6’9″ Ober was tagged for a 5.10 ERA in 27 starts during the 2025 campaign, though most of his struggles were confined to the month of June, and he pitched well upon returning from an IL stint that followed said rough patch. He logged a 4.47 ERA in 2026 but fanned a career-low 17.1% of his opponents while averaging just 88 mph on his four-seamer — a drop of 2.2 mph from 2025 and a huge 4.3 mph slower than his rookie season back in 2022. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz had projected Ober for a $6.9MM salary in 2027.

articles.title: Dodgers To Sign Tink Hence To Minor League Deal
body: The Dodgers are bringing in right-hander Tink Hence on a minor league agreement, per Chase Ford of MiLB Central. The former Cardinals prospect hit minor-league free agency at the end of the season.

Hence’s stock has fallen precipitously over the past few years. He zoomed through the Cardinals system after getting drafted with the No. 63 pick in the 2020 draft. He was among the top prospects in the organization in the early 2020s, and even popped up on some top 100 lists. Injuries have derailed Hence over the past two seasons. He’s missed time with shoulder, chest, and rib issues. Hence has totaled 41 2/3 innings since the beginning of 2025.

St. Louis made the decision to bump Hence off the 40-man roster in August. No team stepped in to claim him, so the righty remained in the organization. He finished out the year with the club’s Florida Complex League affiliate.

Hence was moved to the bullpen in 2026. He scuffled to a 6.64 ERA over 19 appearances at Triple-A Memphis. He had nearly as many walks (18) as strikeouts (20) across 20 1/3 innings. The biggest red flag was the velocity. Hence sat at 91.6 mph with his four-seamer this year. He was regularly in the mid-90s with the heater earlier in his career.

Hence is still just 24. He’ll head to a forward-thinking organization that might have some ideas on how to recover his lost velocity. The Dodgers could also consider stretching Hence back out as a starter or swingman option.

articles.title: Rockies Interested In David Peterson
body: The Rockies added a pair of new rotation members in last night’s trade to acquire Luis Castillo and Davis Martin from the White Sox. They’re still looking to add more arms, and lefty David Peterson is among the free agents in whom they’re interested, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. ESPN’s Jeff Passan wrote this week that the Rockies have been “aggressive” in their search for free agent starters, dangling multi-year deals at prices reflective of their unfavorable home park. Peterson might be a bit more amenable to the challenge of pitching at elevation, given that it’d be something of a homecoming; although he war born in California, he spent his teen years in Colorado and attended high school just 20 miles southeast of Coors Field.

Peterson, who turned 31 in September, is a former first-round pick who’s spent the bulk of his career with the Mets. Struggles early in his platform season for free agency both contributed to the Mets’ early collapse and prompted New York to trade him to the Cubs in June. Peterson had one awful start early in his Cubs tenure but otherwise rebounded, which perhaps shouldn’t be particularly surprising for a prominent ground-ball pitcher who moved from one of the worst defenses in baseball to the very best infield defense in the sport with that change-of-scenery swap.

articles.title: Yankees To Sign Jonathan Loaisiga
body: Reliever Jonathan Loaisiga is heading to the Yankees on a two-year deal. It’s an $18MM agreement that includes a club option for 2029. New York makes yet another addition to its bullpen by bringing Loaisiga back to the Bronx. Loaisiga is a client of the Ballengee Group.

The 32-year-old Loaisiga spent one season away from the Yankees. He made it count, tossing 67 innings of a 2.42 ERA out of the Diamondbacks bullpen. The righty picked up 10 holds and three saves as a key member of Arizona’s relief corps.

Loaisiga left the Yankees in free agency after struggling with health and performance. He had to settle for a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks last winter. The veteran broke camp with the team and worked his way into a high-leverage role in Arizona. He rebuilt his value enough to earn a multi-year agreement from the Yankees.

Elbow injuries plagued Loaisiga’s final years in New York. His average fastball velocity had dipped to 96.7 mph in 2025. That number was back up to 97.6 this past year. Loaisiga posted modest strikeout numbers and a mediocre 10.6% swinging-strike rate, but getting a tick back on his heater was a positive development.

After a brief stint in the Giants’ organization, Loaisiga signed a minor league deal with the Yankees in 2016. He quickly moved through the system and established himself as one of the more intriguing young arms in the minors in the late 2010s. Loaisiga had been strictly a starter in the minors, but took on a multi-faceted role when he debuted with the Yankees in 2018.

articles.title: White Sox Trade Davis Martin, Luis Castillo To Rockies
body: The White Sox and Rockies announced a surprise trade on Thursday. Colorado acquires a pair of veteran starters, Davis Martin and Luis Castillo, in exchange for rookie left-hander Sean Sullivan and minor league catcher Douglas Veliz. The Rockies assume Castillo’s $22.75MM salary as a means of enticing Chicago to part with Martin.

It’s a big investment for a Colorado team starved for starting pitching. Martin is the centerpiece of the deal from their perspective. The Texas Tech product has had an inconsistent career but pitched at a roughly league average level over the last couple seasons. Martin has made 55 appearances over the last two years, pitching to a 4.02 earned run average across 288 2/3 innings.

A 14th-round pick in 2018, Martin debuted four years later. He was up and down from Triple-A as a rookie and then underwent Tommy John surgery, preventing him from establishing himself until 2025. Martin performed at a back-end level that year, posting a 4.10 ERA with a modest 17.3% strikeout rate over 26 games. He missed a month midseason with a forearm strain.

Martin won a camp battle to secure a spot in Will Venable’s season-opening rotation in 2026. He was one of the biggest early-season stories in the American League, pitching at an ace level through the end of May. Martin reeled off 67 2/3 innings with a flat 2.00 ERA while striking out 27% of opponents over his first 11 starts. He seemed ticketed for an All-Star berth and was in some early conversations as a dark horse Cy Young candidate.

articles.title: Mets, Darwinzon Hernández Agree To Three-Year Deal
body: The Mets are signing lefty reliever Darwinzon Hernández to a three-year, $12MM contract, reports José F. Rivera. The signing is still pending a physical. New York opened a spot on the 40-man roster by dropping Chayce McDermott on waivers this afternoon.

It’s a surprising contract length for a player who hasn’t pitched in the majors since 2022. Hernández has spent the last three and a half seasons with the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks in Nippon Professional Baseball. He turned in a 2.46 earned run average across 131 2/3 innings against Japan’s top hitters. That includes a 1.48 mark over 42 2/3 frames this past season, his best year in NPB.

Hernández has been on the radar for a while but won’t celebrate his 30th birthday until December. The Venezuela native was one of the top prospects in the Red Sox’ farm system in the late 2010s. He came up through the minors as a starter with huge raw stuff but never developed the command to match. The Sox moved him to the bullpen before his big league debut in 2019.

The 6’2″, 255-pound southpaw pitched 85 1/3 innings across parts of four seasons in Boston. He allowed just over five earned runs per nine with too much wildness to even stick in a relief role. Hernández punched out 32.2% of big league hitters behind a mid-90s fastball and a pair of breaking pitches. He also walked almost 18% of batters faced, allowing a.388 on-base percentage in the process.

articles.title: Royals Re-Sign Vince Velasquez To Minor League Deal
body: The Royals are in agreement with veteran righty Vince Velasquez on a new minor league contract, reports Robert Murray of FanSided. He’ll be back in MLB camp as a non-roster invitee.

Velasquez spent the second half of the 2026 season in the K.C. system. He signed a minor league deal around the All-Star Break after being waived by the Cubs. Velasquez started 10 of 12 outings with Triple-A Omaha, struggling to a 6.36 earned run average over 52 1/3 frames. He also logged 33 2/3 innings at the top minor league level in the Cubs’ system, combining for a 6.28 ERA. He fanned a league average 22.1% of opponents against an elevated 12.5% walk rate.

The 34-year-old Velasquez made a brief return to the big leagues with Chicago earlier in the season. He made a couple mop-up relief appearances, tossing 3 1/3 scoreless innings. That was first MLB action since 2023. He averaged 92.2 mph on his fastball while throwing a knuckle-curve and cutter.

Kansas City’s rotation depth took a number of injury hits this year. Cole Ragans, Luinder Avila, Ryan Bergert and Stephen Kolek are all going to miss a notable chunk of 2027 rehabbing elbow surgeries. Logan Evans, acquired from Seattle as the third piece of the Maikel Garcia trade, may also need a little more time to work back from January’s internal brace procedure.

articles.title: Orioles Notes: May, Goodman, Rotation
body: The Orioles made a run at Dustin May before the right-hander signed a three-year contract with the White Sox, writes Jeff Passan of ESPN. Chicago gave May a $52.5MM guarantee that was a little surprising given his inconsistency, yet Passan writes that Baltimore was “in the neighborhood” of that offer.

Baltimore hasn’t done much to this point of the offseason, yet they’re seemingly lurking with the potential for a notable move. That’s particularly true on the pitching side, as Jon Heyman of The New York Post writes that they’re primarily focused on arms. Baltimore’s best starter, Trevor Rogers, hit free agency and declined a qualifying offer. They’re trying to bring him back but could bring in another starter even if they’re also able to re-sign Rogers.

The O’s are apparently broadly open to any kind of roster shakeup short of trading Pete Alonso. They could use another leverage reliever, especially one from the left side. Their outfield looks a bat short. A rotation headlined by Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and Brandon Young probably doesn’t have a high enough ceiling to compete for an AL East title.

Baltimore has also looked for an offensive upgrade at backup catcher after trading Adley Rutschman over the summer. They have Samuel Basallo signed to a long-term deal but an uncertain designated hitter picture, so they could bring in another catcher and have the two split time behind the plate and at DH.

articles.title: Hunter Goodman Underwent Shoulder Surgery, Expected To Be Ready For Spring Training
body: Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman underwent left shoulder surgery at the beginning of the offseason, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. It was a cleanup procedure that is not expected to impact his readiness for the start of Spring Training.

Goodman missed a week and a half in the middle of August with a shoulder strain. While he had a minimal stint on the injured list, it seems he played through the injury for the stretch run. It’s probably not a coincidence that September was his worst month of the season, as he batted.192 with some of his lowest exit velocities of the year.

The righty-hitting Goodman still managed five home runs in the final month. That brought him to 41 for the season, 14 more than any other catcher and tied for sixth-most in MLB overall. Goodman has slugged 72 longballs over the last two seasons, batting.262/.317/.525 over that stretch. That rare offensive ability from the position has made Goodman a target of other teams, yet the Rox have unsurprisingly maintained a high ask on their best player.

Jon Morosi of The MLB Network suggested last week that some clubs felt Colorado might be more willing to make Goodman available this winter. The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon wrote earlier this week that while they’re willing to discuss Goodman, they more or less haven’t moved off their deadline demand for a monster return.

articles.title: Brewers Sign Braden Shewmake To Minor League Deal
body: The Brewers have signed infielder Braden Shewmake to a minor league deal, per Todd Rosiak of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. Shewmake also receives an invite to big league camp in spring training.

It’s a birthday present for Shewmake, who turns 29 today. He has become a journeyman depth infielder at this point in his career. When the calendar flipped to 2026, he was on the Royals roster, but he went to the Yankees via waivers before the season began. He was traded to the Astros in April and spent a few months with that club before getting designated for assignment and traded to the Brewers. Milwaukee designated him for assignment less than two weeks later. He cleared waivers, elected free agency and returned to the Astros via a minor league deal.

Around all those moves, he got into 34 big league games and stepped to the plate 91 times, hitting.259/.270/.424 in those. That brought his career numbers to 65 games, 162 plate appearances and a.196/.206/.320 line. He doesn’t do much with the bat but he’s considered a competent defender at shortstop, second base and third base.

articles.title: Rays Release Jesse Scholtens To Pursue KBO Opportunity
body: The Rays announced that right-hander Jesse Scholtens has been released to pursue an opportunity in the KBO League in South Korea. It’s unclear which KBO team is interested in Scholtens. Tampa’s 40-man roster count drops from 39 to 38.

Scholtens, 33 in April, was in an up-and-down role with the Rays this year. The club shuttled him between Triple-A and the majors in order to keep the big league staff stocked with fresh arms. He tossed 47 2/3 innings over 12 appearances, allowing 4.34 earned runs per nine frames. His 17.7% strikeout rate and 38.2% ground ball rate were both subpar but he limited walks to a 7.2% clip and did a good job avoiding damage. Statcast put his hard hit rate in the 66th percentile of qualified pitchers and his average exit velocity in the 70th.

Despite some serviceable results in 2026, Scholtens might have been squeezed off the roster in the future. He exhausted his final option in 2026, meaning he will be out of options going forward. The Rays, or another team, would no longer be able to oscillate him between the minors and the majors with ease. He qualified for arbitration this year and MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected him for a salary of $900K next year. Tomorrow is the non-tender deadline and it’s possible the Rays were going to cut him loose.

articles.title: Twins Looking To Add To Bullpen, Lineup
body: The Twins made two big signings this week but they’re not done. Catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the qualifying offer and right-hander Sonny Gray signed a two-year deal. Gray and general manager Jeremy Zoll met with reporters via Zoom today to re-introduce Gray to the media. Per Aaron Gleeman of AaronGleeman.com, Zoll said that adding to the bullpen and lineup remain priorities even after the Jeffers and Gray deals. “We’re working both paths right now,” Zoll said.

Those are sensible targets. The Twins opened the 2025 season with a respectable bullpen but they tore it down at that year’s deadline, sending out Jhoan Duran, Louis Varland, Griffin Jax, Brock Stewart and Danny Coulombe. That left the relief group in rough shape going into 2026, though they did pick up arms like Jeff Hoffman, Yoendrys Gómez and Tommy Nance midseason. Despite those pickups, Minnesota relievers still posted a collective 4.74 earned run average on the year, a mark that was better than just four other clubs.

Bolstering the bullpen for 2027 makes plenty of sense. It’s unclear at this point where the club wants to end up financially. MLBTR’s Payroll Tracker projects the Twins to spend $125MM on next year’s club, before accounting for Jeffers or Gray. The $55MM Gray deal is backloaded a bit, with just a $20MM salary next year. Between Gray and Jeffers, $43.15MM should be added onto that figure, minus a couple of league minimum salaries for players being bumped off.

articles.title: Cubs Claim Chayce McDermott
body: The Cubs announced they have claimed right-hander Chayce McDermott off waivers from the Mets. Jon Heyman of The New York Post reported the claim prior to the official announcement. There wasn’t any previous indication that McDermott lost his roster spot with New York but they evidently tried to quietly pass him through waivers. The Cubs had multiple 40-man vacancies and won’t need to make a corresponding move. The Mets’ 40-man count drops to 39.

McDermott, 28, hasn’t yet clicked in the majors. He has thrown 20 1/3 innings for the Orioles, Dodgers and Mets over the past three seasons. He has allowed 23 earned runs in that time, giving him a career ERA of 10.18.

In the minors, he has shown big strikeout stuff but a lack of control. Dating back to the start of 2023, he has thrown 320 innings on the farm, mostly at the Triple-A level. In that time, he has a 3.99 ERA. His 30.5% strikeout rate is well above average but his 14.6% walk rate is rough. If he could rein in the walks while keeping the punchouts, then he could be a real asset.

He finished the 2026 season on the Mets’ roster but out of options. They announced earlier this week that they had signed him to a deal for 2027, even though he hasn’t yet qualified for arbitration. The specific salary of that contract hasn’t been reported but teams do these deals for pre-arb players with the plan of later putting them on waivers. The hope is that the salary on the contract is high enough for other clubs to pass.

articles.title: Blue Jays Claim Christian Cairo, Designate Chase Lee For Assignment
body: The Blue Jays announced that they have claimed infielder Christian Cairo off waivers from the Dodgers. Right-hander Chase Lee has been designated for assignment in a corresponding 40-man move. The Dodgers designated Cairo for assignment earlier this week when they added several young players to the roster in order to protect them from the Rule 5 draft.

Cairo, 26 in June, is a glove-first infielder. He hasn’t made his major league debut yet but he is clearly valued as a borderline roster player. Atlanta took him from Cleveland in the Rule 5 draft two years ago. He didn’t break camp and was sent back to the Guardians at the end of 2025 spring training. He became a free agent a year later and got a minor league deal with the Phillies. That deal had an upward mobility clause in it. The Phils gave him a roster spot but kept Cairo on optional assignment. He was put on waivers in September and claimed by the Mets.

Earlier this month, the Mets signed Cairo to a contract for 2027, even though he hasn’t yet qualified for arbitration. The specific salary on that deal hasn’t been reported but teams do this sometimes with the goal of getting the player through waivers, hoping that the salary is high enough for other teams to pass. It hasn’t worked in this case as the Dodgers and now the Blue Jays have grabbed him from the wire.

articles.title: Royals, Randy Dobnak Avoid Arbitration
body: The Royals and right-hander Randy Dobnak have agreed to a $1.35MM salary for next year, thus avoiding arbitration, reports Jeff Passan of ESPN. Tomorrow is the deadline for teams to decide whether or not to tender contracts to their arbitration-eligible players.

Dobnak, 32 in January, took a circuitous route to his first arbitration deal. He made his debut for the Twins in 2019 and pitched for that club again in 2020. In March of 2021, before Dobnak had qualified for arbitration, he and the Twins agreed to a five-year, $9.25MM extension covering the 2021 through 2025 seasons.

The righty’s performance fell off in the first year of that pact, as he posted a 7.64 earned run average. He was stuck in the minors in 2022 and 2023 and then made very brief appearances in the majors in 2024 and 2025. He was traded to the Tigers at the 2025 deadline. Detroit kept him in the minors and then declined the 2026 club option on Dobnak’s deal.

That sent Dobnak to free agency. He secured a minor league deal with the Mariners for 2026. He triggered an upward mobility clause in that deal in June and got flipped to the Royals. Kansas City had Cole Ragans, Kris Bubic and Seth Lugo on the injured list at the time and multiple depth arms had undergone surgery, so the team needed innings.

articles.title: Astros To Hire Bobby Wilson As Bench Coach
body: The Astros are going to hire Bobby Wilson as their bench coach, per a report from Chandler Rome and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. Wilson will work under new manager Brad Ausmus. He was previously working with the Nationals as catching coordinator.

Wilson, now 43, played in the big leagues as a catcher from 2008 to 2019. When his playing days were done, he quickly pivoted to the next phase of his career. In December of 2019, just a few months after his last game as a player, the Rangers hired him as a Double-A manager. One year later, he got bumped to the big league staff as catching coordinator. He got that same job with the Nats one year ago.

Per Mark Zuckerman of Nats Journal, Wilson is credited with improving the defense of Keibert Ruiz this year. Ruiz was graded as a negative defender by Fielding Run Value from 2022 to 2025 but he crept into positive territory in 2026. Defensive Runs Saved had him below par in the first two years of that span and just barely above average in 2024 and 2025 before a jump to a mark of seven DRS this year. Wilson has a good reputation in the game and should also be familiar to Ausmus. Wilson played five games for the Tigers in 2026 when Ausmus was the skipper there.

The Astros moved on from manager Joe Espada at the end of this season and parted ways with many of his staff members as well. Bench coach Omar Lopez was offered another role in the organization but was not retained in his previous job. Wilson will now take up that mantle as Ausmus takes over as the skipper.

articles.title: Yankees Notes: Garcia, Bohm, Hyde
body: The Mariners were looking for infield help and got it yesterday, agreeing to a six-player deal with the Royals which sent Maikel Garcia to Seattle. The Yankees are also looking to make changes on the infield and Jon Morosi of MLB Network reports they checked in with the Royals about Garcia prior to him becoming a Mariner.

The infield in the Bronx is pretty up in the air right now. Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. is now a free agent. Third baseman Ryan McMahon had a rough year and the club might make a change at that position, even though he’s signed for one more year. Shortstop George Lombard Jr. has just 42 games of big league experience. Ben Rice and Luis García Jr. are battling for first base time with Giancarlo Stanton potentially in the designated hitter slot, so García might end up playing some second base.

At this relatively early stage of the offseason, there are many ways it could play out, so it makes sense for the front office to consider all sorts of possibilities. They’ve already been connected to free agents such as Brandon Lowe and Alec Bohm.

Calling the Royals on Maikel Garcia could have made a lot of sense. Kansas City was clearly looking for starting pitching help. Two of the three players they got from Seattle were immediate rotation additions, health permitting. Bryce Miller already has over 500 big league innings under his belt. Logan Evans has under 90 major league frames to his name and missed 2026 while recovering from UCL surgery but he could jump into the Kansas City rotation as soon as he is recovered.

articles.title: Orioles Claim Braden Nett, Carson Baumler Returned By Rangers
body: The Orioles have claimed righty Braden Nett off waivers from the Athletics, per a team announcement. Nett was designated for assignment on Tuesday after the A’s acquired Raymond Burgos from the Red Sox. Baltimore also announced that 2025 Rule 5 Draft pick Carter Baumler was returned by the Rangers.

Nett’s stock plummeted quickly with the A’s. He came over from the Padres at the 2025 trade deadline in the deal that sent Mason Miller to San Diego. The righty slotted in among the better pitching prospects in the A’s system. Nett struggled through a brutal 2026 campaign plagued by injuries and poor performance.

San Diego signed Nett as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He topped out at Double-A in the organization. Nett posted intriguing strikeout numbers, but untenable walk rates. He took that to an extreme level this past season. In 41 2/3 minor league innings across three levels, Nett struck out 51 and walked 47. He recorded a 7.99 ERA.

Nett has a five-pitch arsenal that has graded out well with scouts. FanGraphs has his fastball and curveball as plus pitches, with his slider and cutter also being league-average offerings. Nett just hasn’t been in the strike zone often enough to take advantage of his solid stuff. He’ll get another fresh start in Baltimore’s organization.

articles.title: Reds To Sign Dominic Fletcher To Minors Deal
body: Veteran outfielder Dominic Fletcher is sticking with the Reds on a minor league deal, per Mark Sheldon of MLB.com. The agreement includes an invitation to MLB Spring Training. Fletcher spent the final month of last season at Triple-A Louisville.

The 29-year-old Fletcher began the year in the Pirates’ system. He had a strong year at Triple-A Indianapolis, slashing.301/.386/.485 across 63 games. Fletcher didn’t earn a big-league promotion and exercised an opt-out clause in his deal in July. He wound up back with Indianapolis later in the month.

Pittsburgh released Fletcher again in mid-August. He latched on with the Reds in early September. Fletcher struggled in 14 games with Louisville and returned to minor league free agency. He’s decided to stay in the organization and will have a shot to earn a roster spot in the spring.

Fletcher last played in the majors in 2025. He appeared in 12 games with the White Sox. He was a league-average bat in Chicago across a small sample, but has generally underwhelmed in the big leagues. Fletcher has a 67 wRC+ in 377 MLB plate appearances. He debuted with the Diamondbacks in 2023. The White Sox acquired him straight up for minor league pitcher Cristian Mena in February 2024.

articles.title: White Sox Hire Kyle Wilson As Assistant Hitting Coach
body: The White Sox are hiring Kyle Wilson as an assistant hitting coach, reports James Fegan of The Chicago Sun-Times. He’d been a hitting coordinator with the Rays.

Wilson replaces Joel McKeithan, who held the assistant HC role on the South Side for the last two seasons. McKeithan got the lead hitting coach job with the Cardinals a couple weeks ago, returning to the lead role he’d held in Cincinnati from 2023-24. This will be Wilson’s first job on a big league staff.

The 39-year-old Wilson (40 in February) played collegiately at North Carolina State. He was twice drafted but never appeared in a game as a professional player. Wilson worked as a volunteer assistant with his alma mater and spent a year coaching in the Seattle farm system before getting hired by the Rays in 2019. He’s worked with Tampa Bay prospects for the past seven years.

Derek Shomon is entering his second season as Chicago’s lead hitting voice. General manager Chris Getz said at the end of the year that he expected to bring back Will Venable’s entire staff. While McKeithan got a better opportunity in St. Louis, the assistant hitting coach role appears to be their only change.

articles.title: Cubs Interested In Teruaki Sato, Jarren Duran
body: The league’s top offense is in the market for more bats this winter. Patrick Mooney of The Athletic reports that the Cubs have extensively scouted NPB import Teruaki Sato. The club has also evaluated Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran, a popular trade candidate.

While the Cubs have clearer needs on the pitching side, there are holes to fill in the lineup. Longtime outfielders Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki are both free agents. Reserve outfielders Michael Conforto and Tyrone Taylor are also on the open market, along with catcher Carson Kelly.

Sato is one of the most sought-after hitters available this offseason. He ranked behind only Suzuki and Randy Arozarena among bats in our Top 50 Free Agents list. Sato has racked up 79 home runs and 208 RBI with the Hanshin Tigers over the past two seasons. He won the NPB’s Triple Crown in 2026.

The defensive fit for Sato in Chicago isn’t ideal. He’s been almost exclusively a third baseman for the past four seasons. The Cubs obviously have Alex Bregman locked in at the hot corner for the foreseeable future. It’s a rock-solid group around the infield with Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner, and Michael Busch joining Bregman.

Sato does have experience in the outfield. He played mostly right field in 2021 and 2022 before moving to the infield on a near full-time basis. He’s mixed in on the grass in recent seasons, making 44 appearances in right field and one in left field over the past two years.

articles.title: Nationals Prefer Short-Term Deals In Search For Rotation Help
body: The Nationals are in the market for rotation help, but it doesn’t sound as though a particularly big free agent splash is in the cards. Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic reports that while Washington has explored the trade market for controllable starting pitching, the team prefers to stick to short-term deals when it comes to free agency. They’ve inquired on Kris Bubic, Brady Singer and Kona Takahashi, per the report.

Bubic, 29, is the youngest of the bunch and has the highest upside. He’s been persistently plagued by injuries in recent years but is a former first-round pick and top prospect who’s posted a 2.98 ERA, 25.5% strikeout rate, 8.1% walk rate and 48.6% ground-ball rate in his past 217 1/3 big league innings. That production has been stretched out across four seasons, however. Bubic had Tommy John surgery in 2023, missed significant time in 2025 due to a strained rotator cuff and was limited to 55 innings this past season due to elbow troubles.

articles.title: Astros To Hire Matt Bayer As Assistant GM
body: The Astros are making another addition in the front office. Matt Bayer is expected to join general manager Randy Flores’ staff, reports Brian McTaggart of MLB.com. Bayer will serve as an assistant general manager, replacing Connor Huff.

Bayer has worked in baseball for nearly 15 years. His entire career has been spent in the Cardinals organization. Bayer first came aboard as a quantitative analyst heading into the 2012 season. He steadily worked his way up the ladder in the scouting and baseball development departments. Bayer earned the title of senior director of baseball development at the end of the 2024 season.

Huff resigned last week to take a job outside of baseball. He’d been with the organization for the past five seasons. Flores had the green light to hire a replacement, and he found a fit in his former organization. The newly installed GM had been in the Cardinals front office for more than a decade before getting the top gig in Houston. He overlapped for many years with Bayer.

The Astros are back up to three AGMs, with Bayer joining Gavin Dickey and Charles Cook. Dickey and Cook are holdovers from former general manager Dana Brown’s staff. It’s been an offseason of change in the organization, with Flores replacing Brown and Brad Ausmus taking over for former manager Joe Espada.

articles.title: MLBTR Podcast: Jake Bauers, Ryan Jeffers, Dustin May, Reliever Deals, And More
body: The latest episode of the MLB Trade Rumors Podcast is now live on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and wherever you get your podcasts! Make sure you subscribe as well! You can also use the player at this link to listen, if you don’t use Spotify or Apple for podcasts.
This week, host Darragh McDonald is joined by Steve Adams of MLB Trade Rumors to discuss…

The Red Sox signing Jake Bauers (2:00) What does this mean for Jarren Duran, Triston Casas and Masataka Yoshida? articles.title: A’s Agree To Minor League Deals With Joey Wiemer, Luke Little
body: The Athletics and outfielder Joey Wiemer are in agreement on a minor league contract, reports Martin Gallegos of MLB.com. The team’s transaction log also indicates that they’ve added left-handed reliever Luke Little on a minor league pact. Presumably, both players will be in big league camp next year.

Wiemer, 28 in February, has suited up for four teams in parts of four big league seasons (2023-26). He’s a 2020 fourth-rounder who has previously garnered some top-100 fanfare but has yet to settle into any kind of regular role in the majors, due in no small part to his lofty strikeout totals. The righty-swinging Wiemer has plenty of pop in his bat and a plus glove across all three outfield slots, but he’s a career.216/.296/.380 hitter with a 30.4% strikeout rate in 582 plate appearances.

Wiemer had a big first week of the 2026 season with the Nationals, collecting 10 hits (two homers, one triple) in his first 22 trips to the plate. He only tallied 10 more knocks over his next 61 plate appearances before being designated for assignment.

With the A’s, Wiemer will hope to carve out a bench role. He’s a.273/.324/.535 hitter (129 wRC+) in 216 career plate appearances versus lefties, although even that production comes with a 32.4% strikeout rate and is heavily buoyed by a.356 average on balls in play. The A’s have lefty hitters Tyler Soderstrom and Lawrence Butler in left and right field, respectively. Soderstrom has held his own against southpaws in his career, but Butler is a.229/.282/.387 hitter versus southpaws.

articles.title: Royals, Mariners Swap Maikel Garcia For Bryce Miller In Six-Player Deal
body: The Mariners and Royals have lined up on a six-player blockbuster, announcing Wednesday that infielder Maikel Garcia, reliever James McArthur and right-handed pitching prospect L.P. Langevin are going from Kansas City to Seattle in exchange for right-handed starters Bryce Miller and Logan Evans as well as left-handed reliever Jose A. Ferrer.

Seattle was known to be hunting for an infielder on the left side to pair with young shortstop Colt Emerson. Kansas City was in the market for pitching help. Both sides accomplished their goals with today’s deal. Garcia was an All-Star and Gold Glove award winner in 2025. Miller will immediately slot into the Royals’ rotation, with Ferrer potentially taking over as closer and at the very least filling a key late-inning role.

Garcia inked a five-year, $57.5MM extension covering the 2026-30 seasons just last winter. The deal also includes a $21MM club option ($3.2MM buyout) for the 2031 season. It added an extra two years of club control, with the club option factored in. Garcia is set to make $7MM in 2027.

After serving as a speedy utility option in his first few seasons, Garcia broke out as a critical cog in Kansas City’s lineup in 2025. He slashed.286/.351/.449 with 16 homers and 23 steals as the everyday third baseman. Garcia posted a career-best 120 wRC+ across 666 plate appearances.

articles.title: Twins Sign Sonny Gray
body: Sonny Gray is headed back to Minnesota. The Twins announced Wednesday that they’ve signed the free-agent righty to a two-year contract that’ll reportedly guarantee him $55MM and contains both full no-trade protection and an opt-out opportunity following the 2027 season. Gray, a client of McKinnis Sports, starred for Minnesota in 2022-23 and finished second in American League Cy Young Award voting in the latter of those two seasons.

Gray will make a $20MM salary next year and would collect a $5MM buyout if he declines a $30MM player option for 2028. There’s a $27.5MM mutual option for the’29 season that comes with a $5MM buyout. He’ll essentially need to decide whether to opt out of one year and $30MM next offseason.

The righty’s original departure from the Twins came on the heels of a postseason run that was immediately followed by swift payroll reductions. Minnesota’s 2023 payroll pushed upwards of $155MM, but as the Pohlad family explored a sale of the club, payroll was slashed by around $50MM over the next two seasons. The Pohlads eventually walked back their efforts to sell the team, instead bringing in a trio of minority investors to pay off a reported debt in excess of $400MM.

articles.title: Mets To Meet With Kaima Taira
body: The Mets have scheduled an upcoming Zoom meeting with free agent right-hander Kaima Taira, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post. They join the Padres, Blue Jays, and both Chicago clubs as teams known to be in the market for the 27-year-old.

Taira will almost certainly sign in the next two weeks. His 45-day posting window won’t pause with the lockout, so all the players available via the posting system need to sign before then or remain with their teams in Asia. Taira shouldn’t have any problem commanding a significant contract as the consensus top pitcher coming over from a foreign league this offseason.

The 5’8″, 209-pound righty has spent his entire career with the Seibu Lions. He’s been a reliever for the majority of his career but worked from the rotation in 2023 and moved back to starting this year. Taira fired 146 innings of 1.36 ERA ball while striking out 24.8% of opposing hitters across 23 appearances. He led NPB starters in ERA and ranked seventh in strikeout percentage among the 45 pitchers with 100+ innings.

Evaluators with whom MLBTR spoke credited Taira for holding his mid-upper 90s velocity deep into starts and praised his splitter. He also features a cutter and slider and has more advanced command than Tatsuya Imai did when he was the top pitcher from NPB last offseason. Taira’s limited track record as a starter could dissuade some teams, but whichever club tops the bidding is likely to be one that buys him as a mid-rotation starter.

articles.title: White Sox Seeking Another Notable Starter After May Signing
body: The White Sox made one of the biggest strikes in free agency thus far, finalizing their three-year deal with Dustin May this afternoon. That $52.5MM guarantee was already the organization’s biggest signing since Andrew Benintendi four years ago, but it may not be their most notable move of this offseason.

ESPN’s Jeff Passan wrote this morning that the White Sox remained in the market for starting pitching. James Fegan of The Chicago Sun-Times suggests they’re aiming for someone who’d at least slot into the middle of the staff, reporting that they’re pursuing a starter “of similar magnitude” to May.

There are plenty of mid-rotation starters on the open market. Chicago has shown interest in NPB starter Kaima Taira, for one. Foster Griffin, Michael Soroka, Clay Holmes, Tyler Mahle, Casey Mize, Shota Imanaga, and Nick Pivetta are all candidates for a contract similar to or slightly below the May guarantee. That’s also true of Kevin Gausman or Nick Martinez if they command two-year deals, though they might pull $20MM+ annually on shorter terms.

Trevor Rogers, Freddy Peralta and Michael King should all beat the May deal and would probably require the White Sox to go north of $75MM — which they’ve incredibly still never done for any player. Rogers would also come attached to draft compensation after rejecting a qualifying offer from the Orioles.

articles.title: Mets, Joel Kuhnel Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Mets are in agreement with reliever Joel Kuhnel on a minor league contract, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post. The Octagon client will presumably be in camp as a non-roster invitee.

Kuhnel qualified for minor league free agency when he was outrighted by the Giants at the beginning of the offseason. They’d only claimed him off waivers in the waning weeks of the regular season as they navigated more than a dozen injuries on the pitching staff. He also pitched for the Athletics and Brewers earlier in the season, and his 10 appearances in Milwaukee should net him a World Series ring.

Between the trio of teams, the 31-year-old Kuhnel tossed 45 innings with a 4.40 earned run average. He got some early run in the A’s closer role and picked up eight saves, but most of the positives came in his first few weeks on the roster. Kuhnel only fanned 14% of batters faced overall and got grounders on half the batted balls he allowed. That’s the approach the 6’5″, 290 pound righty has had throughout his career. He leans on a 95 mph sinker and generates a lot of low-angle contact, but he’s never had bat-missing stuff.

Kuhnel doesn’t have any minor league options, which limits his roster flexibility. If he cracks the Mets’ big league roster at any point, they’d need to keep him in the majors or run him through waivers and allow him to retest free agency. He’ll need to pitch his way onto the roster for that to be a consideration, as the Mets are likely to add multiple reinforcements to a bullpen that doesn’t have a ton of certainty in the middle or late innings.

articles.title: Orioles Sign Junior Pérez, Alex Carrillo To Minor League Deals
body: The Orioles announced that they have signed outfielder Junior Pérez and right-hander Alex Carrillo to minor league deals. Presumably, each player will receive an invite to big league camp in spring training, though that wasn’t specified in the announcement.

Pérez, 25, seemed to have a breakout in 2025. A minor leaguer with the Athletics at the time, he drew walks at a 14.8% clip, hit 26 home runs and stole 27 bases. His 28.1% strikeout rate was really high but that was actually an improvement for him, as he struck out at a 35.4% pace the year prior.

The A’s gave him a 40-man spot at this time a year ago to keep him out of the Rule 5 draft. Unfortunately, his strikeout problems returned in 2026. He was designated for assignment midseason and traded to the White Sox. He was outrighted off the Chicago roster at season’s end and elected free agency.

He got to make a brief major league debut with the Sox, making 36 plate appearances. He struck out in 14 of those, a 38.9% pace. On the farm, he slashed.219/.301/.420 while striking out in 35.4% of his trips to the plate but still managed to hit 13 home runs and steal 19 bases in just 87 games.

Pérez clearly has some tools, though he will have to get the punchouts under control. If he’s able to earn his way back onto the roster, he has options remaining and could be an up-and-down depth piece. Baltimore’s outfield group currently consists of Colton Cowser, Dylan Beavers, Tyler O’Neill and others but the offseason is young and the club will likely change that outlook with some transactions before the next season begins.

articles.title: White Sox Designate Jordan Leasure For Assignment
body: The White Sox officially announced their signing of right-hander Dustin May. Fellow righty Jordan Leasure has been designated for assignment as the corresponding 40-man roster move. Leasure is expected to miss 2027 while recovering from surgery.

Leasure, now 28, seemed to have a breakout year in 2025. He gave the Sox 64 1/3 innings, allowing 3.92 earned runs per nine. His 11.2% walk rate was to the high side but he offset that by punching out 30.1% of batters faced. He was able to push into a leverage role with the rebuilding club, earning 14 holds and seven saves.

2026 was much more of a challenge for him. He got out to a rough start, getting optioned to the minors in May. He was recalled a couple of weeks later but then landed on the injured list with a flexor strain. He underwent surgery in August to repair a tear in his ulnar collateral ligament. The Sox announced that he was expected to be ready by spring training 2028, suggesting he would miss the entire 2027 campaign. He finished 2026 with a 6.27 ERA in 18 2/3 innings.

Leasure’s service time count is just under three years. He was going to qualify for arbitration as a Super Two player. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected him for a $1MM salary next year. Friday is the non-tender deadline and it’s possible the Sox weren’t planning to tender him a contract.

articles.title: White Sox Sign Dustin May
body: November 18: The Sox made it official today.

November 17: The White Sox and right-hander Dustin May are in agreement on a three-year, $52.5MM contract. The team has yet to officially announce the deal. May is represented by Paragon Sports International.

It’s a surprisingly strong deal for the pitcher. The White Sox are placing a notable bet on the right-hander’s relative youth — he’ll pitch next season at 29 — and power arsenal, while looking past his lengthy injury history and middling bottom-line results when healthy in each of the past two seasons.

May played the 2026 season on a one-year, $12.5MM deal originally signed with the Cardinals, who traded him to the Brewers alongside reliever JoJo Romero at the deadline. He posted back-end results in St. Louis and was torched for a 5.65 ERA in 10 starts (36 2/3 innings) with Milwaukee before also struggling in the playoffs. May finished out the regular season with a 4.70 ERA in a career-high 145 2/3 innings (4.77 in 156 2/3 frames, including the playoffs).

Over the past two seasons, May has combined to toss 278 innings with a 4.82 ERA. He’s fanned a roughly average 22.2% of his opponents in that time with similarly average command (8.8% walk rate) and ground-ball tendencies (42%).

articles.title: Dipoto: “Zero” Chance Mariners Trade Another Starter
body: The Mariners’ blockbuster acquisition of third baseman Maikel Garcia earlier today subtracted righties Bryce Miller and Logan Evans from their rotation outlook. It’s been known for some time that Seattle was much, much more open to dealing from its rotation supply this winter than in offseasons past, but it seems that swap with the Royals is where the starting pitching trades both start and end.

President of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto told the Mariners beat today that there’s “zero” chance he moves another starting pitcher now that Miller and Evans are out the door (link via Adam Jude of the Seattle Times). Dipoto added that the Mariners would like to add another right-handed bat, a veteran infield presence and, with Jose A. Ferrer headed to Kansas City as part of that swap, bring in an established left-handed reliever.

Seattle’s 2027 rotation now lines up to include Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and touted prospect Kade Anderson, the No. 3 overall pick from the 2025 draft. Young right-hander Ryan Sloan is widely considered one of the best pitching prospects in baseball behind Anderson — if not the best — and could arrive in the majors “at any point” next year, according to Dipoto.

articles.title: Seth Halvorsen Undergoes Tommy John Surgery
body: The Dodgers announced that right-hander Seth Halvorsen has undergone ulnar collateral ligament reconstruction surgery, also known as Tommy John surgery, on his throwing arm. He will miss the entire 2027 season.

Halvorsen, 27 in February, was acquired from the Rockies ahead of the trade deadline a few months back. He has huge velocity, with a four-seamer and sinker that both average over 99 miles per hour, but hasn’t translated that into big league results just yet. Between the Rockies and Dodgers, he has thrown 81 major league innings thus far with a 4.78 earned run average. His 49.2% ground ball rate is strong but his 20% strikeout rate and 11.1% walk rate are both worse than average.

Despite the underwhelming numbers, the Dodgers took a shot on the stuff. The club has a strong reputation for helping pitchers reach their ceilings. If that’s going to happen with Halvorsen, it will have to wait.

There’s no injured list during the offseason. It goes away five days after the World Series and doesn’t come back until camps open in the spring. If the Dodgers still believe in the arm over the long term, they could keep Halvorsen on the 40-man through the winter. Once spring training begins, he could be put on the major league 60-day injured list to open a 40-man spot. That would require giving him a full year of big league pay and service time. He was on optional assignment at the end of the 2026 season and still has options, so he could be kept in the minors next year, but that would involve him holding his 40-man spot.

articles.title: Rockies Re-Sign TJ Shook To Minor League Deal
body: The Rockies announced that they have re-signed right-hander TJ Shook to a minor league deal. Prior to the official announcement, it was reported by Thomas Harding of MLB.com, who noted that Shook has been assigned to Triple-A Albuquerque.

Shook, 29 in May, played minor league ball for the Brewers and Mets from 2021 to 2025. The Rockies took him from the latter club in the minor league phase of the Rule 5 draft a year ago. He got to make his major league debut with Colorado this year, allowing seven earned runs in 7 2/3 innings. He was outrighted off the roster at season’s end and elected free agency.

The results were better in the minors, as Shook tossed 57 1/3 innings for the Isotopes with a 3.45 earned run average. There was probably some good fortune in there, as his 21% strikeout rate and 12.1% walk rate were subpar while his 77% strand rate was to the fortunate side. Shook’s fastball only averaged about 92-93 miles per hour on the year but he also mixed in a cutter, slider and changeup.

The Rockies will undoubtedly need arms next year. It’s always a challenge having a competent pitching with Coors Field as a home field but the club has been struggling even more than usual in recent years. Colorado’s pitchers had a collective 5.59 ERA in 2026, worst in the majors. If Shook can earn his way back onto the 40-man, he still has a couple of option years.

articles.title: Royals Designate Kyle Isbel For Assignment
body: The Royals announced their six-player trade with the Mariners, which was reported earlier today. It was a three-for-three swap but all three players heading to Kansas City had 40-man roster spots, compared to just two of the players going to Seattle. The Royals therefore needed to open a 40-man spot and designated outfielder Kyle Isbel for assignment.

Isbel, 30 in March, has played for the Royals in parts of the past six seasons. He has been a standout defender and decent baserunner but hasn’t done much at the plate. He has made 1,832 plate appearances to this point in his career with just 29 home runs and a subpar 5.7% walk rate. He has a.235/.284/.357 slash line and 75 wRC+, indicating he has been 25% worse than league average as a hitter overall.

Despite that lack of punch from the batter’s box, he has been a valuable player thanks to his work on the grass. In over 4,000 innings of outfield work, mostly in center, Isbel has been credited with 34 Defensive Runs Saved, 51 Outs Above Average and a grade of 40 from Fielding Run Value.

That defense was enough for the Royals to stick with Isbel through two arbitration seasons. He made $1.75MM last year and $2.7MM this year. He was slated for one more arb year in 2027 before reaching free agency. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected him for a bump to $3.5MM.

articles.title: Athletics Add Trevor Amicone, Casey Weathers To Coaching Staff
body: The Athletics announced a pair of new additions to their coaching staff Wednesday. Trevor Amicone has been hired as the team’s new hitting coach. He’d previously been an assistant hitting coach with the Twins. The A’s also named Casey Weathers their new pitching coach. He’d previously been the Phillies’ director of pitching development.

Amicone spent the 2025-26 seasons as Minnesota’s assistant hitting coach at the major league level. He’d previously been a hitting coach in the Yankees’ minor league ranks for five seasons, breaking in with their Dominican Summer League affiliate before spending the 2023-24 seasons as the hitting coach for the Yankees’ Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Triple-A affiliate. He was one of two assistant hitting coaches in Minnesota. It’s not clear yet whether the Twins will replace him or simply give a larger workload to lead hitting coach Keith Beauregard and remaining assistant Rayden Sierra.

Weathers was a first-round draft pick by the Rockies in 2007 and ranked as one of their best prospects for several years. The now-41-year-old Weathers (no relation to Yankees southpaw Ryan Weathers) pitched in the minors from 2007-16 across four organizations but never reached the majors. Following his retirement as a player, Weathers was hired by the Reds to coach in their minor league ranks. He’s been the pitching coach for their Rookie-level and Triple-A clubs but was hired by Philadelphia to oversee the organization’s pitching development efforts following the 2024 season.

articles.title: Red Sox Acquire Nick Fortes
body: The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the Rays, according to announcements from both clubs. Tampa gets minor league right-hander Angel Roa in return. The Sox designated catcher Connor Wong to open a 40-man spot for Fortes.

It’s probably not a coincidence that this deal came together just before Friday’s non-tender deadline. The Red Sox and Rays both have a starter behind the plate, as Boston has Adley Rutschman and Tampa has Liam Hicks. Each club also went into the winter with an arbitration-eligible backup on the roster, the Rays with Fortes and the Red Sox with Wong.

MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects Wong for a $2MM salary next year. Fortes is projected slightly higher at $3.4MM. Wong’s defense doesn’t get strong grades. He seemed like maybe he was breaking out at the plate in 2024 when he hit 13 home runs and slashed.280/.333/.425. Unfortunately, he has hit.214/.287/.299 over the past two seasons. That has made him replacement level or worse for that span.

Wong still has an option remaining. The Sox could have tendered him a contract and kept him as depth in the minors, but they also have Mickey Gasper on the roster. Gasper is also still optionable and he is cheaper because he hasn’t qualified for arbitration yet. The Sox have decided to move on from Wong. They have some time to work out a trade but the most likely outcome is that he will be non-tendered on Friday.

articles.title: Reds Receiving Trade Interest In Nick Lodolo
body: As clubs around the league scour the market for rotation help, the Reds have been receiving trade interest in left-hander Nick Lodolo, per Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. There’s no indication any kind of deal is close at the moment.

Lodolo, 29 in February, is down to one final year of club control. He’s eligible for arbitration this winter and projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz to earn $5.7MM for the upcoming 2027 campaign.

If the Reds were to trade Lodolo, they’d be selling low. The former No. 7 overall pick and top prospect broke out with a terrific 2025 season that saw him pitch 156 2/3 innings with a 3.33 ERA, 24.3% strikeout rate, 4.8% walk rate and 42.6% ground-ball rate. All of his numbers trended the wrong direction during an injury-marred 2026 campaign, however.

Recurring blister issues have been a problem for Lodolo over the years, and that was again the case in’26, when he started just 21 games and pitched 108 2/3 frames. Lodolo managed only a 4.97 earned run average in that time. His strikeout rate plummeted to 17.1%, while his walk rate nearly doubled to 9.5%. Lodolo posted a strong 12.4% swinging-strike rate and 32.7% opponents’ chase rate in’25 but saw those numbers drop to 9% and 28.4%, respectively. Both are below average.

articles.title: Latest On Corey Seager
body: It’s no big secret that the Rangers are putting out feelers, trying to line up a Corey Seager trade. Even if they can agree to a framework with another club, Seager would have to give his consent. As a 10-and-5 guy, Seager has full no-trade rights. Jeff Passan of ESPN reports that Seager is open to moving but has a narrow list of teams he’s willing to join. Passan adds there’s no momentum towards a deal right now.

Players get full no-trade protection when they have at least ten years of big league service and have spent at least the last five years with the same club, hence “10-and-5”. Seager is five years into his ten-year pact with the Rangers, so there’s still five years left to go. He’ll make $31MM in each of those remaining seasons for a total of $155MM. Seager is still capable of strong production when on the field but that’s a lot of money for an injury-prone player who will celebrate his 34th birthday in April.

In 2026, Seager went on the injured list for a concussion and twice hit the IL related to lower back inflammation. He also had surgery after the season was done to remove a bone spur from his elbow. He got into just 102 contests on the year, his fourth straight season coming up short of the 125-game mark. He hit 20 home runs but his 23.6% strikeout rate was a career high. His.227/.312/.424 batting line led to a 106 wRC+, tied for the worst mark of his career.

articles.title: Angels Acquire Jace Jung
body: The Angels announced Wednesday that they’ve acquired infielder Jace Jung from the Tigers in exchange for cash. Detroit designated Jung, a former No. 12 overall pick (2022) and top prospect, for assignment yesterday.

The younger brother of Rangers third baseman Josh Jung, Jace has appeared in parts of three major league seasons. He’s totaled only 160 big league plate appearances and carries an ugly.193/.319/.230 batting line. Jung has walked in a stout 15% of his plate appearances but has also fanned at an untenable 30%.

Jung’s time in Detroit’s minor league system has had its ups and downs but has generally been productive. He’s posted an.801 OPS or better at each individual minor league level, including a career.244/.362/.439 slash in 1478 Triple-A plate appearances across the past three seasons. That said, Jung’s production in Triple-A has dipped with each repeat of the level; this year, he produced only a.227/.344/.421 slash in 133 games. By measure of wRC+, he was still seven percent better than average (thanks to that big OBP), but Jung didn’t make particularly strong levels of contact (88.6 mph average exit velocity, 36.5% hard-hit rate).

articles.title: The Best Fits For Trevor Rogers
body: MLBTR’s series of examining the market for the best free agents continues. We’re on to Trevor Rogers, the only starting pitcher who declined the qualifying offer and arguably the #2 pitcher in the class. Rogers’ first couple seasons were up and down, with his career reaching a nadir when he was optioned to Triple-A by the Orioles within three weeks of that club acquiring him at the 2024 deadline. He was in the minors as recently as June 2025, as Baltimore’s acquisition of the southpaw for Kyle Stowers and Connor Norby initially looked disastrous.

Rogers flipped a switch midway through the’25 campaign. He managed a sub-2.00 ERA in his final 17 starts of that season, going from rotation depth to Opening Day starter in 2026. Rogers had a rocky opening to the’26 campaign and missed a couple weeks due to illness, but he was lights out again for the final four months of the season. Rogers pitched to a 2.90 ERA with a 24.8% strikeout rate and tidy 4.4% walk rate from June 1 onward. Only seven pitchers threw more innings than his 121 frames in that stretch.

The former first-rounder is up to 47 starts with a 3.23 earned run average since he returned to the big leagues last June. He’s fanned 23.2% of opponents against a 6.2% walk rate while averaging nearly six innings per start. Rogers doesn’t have the huge swing-and-miss rates associated with most top-end starters, but he gets excellent life on a 94 mph fastball that opponents have a difficult time squaring up. He’s fifth in infield pop-up rate among pitchers with 200+ innings over the last two seasons.

articles.title: Giants Open To Offers On Casey Schmitt In Search For Pitching Help
body: As the Giants scour the market for pitching help, they’ve floated the possibility of trading infielder/outfielder Casey Schmitt, reports Jeff Passan of ESPN. There’s no indication any sort of deal is close, but Schmitt is the type of controllable infielder who could net them some needed arms.

Schmitt, 28 in March, swatted a career-high 21 home runs this past season while slashing.271/.301/.478. His 2.7% walk rate ranked dead last among the 205 big leaguers who totaled at least 400 plate appearances, but a lack of plate discipline seemed to permeate the entire 2026 Giants roster; San Francisco’s 7.4% walk rate was also the worst in baseball, and several Giants hitters posted career-worst walk rates in’26. Schmitt himself walked at a much healthier (albeit still below-average) 7.8% rate as recently as the 2025 season.

While Schmitt has long graded as a plus defender at third base, that spot is spoken for by Matt Chapman. Willy Adames is locked in at shortstop. Rafael Devers and Bryce Eldridge have first base and designated hitter covered. Schmitt could play second base, but if the Giants want to get a real look at former top prospect Marcelo Mayer — who came over from the Red Sox in the Erik Miller deadline swap — that’s the only available spot for Mayer, a former No. 4 overall draft pick.

articles.title: Nationals To Sign Hagen Danner To Minor League Deal
body: The Nationals are adding right-hander Hagen Danner on a minor league agreement, reports Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic. He spent last season in the minors with the Reds and Angels.

The 28-year-old Danner posted a 6.35 ERA in 37 appearances at Triple-A in 2026. He had a middling 22.1% strikeout rate and a massive 15.6% walk rate. Danner was in Spring Training with the Reds and pitched well over nine games (3.12 ERA, 28.6% strikeout rate). He didn’t break camp with the team and struggled with Louisville. Cincinnati released him in July. He latched on with the Angels in August.

Danner was drafted by the Blue Jays out of high school in 2017. He was a catcher back then. Danner transitioned to pitching in 2021. He posted solid results in the minors with Toronto and earned a brief look in the majors in 2023. Danner recorded one out before leaving with an oblique injury in his lone appearance.
The oblique strain ended Danner’s 2023 campaign. He never made it back up with the Blue Jays and was designated for assignment at the end of the 2024 season. He was in Seattle’s system in 2025.

Danner was generally a two-pitch guy at Triple-A this past year. He leaned on a mid-80s slider more than half of the time. He threw a four-seamer that sat at 96.3 mph at a 46.1% clip. Danner also used the occasional sinker and cutter. The pitch mix resulted in an underwhelming 10% swinging-strike rate this season. He’ll likely need to miss more bats and throw more strikes to get another look in the majors.

articles.title: Ryan Jeffers Declined Multi-Year Offer From Twins To Accept QO
body: Ryan Jeffers will be back in Minnesota for another season. The slugging catcher surprisingly accepted the one-year, $23.15MM qualifying offer this afternoon — just days after reports that he planned to decline in search of a multi-year deal. Jeffers apparently had at least one multi-year offer on the table from his longtime club.

Dan Hayes of The Athletic reports that Jeffers rejected a multi-year proposal from the Twins in favor of the QO. Financial terms of that offer aren’t clear, though the 29-year-old clearly preferred to bet on himself with the hefty salary. Jeffers narrowly secured the record for highest salary by a catcher in history, beating the $23.1MM average annual value of J.T. Realmuto’s five-year contract with Philadelphia. (Yankees reliever David Bednar coincidentally also narrowly locked in the salary record at his position as the only other player in this year’s class to accept the qualifying offer.)

Nothing stops the Twins and Jeffers from continuing to discuss multi-year frameworks now that the QO is in place. However, Jeffers seemed excited about the idea of betting on himself with the short-term commitment. “(Owner Tom Pohlad’s) commitments to the 2027 team and the team going forward plays a factor in me coming back and wanting to see where this core goes,” he told Hayes. “Taking the one-year deal gives us opportunities that something else might not.”

articles.title: Mariners, Bryce Conley Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Mariners are in agreement with right-hander Bryce Conley on a minor league contract, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. He’ll be in camp as a non-roster invitee.

Conley, 32, spent the 2026 season in the Mets’ system. He started 18 of 29 games between Double-A Binghamton and Triple-A Syracuse, working 111 2/3 innings of 5.48 ERA ball. Conley recorded a combined 23.6% strikeout percentage against 10.7% walk rate, though his underlying numbers were much better at Double-A than against Triple-A opposition.

The Mets called Conley up on August 2 this past season. He was on the roster for one game, didn’t pitch, then got designated for assignment.
