Ken Rosenthal, Will Sammon and Katie Woo of The Athletic report that Arizona has done its due diligence on Nippon Professional Baseball star Teruaki Sato, who is available to MLB clubs after being posted by NPB’s Hanshin Tigers.

Sato, 27, is the reigning Triple Crown winner in NPB. He belted 39 home runs this past season (and hit 40 in 2025) while slashing.303/.386/.609 in 614 plate appearances. It’s the most productive season of Sato’s career. He’s steadily improved throughout his 20s in NPB, debuting with a slightly better-than-average line as a 22-year-old rookie back in 2021 but emerging as one of Japan’s best offensive players over the past two seasons.

The D-backs have a known preference for left-handed bats. Sato has been a third baseman in Japan, though he’s dabbled in the outfield corners as well. Third base is spoken for by Nolan Arenado in Arizona — but there’s been talk of Arenado potentially playing some first base. Some scouts around the league feel Sato is athletic enough to shift to the outfield and become a better defender there than he is at the hot corner, however. Arizona has some uncertainty in the outfield, where inexperienced former top prospects Jordan Lawlar and Ryan Waldschmidt are set to take regular reps in conjunction with veterans Corbin Carroll and Lars Nootbaar.

articles.title: Chris Martin Retires
body: Veteran right-hander Chris Martin has retired as a player, per Robert Murray of FanSided. He pitched in 11 different MLB seasons for seven different clubs and also spent a couple of years in Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball.

It’s not a shock that Martin is hanging up his spikes. Back in September of 2024, he said that he was 95% sure that 2025 would be his last season. In the end, the 5% won out, as Martin returned to the Rangers for the 2026 campaign. But he made multiple trips to the injured list this year due to a shoulder impingement and had poor results in the 16 games he did play. He was released in August.

Martin was born and played high school ball in Texas. The Tigers drafted him out of high school in 2004 but he didn’t sign and went to McLennan Community College. The Rockies drafted him in 2005 and went the draft-and-follow route, when that type of strategy was still allowed. Martin then required surgery on a torn labrum in shoulder. The Rockies opted not to sign him. He went undrafted in 2006 and then started his professional career in independent ball.

Due to continued shoulder troubles in indy ball, Martin thought his career was over. He took odd jobs for places like UPS, Lowe’s and an appliance warehouse. A game of catch behind that warehouse led to Martin discovering that his shoulder felt better, so he tried baseball again. After some time in indy ball, he was able to get a minor league deal with the Red Sox in 2011.

articles.title: Dodgers Reportedly Prefer Short-Term Deal In Skubal Bidding
body: The Dodgers are in the mix for free agent Tarik Skubal but the framework of his eventual deal could be very important. Katie Woo of The Athletic reports that their interest would be contingent on Skubal being open to a short-term deal. Jeff Passan of ESPN reports that Skubal has no interest in that kind of arrangement, which would seemingly work against the Dodgers in the bidding.

It’s not really a surprise to hear that the Dodgers are leaning this way. Though they have acquired a number of talented players over the years, they have a clear preference to avoid really long free agent deals. In the past decade, they have only twice gone longer than six years for a free agent, both under special circumstances. One was for Shohei Ohtani, the other for Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Ohtani is a unicorn talent who got a ten-year deal with the Dodgers, with almost all of the money deferred. Yamamoto got a 12-year deal because he was unusually young, coming over from Japan ahead of his age-25 season.

Though it might feel like the Dodgers always sign the top players, they are often happy to let them go elsewhere when the bidding is strong. Juan Soto got 15 years from the Mets. Bryce Harper got 13 years from the Phillies and Trea Turner 11 from that same club. Gerrit Cole and Max Fried got their deals from the Yankees and Dylan Cease ended up with the Blue Jays.

In some of those cases, the Dodgers were involved but would only pounce if the player didn’t find a satisfactory long-term deal and became open to short-term offers. This approach has been described as “hanging around the backboard.”

articles.title: Phillies, Bryan Ramos Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Phillies and free agent infielder Bryan Ramos have agreed to a minor league contract, reports Francys Romero of BeisbolFR.com. The ISE Baseball client will be in camp as a non-roster invitee ahead of the 2027 season.

Ramos, 25 in March, is a former top prospect in the White Sox system who spent the 2026 season with the Orioles organization. He didn’t see the majors, instead suiting up for the Triple-A club in Norfolk all season. The righty-swinging third baseman batted.216/.326/.320 in 100 games and 370 trips to the plate.

That marks three straight seasons with sub-par results at the plate in the upper minors and, more briefly, in occasional big league work. Ramos saw major league time with the 2024-25 ChiSox but totaled only 120 plate appearances. He hit.198/.244/.333 with three homers in that small sample.

While Ramos hasn’t been particularly productive in recent years, he posted big minor league numbers up through the 2023 season. He hit.264/.358/.450 between High-A and Double-A that season but hasn’t produced even average minor league numbers since. Back in the 2023-24 offseason, Baseball America ranked him fourth among White Sox farmhands, calling him a near-MLB-ready option at the hot corner. Even when he struggled through a middling 2024 campaign, Ramos sat 15th among Sox prospects ahead of the 2025 season.

articles.title: Twins To Sign Jose Espada To Minor League Deal
body: The Twins are expected to add right-hander Jose Espada on a minor league agreement, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post. Espada spent last season with the Orioles. He’s represented by The MAS Agency.

Espada, not to be confused with former Astros manager Joe Espada, has made three MLB appearances over the past four years. He’s yet to allow a run across five innings. There was a year in Japan mixed in between his stints in the majors. Espada’s lone MLB outing this season came as the extra man for a doubleheader against the Astros in April. He finished off a blowout win with a scoreless ninth inning.

The majority of Espada’s 2026 campaign was spent in Triple-A Norfolk’s bullpen. He had a solid year, tossing 48 2/3 frames with a 2.77 ERA and just over a strikeout per inning. Espada picked up eight saves with the Tides. The main flaw was a 12.7% walk rate. As tends to be the case with veteran relievers who struggle to get a look in the majors, Espada has had decent strikeout numbers but big walk issues.

Espada flashed a solid three-pitch mix at Norfolk. He led with a slider, which he threw more than 40% of the time. He backed it with a four-seamer that sat around 94 mph. Espada also throws a 90 mph splitter. The arsenal has generated a strong swinging-strike rate in the minors, including a 14.2% mark in 2026.

articles.title: Reds Notes: Sal, Elly, Rotation, Coaching Staff
body: Newly minted National League Rookie of the Year Sal Stewart is a clear building block in Cincinnati, but the Reds have yet to approach Stewart about a contract extension, reports Gordon Wittenmyer of the Cincinnati Enquirer. The Reds locked up budding ace Chase Burns on a seven-year, $105MM contract over the summer. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see them try to work something out with Stewart, though his price tag will probably exceed that of Burns — particularly with some hardware under his belt and a chance to earn some more next week, when Silver Slugger winners are announced.

Stewart, 23 next month, split his 2026 season between the infield corners and batted.263/.330/.457 (112 wRC+) with 32 home runs and an MLB-best 115 runs batted in. He walked at a nine percent clip, fanned at a roughly average 22.1% rate and chipped in 15 stolen bases — albeit in less-than-efficient fashion; he attempted 23 steals on the year (65.2% success rate).

The Reds control Stewart for five more seasons. He won’t reach arbitration until the 2028-29 offseason. Most of the recent pre-arb extensions for players with under two years of service have gone to young stars who play more premium defensive positions than Stewart, who played 948 of his 1311 innings at first base.

articles.title: Astros Name Brad Ausmus Manager
body: The Astros announced that Brad Ausmus has been hired as the club’s manager. Prior to the official announcement, John Granato of ESPN 97.5 Houston reported that Ausmus would be flying to Houston tomorrow to accept the gig, a report confirmed by Brian McTaggart of MLB.com.

The ties between Ausmus and the Astros go way back. During his playing days, he spent ten seasons as an Astro. He suited up for Houston in 1997 and 1998 and then again from 2001 to 2008. In his post-playing days, he has worked as a manager, coach and has done some front office work as well.

Those various post-playing jobs have come with the Padres, Tigers, Angels, Athletics and Yankees but there have been whispers connecting him to the Astros along the way. Astros owner Jim Crane bought the Astros in 2011, after Ausmus had retired, but Crane has a close relationship with Jeff Bagwell. Over the years, Bagwell has been a key advisor to Crane relating to club matters. Bagwell played for the Astros from 1991 to 2005 and therefore shared a clubhouse with Ausmus for many years.

Since Crane bought the team, the Astros have cycled through various managers, hiring Bo Porter, A.J. Hinch, Dusty Baker and Joe Espada. The Ausmus name would often come up when the job was open and he even got connected to the general manager position in Houston a few times but he continued to bounce around to other clubs.

articles.title: Pirates Notes: Keller, Pitching Pursuits, Lineup
body: Pirates righty Mitch Keller saw his season end on Aug. 2 with a teres major strain that wound up being more severe than was originally known. Keller hit the 60-day IL in early August, but it didn’t come out until after the season that he’d suffered a Grade 3 strain, which entailed the teres major muscle completely detaching from the bone. He remarkably did not require surgery.

General manager Ben Cherington said at this week’s GM Meetings that the Bucs have been conducting in-person visits with members of the roster to discuss offseason plans (link via Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette). Keller’s visit revealed the right-hander to be “basically recovered” after more than three months of downtime, per Cherington. He’s resumed throwing from flat ground and is looking at a mostly normal offseason.

Keller said last month that there wasn’t one specific point where he felt the injury take place. He was likely pitching through the injury for some time before it became fully untenable. Keller started the season well, with a 3.64 ERA through his first 11 trips to the mound. Over his next 11 starts, Keller was decimated for a 7.36 ERA. He showed diminished bat-missing ability, worse command, a greater susceptibility to home runs and, eventually, reduced velocity. Keller sat 93.5 mph on his heater for much of the season but dipped to 92.8 mph over his final five starts — including a season-worst 91.9 mph average in his final trip to the mound.

articles.title: MLBTR Podcast: The Nats Extend Jacob Young, Drew Rasmussen’s Future, The Angels’ GM Limbo, And More!
body: The latest episode of the MLB Trade Rumors Podcast is now live on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and wherever you get your podcasts! Make sure you subscribe as well! You can also use the player at this link to listen, if you don’t use Spotify or Apple for podcasts.
This week, host Darragh McDonald is joined by Anthony Franco of MLB Trade Rumors to discuss…

The Nationals signing an extension with Jacob Young (2:40) The Rays hinting that they could keep Drew Rasmussen (7:15) The Angels being stuck with no front office leader in place while they wait for the franchise sale to be approved (14:15) Plus, we answer your questions, including…

If a salary cap is implemented, what happens to the teams that already have big contracts on the books into the long term? (27:25) What are the priorities for the Brewers this winter and can they extend William Contreras? (35:00) How will the Mets construct their pitching staff for the upcoming season? (41:30) Is it possible the Cardinals trade Andre Pallante? (48:25) What is the ideal landing spot for Jasson Domínguez of the Yankees? (51:40) Check out our past episodes!

Offseason Preview – listen here Angels’ Leadership In Flux, The Yankees Keep Boone And Cashman, And The Giants And Cardinals Offseasons – listen here Brewers vs. Rays, Dodgers and Guardians Post-Mortem, And The A’s New Front Office Boss – listen here The podcast intro and outro song “So Long” is provided courtesy of the band Showoff. Check out their Facebook page here!

articles.title: Mariners Interested In Seiya Suzuki, Not Likely To Re-Sign Randy Arozarena Or J.P. Crawford
body: The Mariners appear to be in the process of shuffling up their offense this winter. They’ve already informed longstanding shortstop and clubhouse leader J.P. Crawford that they’re planning to move on, reports Adam Jude of the Seattle Times. Jude and colleague Ryan Divish further report that the M’s won’t pursue a long-term deal with Randy Arozarena but do have interest in fellow free-agent corner outfielder Seiya Suzuki. As is the case with Arozarena, Suzuki received a $23.15MM qualifying offer that he is expected to reject.

Starting with the outfielders, the disparity in interest might seem odd at first glance. Suzuki and Arozarena are both 32-year-old corner outfielders with plus power. They’re coming off similar seasons, and there’s expected to be a good bit of overlap in their markets.

However, while the two have similar track records and platform seasons, there are some underlying metrics that might cause a team to lean toward Suzuki. There’s no clear indication of the Mariners’ reasoning, but Suzuki is coming off the better defensive season and has the sort of plus arm that’s generally needed for a right fielder. Arozarena is more confined to left field; his arm strength on throws from the outfield ranked in just the 32nd percentile of big league outfielders, with an average velocity of 82.1 mph. Suzuki’s sat in the 85th percentile, with an average velocity of 89.9 mph.

articles.title: Will Venable, Pat Murphy Named Managers Of The Year
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced the results of Manager of the Year balloting on Tuesday. White Sox skipper Will Venable won the American League honors, while Milwaukee’s Pat Murphy takes home the National League award for a third straight year.

Venable oversaw the league’s most dramatic turnaround in 2026. After going 60-102 in his first season at the helm, the ChiSox went 84-78 to make the playoffs for the first time since 2021. Chicago squandered their lead in the AL Central to Cleveland in September but secured the #6 seed in the American League.

Chicago succeeded behind one of the younger lineups in baseball. According to Baseball Reference, only three teams (Washington, St. Louis and Miami) had a younger average age among their hitters. They felt some of that youth with one of the higher strikeout rates in the league, but they were fifth in the majors in home runs and overall scoring.

While the Sox have a lot of young talent in the lineup, Venable and his staff had to work around an overall lack of pitching depth. That’s especially true in the rotation, where Sean Burke and Anthony Kay were their only sources of consistency down the stretch. The Sox leaned heavily on openers and multi-inning relievers to compensate for the lack of starting pitching; no team got fewer innings out of their “starters” than Chicago’s 674 2/3 frames.

articles.title: Rangers Planning To Explore Corey Seager Trades
body: The Rangers plan to asses the trade market for shortstop Corey Seager at the general managers’ meetings in Las Vegas, per reports from Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic and Evan Grant of The Dallas Morning News.

It’s a notable development but not really a shocking one. Seager was in some trade rumors around the deadline a few months ago. He ultimately stayed put but it’s not a shock to see the Rangers circle back to the possibility. The club appears to have limited financial flexibility while having big commitments on the books to Seager, Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi and Brandon Nimmo.

Moving one or more of those contracts off the books could allow the club some more maneuverability in the offseason. With Seager in particular, there’s an added incentive to pursue a trade because Texas may have an in-house replacement ready to go. Sebastian Walcott is a consensus top-15 prospect in the league. An internal brace surgery on his elbow in February slowed him down in 2026 but he got back into the lineup by July and hit well at the Double-A level. He got up to Triple-A for two games in September. A big league debut in 2027 is distinctly possible.

articles.title: Bob Boone Passes Away
body: Longtime MLB catcher/manager Bob Boone passed away yesterday at 78, according to a family announcement. Boone was a baseball lifer who spent over five decades in the game in various capacities. He was also part of a three-generation family of big leaguers, the son of a 13-year MLB veteran and father of two All-Stars.

Bob Boone was born in 1947, at a time when his father Ray Boone was playing in the Cleveland farm system. Ray would reach the majors a year later and had a couple All-Star selections and a few down ballot MVP seasons among a career that spanned until 1960. While Ray Boone was a multi-positional infielder, Bob moved behind the plate after being drafted by the Phillies in the sixth round in 1969.

Boone quickly took to the position and became one of the best defensive catchers of his era. He reached the majors in 1972 and would spend a decade as Philadelphia’s starting catcher. Boone was rarely a huge offensive threat, though he had a trio of decent years at the plate in the late 1970s. He was a standout defender who led MLB with 54 runners caught stealing in his first full season. Boone would do so two more times in his career and earned his first Gold Glove award in 1978. He appeared in three All-Star games over his time in Philadelphia, a run that saw the team earn five playoff berths between 1976-81.

articles.title: Angels To Begin Preliminary Meetings With GM Candidates
body: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, the Angels’ incoming ownership group, will conduct informal meetings with candidates for their general manager job at this week’s GM Meetings. Interim GM John Mozeliak relayed the update to Jeff Fletcher of The Orange County Register on Monday.

While this marks a preliminary start to the GM search, the organization remains in a holding pattern. They’re awaiting approval of the franchise sale from Arte Moreno to KSE from Major League Baseball. Mozeliak said last week that the Angels weren’t likely to hire a full-time GM until MLB approves the sale, which he reiterated this evening.

Mozeliak remains in charge of the front office until December. He could handle the team’s offseason business right up to the inevitable December 2 lockout. It’s an odd spot for the organization, as they’d surely prefer for their new ownership group and permanent front office to handle any significant moves. That could force them to miss out on free agent and trade opportunities over the next few weeks. The market is expected to move more quickly than usual as teams try to get business done before the transaction freeze.

articles.title: Best Fits For A Ketel Marte Trade
body: Teams are expected to lay the foundation for their offseason trade talks as the GM Meetings get underway. Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte is one of the biggest names available. The Snakes have more or less acknowledged that they’ll listen to offers on the three-time All-Star, who has clearly frustrated many within the organization by failing to show up for certain games over the years.

Marte has full control over his destiny, as he secured no-trade protection by reaching 10 years of service time (the last five of which have come in Arizona). He’s signed for another five years at a total of $87.5MM, covering ages 33-37. Marte is only making a $12MM salary next year, though, and $3MM of that is deferred.

That’s a fine salary even if he only repeats his league average.249/.316/.432 showing this year. If he bounces back some or all of the way to the player he was before, arguably the best second baseman in the sport, it’s a bargain for the on-field production. There’ll surely be teams that have trepidations about Marte’s work habits, and some might take him off their target list altogether, but the D-Backs should get some kind of interest given the star offensive upside he’s shown at his best.
Let’s run through the league to determine which teams should be most motivated to pull Marte from the desert.

articles.title: Sal Stewart Wins NL Rookie Of The Year, Earns PPI Pick For Reds
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday evening that Reds first baseman Sal Stewart has won the National League Rookie of the Year award. The win earns Cincinnati a pick after the first round of the 2027 draft via the Prospect Promotion Incentive.

Stewart received 20 of 30 first-place votes and was the only player in the NL field to land in the top five on every ballot. He beat out Mets outfielder Carson Benge and Cardinals middle infielder JJ Wetherholt for the honors. Benge received seven first-place votes and was on all but two ballots overall, leading to the runner-up finish. Wetherholt, who finished in third, received the three other first-place votes.

Nolan McLean, TJ Rumfield, and Logan Henderson were the other players to receive one or more votes in the top three. They respectively finished fourth, fifth and sixth in the voting. Bryce Eldridge, Didier Fuentes, and A.J. Ewing were the only other players to appear on ballots (no higher than fifth in their cases).

articles.title: Kevin McGonigle Wins AL Rookie Of The Year, Earns PPI Pick For Tigers
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced Monday evening that Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle has won the AL Rookie of the Year award. McGonigle’s win earns Detroit a pick after the first round of the 2027 draft via the Prospect Promotion Incentive.

McGonigle received 28 of 30 first-place votes. Guardians left-hander Parker Messick earned the other two first-place votes en route to the runner-up finish. Messick is also a top three finisher for the Cy Young award, which means he earned Cleveland a PPI pick in 2027. McGonigle finished second for the two voters who had Messick in the top spot. Messick received 25 second-place votes, placed third on two ballots, and landed fourth for one voter.

Red Sox southpaw Payton Tolle led a crowded field for the third-place finish. Munetaka Murakami, Carter Jensen, Chase DeLauter, Kazuma Okamoto, Tristan Peters, Sam Antonacci, Travis Bazzana, Walbert Ureña, Dylan Beavers and Henry Bolte all appeared in the top five on at least one ballot.

McGonigle’s runaway win doesn’t come as much surprise even in a very strong field. The 22-year-old infielder, who entered the season as the consensus #2 prospect in baseball behind Pittsburgh’s Konnor Griffin, hit the ground running. He had a four-hit performance in his debut and never really looked back. McGonigle batted.278/.376/.430 across 707 plate appearances, entrenching himself in the top third of A.J. Hinch’s lineup by the second week of the season. He walked at an excellent 13.4% clip against a modest 14.1% strikeout rate.

articles.title: Cardinals, JoJo Romero Have Mutual Interest In Reunion
body: 6:17pm: Jeff Jones of The Belleville News-Democrat reports that there’s interest on both sides in a reunion.

11:13am: After shipping him to Milwaukee at the trade deadline, the Cardinals have interest in bringing back left-hander JoJo Romero, reports Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. Romero was a crucial cog in a Brewers’ bullpen that dominated en route to a title.

St. Louis closed the 2025 season with an unsettled relief corps after Ryan Helsley and Phil Maton were traded away. Romero filled in at closer at times to close the year and seemed to have a shot to take the job in 2026. Instead, Riley O’Brien emerged as an All-Star stopper. That allowed Romero to stay in his high-leverage lefty role. He racked up 20 holds in 44 appearances.

With free agency looming, the Cardinals sent Romero and Dustin May to the Brewers for outfield prospects Alexander Frias and Josiah Ragsdale. The swap worked out well for both sides. The addition of Romero gave manager Pat Murphy another southpaw alongside Aaron Ashby in the later innings. Romero was scored upon in just one of seven playoff outings. He picked up wins over the Dodgers in Games 2 and 4 of the NLCS.

St. Louis recouped a pair of young outfielders who immediately ranked among their better hitting prospects. MLB Pipeline slotted Frias at No. 5 and Ragsdale at No. 11 in the system. Eric Longenhagen and Brendan Gawlowski of FanGraphs ranked Frias as the third-best prospect moved at the deadline.
[Related: 2026-27 Offseason Outlook — St. Louis Cardinals]

articles.title: Dipoto: Mariners Eyeing Bullpen Upgrades, At Least One Bat
body: With Jason Kanzler installed as the new skipper out in Seattle, the Mariners have one piece of offseason business checked off the list. There will still be a handful of coaching hires to sort out, but with the GM Meetings underway in Las Vegas, the focus will also turn to upgrading roster. President of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto chatted with Teren Kowatsch of Mariners Roundtable following last week’s Kanzler introduction and gave a relatively candid assessment of his group’s targets.

“This year’s bullpen market is pretty appealing,” said Dipoto. “There’s a lot of guys out there we feel like could help us. We’ve already identified who they might be. Whether we can land them or not is a different story. But, we’re looking to add to our bullpen. We’re looking for one, maybe two more bats. And we’d like to add a veteran infield presence. Whether that is part of the bats or just a presence is something entirely different.”

articles.title: Latest On Emilio Pagán
body: Right-hander Emilio Pagán recently turned down a $10MM player option with the Reds, thus becoming a free agent. Gordon Wittenmyer of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports that Pagán already has a busy market and would prefer to sign before the lockout, so perhaps he will have a deal in place in the next few weeks.

Pagán turns 36 in May but it’s not surprising that he has a robust market. His 2026 season was okay if you look at the whole thing but he finished on quite a heater. On the whole, he tossed 42 2/3 innings with a 3.38 earned run average. He posted a 6.43 ERA through 14 innings before a hamstring strain put him on the injured list in May. He came off the IL in June and shoved through the rest of the season with a 1.88 ERA in 28 2/3 innings. He struck out 30.4% of opponents and only gave out walks at a 4.5% clip, both excellent figures.

After that showing, Pagán left $10MM on the table in search of more. His earning power is limited by his age but beating that number should be doable. MLBTR predicted Pagán to secure a two-year, $20MM deal this winter.

It wouldn’t be a shock if Pagán’s next deal was with the Reds, as his last two deals were with Cincinnati. Going into the 2024 season, the Reds gave him a two-year, $16MM deal, with the second year being a player option. It was a bit of a surprising pairing, as Pagán’s main issue in his career has been the long ball and Great American Ball Park is fairly hitter-friendly in that regard.

articles.title: Marlins Interested In Adrian Morejon, Alex Vesia, Sean Newcomb
body: A recent report from the Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson indicated that the Marlins were looking for upgrades to the rotation, bullpen, and at least one of the corner infield or outfield situations. Adding some further context, Kevin Barral of Fish On First writes that the team would prefer to bring in a right-handed bat and left-handed pitchers. This makes sense given that the Marlins already have a good number of lefty hitters, and an overload of right-handed pitching. Cade Gibson and prospect Dax Fulton are the only healthy southpaws on the 40-man roster, as Robby Snelling and Andrew Nardi (a non-tender candidate) are recovering from internal brace surgeries.

To this end, Barral lists Adrian Morejon, Alex Vesia, and Sean Newcomb as left-handed bullpen targets on Miami’s wishlist. The trio in general covers a broad range of possibilities for the Marlins’ winter shopping, and while Morejon is in a tier by himself, Barral notes that Vesia is favored over Newcomb.

Morejon landing with the Marlins would count as a big surprise, as it would surely require owner Bruce Sherman to make his biggest free agent expenditure since buying the team over nine years ago. Avisail Garcia’s four-year, $53MM contract represents the biggest free agent deal of the Sherman era. Over the three seasons Peter Bendix has been Miami’s president of baseball operations, Pete Fairbanks’ one-year, $13MM deal from last winter represents the club’s high-water mark in free agent spending.

articles.title: Guardians Sign Antoine Kelly To Minor League Deal
body: The Guardians announced Monday that they’ve signed left-hander Antoine Kelly to a minor league contract and invited him to major league spring training. The Bledsoe Agency client made his big league debut with the Cubs this past season.

Kelly, not to be confused with Pirates left-handed pitching prospect Antwone Kelly, pitched just 1 1/3 innings in his first call the majors. The 26-year-old (27 in December) held the Yankees scoreless in that one-off appearance. Kelly spent the remainder of the 2026 season pitching with the Triple-A affiliates for the Cubs and Dodgers, combining for 50 2/3 innings with a 4.62 ERA, 23.7% strikeout rate and sky-high 16.7% walk rate.

That gives Kelly parts of four seasons at the Triple-A level. He hasn’t fared well there, logging a 5.82 ERA in 120 2/3 innings. Kelly’s 23.5% strikeout rate in that time is respectable, but he’s been his own worst enemy far too often, evidenced by a bloated 16.6% walk rate.

It’s not the most alluring track record, but Kelly is a former second-round pick (No. 65 overall to the Brewers in 2019) who has previously drawn praise for a dominant fastball/slider pairing that could make him an elite reliever if he could even get his command up from its currently dismal levels to merely below-average.

articles.title: Looking For A Match In A Steven Kwan Trade
body: “As we sit here today, we’re expecting Steven Kwan to be a big part of a contending team next year,” Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti told reporters during the team’s season wrap-up press conference after the ALCS. This was something less than a confirmation that Kwan will be back with the Guards in 2027, and it could indeed be that Kwan’s “contending team” plays somewhere other than Cleveland.

The Guardians have made a habit of winning without much offense in recent years, and the club’s collective 97 wRC+ (ranking 22nd in baseball) in 2026 was no exception. Trading one of their most dependable hitters therefore doesn’t make too much sense on paper for the Guardians, especially when the outfield in particular has been a weak link, and Kwan adds a ton of defensive value beyond his contributions at the plate.

That said, trading an increasingly expensive veteran a year or two prior to free agency has long been a favored tactic of the Guardians’ front office (not to mention other consistently small-market teams like the Brewers or Rays). Kwan is projected to earn $11.3MM in his final season of arbitration eligibility, before he is slated to hit the open market next winter. Unless Kwan is open to a very team-friendly extension a la Jose Ramirez, chances are Kwan will be playing for another team by 2028 anyway, so trading him now would allow Cleveland to again restock the roster for both 2027 and the future.

articles.title: Tigers Scouted Teruaki Sato, Kaima Taira; Showed Past Interest In Shota Imanaga
body: The Tigers are among the many MLB teams who have scouted Teruaki Sato and Kaima Taira, Evan Petzold reports in a YouTube video exploring several potential targets for the Tigers this winter. Petzold notes Shota Imanaga as a possible rotation addition, with the added detail that Imanaga drew interest from Detroit when the left-hander made his own jump from Japan to the majors during the 2023-24 offseason.

Framber Valdez’s three-year, $115MM contract (which has an opt-out after the 2027 season) is far and away the largest free agent deal the Tigers have completed under president of baseball operations Scott Harris. Detroit’s two-year, $35MM deal with Jack Flaherty from the 2024-25 offseason is second on that list, and while the Tigers have explored larger splurges on such players as Alex Bregman, Harris has been pretty steadfast in his approach of limiting the club’s forays into the open market.

MLB Trade Rumors projects Sato for a five-year, $80MM deal this winter, Taira for a four-year, $72MM deal (with at least one opt-out), and Imanaga for two years and $40MM. Estimates for players coming from NPB to MLB are sometimes particularly difficult to predict, but if these projections hold, Imanaga might be the cleanest financial fit for a Detroit club that is wary of free agent spending. If Imanaga is still on the Tigers’ radar as a potential add as he enters his age-33 season, the Tigers have more data on what to expect based on the southpaw’s three years in the Show.

articles.title: Emilio Pagán Keeps Getting It Done
body: Right-handed reliever Emilio Pagán is a free agent after declining his $10MM player option with the Reds. We ranked him at No. 35 on our list of the Top 50 Free Agents, and two of MLBTR’s three full-time writers expect him to rejoin the Reds on a new deal. As noted in that article, Pagán’s extreme fly ball tendencies have made him a curious fit at the hitter-friendly Great American Ball Park, but he somehow keeps getting it done.

Since the 2024 season, 190 pitchers have thrown at least 100 innings out of the bullpen. Pagán carries a 28.4% strikeout rate and 7.4% walk rate in that time, tying the recently retired Kirby Yates for 23rd with a 21.0% K-BB rate. The league average in that three-year span is just under 14%. From a strikeout and walk perspective, Pagán is right there in the second-tier of quality relievers, even though his run prevention numbers keep him from elite status.

The biggest drawback is Pagán’s propensity for giving up home runs. In the last three years, he’s given up 23 homers in 147 1/3 innings (not counting a two-inning opener appearance in 2024). He’s allowed 1.40 home runs per nine innings, ranking 17th-worst in the 190-reliever group. Unsurprisingly, Pagán is also one of the worst in the group at keeping the ball on the ground. Only six relievers on that list have a worse ground ball rate since 2024 than Pagán’s 28.3%. For comparison, the league average ground ball rate in 2026 was 41.6%.

articles.title: Ryan O’Hearn’s Adjustments In Pittsburgh
body: The Pirates overhauled their offense last season. Brandon Lowe arrived via trade. Ryan O’Hearn and Marcell Ozuna came aboard through free agency. Konnor Griffin was promoted a week into the season.

The moves came with varying degrees of success, but the end result was an offense that ranked sixth in scoring, sixth in OPS, and ninth in SLG. Those numbers looked a lot better until injuries thinned out the lineup in the summer.

O’Hearn was a key cog in the middle of the order. He signed a modest two-year, $29MM deal after a strong season split between the Orioles and Padres. O’Hearn was an above-average bat for the fourth straight season, finishing with a 109 wRC+. He slashed.265/.330/.440 over 451 plate appearances. A severe quad injury derailed his season in August.

After five unremarkable seasons in Kansas City, O’Hearn broke through as a viable big-league bat in 2023 with Baltimore. He cut down the strikeouts, improved his barrel rate, and hit the ball hard at an elite rate. O’Hearn continued to produce even as he was given more opportunities against same-handed pitching. He settled in as a reliable contributor who didn’t have the typical power of a first baseman/corner outfielder but had a higher batting average ceiling.

The 2026 campaign looked different for O’Hearn. His strikeout rate ticked back up to 22%. He didn’t barrel the ball as frequently, but hit a career-high 18 home runs. O’Hearn hit.265 and posted a.247 expected batting average. It’s not a bad profile, but it wasn’t what we’ve seen in recent seasons.

articles.title: Details On Braves’ Rotation Search
body: The Braves’ rotation overcame several injuries to post very solid numbers for most of the season, though a lack of depth caught up to the team in the playoffs, as Chris Sale and deadline pickup Tyler Mahle were the only pitchers trusted to operate as true starters. With Mahle and Martin Perez now free agents and questions about health and consistency still swirling over several other Atlanta starters, it’s no surprise that the Braves are widely expected to seek out rotation help this winter.

Gabriel Burns of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution looks at the free agent market to see how many starters are plausible fits for the Braves, and adds a couple of interesting details about two potential targets. Nick Pivetta has drawn interest from the team “in [the] past, but there are currently concerns about his elbow,” Burns writes. The club is also wary of Casey Mize’s injury, which is part of the reason Atlanta held off making a full-fledged push for Mize this past summer. As Burns puts it, “t he Braves were prominently linked to Mize at the trade deadline, though that interest was overstated.”

articles.title: Tigers Outright Yilber Díaz
body: The Tigers sent right-hander Yilber Díaz outright to Triple-A Toledo, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. Detroit designated him for assignment on Monday when they dropped their offseason roster count to 40.

Díaz was claimed off waivers from Arizona in late June. He spent most of the remaining season on optional assignment with Toledo, though he made a couple brief appearances on the big league roster. Díaz pitched four times as a Tiger, allowing four runs across 5 1/3 innings. He’s thrown 37 1/3 big league frames over parts of three seasons, posting a 6.27 earned run average. Díaz has a modest 15.5% strikeout rate against a lofty 11.9% walk percentage at the MLB level.

The Venezuelan-born Díaz was viewed as one of the better starting pitching prospects in a thin Arizona farm system a couple years ago. He has a power arsenal but was held back as a starter by a lack of a viable changeup and subpar command. The D-Backs moved him to the bullpen in 2025. Díaz has posted big strikeout numbers in the minors but still isn’t throwing enough strikes to stick in the majors, even in a middle relief capacity. He worked 54 innings of 3.50 ERA ball with a 28% strikeout rate and an untenable 15% walk percentage in Triple-A this year.

This is the first time that Díaz has cleared waivers in his career. He’ll remain in the Detroit organization and should receive a non-roster invite to Spring Training. Díaz has exhausted his minor league option years, which limits the flexibility to shuffle him back and forth between Triple-A moving forward.

articles.title: Corbin Carroll Undergoes Elbow Surgery; Expects Mostly Normal Offseason
body: Diamondbacks outfielder Corbin Carroll tells Nick Piecoro of the Arizona Republic that he recently underwent elbow surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow. The procedure used the NanoNeedle, the same technology used in Tarik Skubal’s surgery earlier this year. Carroll planned to start swinging in November. That offseason work will now be delayed but only by two weeks.

Carroll tells Piecoro that he felt some discomfort in that right elbow, which is his non-throwing arm, during the season. That discomfort worsened lately, which eventually led to this surgery. The NanoNeedle is a fairly new technology. In essence, it’s smaller than other arthroscopes, which hopefully leads to smaller incision and therefore less pain, swelling and recovery time. In Skubal’s case, it seemed to work, as he returned in about six weeks from a procedure that would usually take a few months.

With Carroll, it should be even less significant. As mentioned, this surgery was performed on his non-throwing arm. Also, position players can usually return from elbow surgeries quicker than pitchers. Carroll’s offseason swinging program was set to start in November but will now be pushed by a few weeks into December. Apart from that, it will hopefully be a normal winter for Carroll.

articles.title: Guardians Claim José Tena
body: The Guardians have claimed infielder José Tena off waivers from the Nationals, per a team announcement. He’d been designated for assignment earlier in the week. Tena was originally a Cleveland signee as an amateur out of the Dominican Republic but was traded to the Nats back in the 2024 deadline deal that brought outfielder Lane Thomas to the Guardians.

Now 25 years old, Tena once ranked as one of the top prospects in Cleveland’s system. He sat ninth in their system at MLB.com ahead of the 2022 campaign and 11th at Baseball America’s rankings. He’s a lefty-swinging infielder who’s experienced at every spot on the dirt to the left of first base, though he’s far better suited at second and third than he is at shortstop.

Tena has appeared in parts of four major league seasons between Washington and Cleveland. He’s taken 659 plate appearances in the bigs and turned in a.240/.303/.358 batting line — 17% worse than average, by measure of wRC+.

It’s not an especially encouraging line, particularly when juxtaposed with Tena’s career 27.5% strikeout rate (including a 31.3% mark in a career-high 288 plate appearances this past season). However, he has good bat speed, makes plenty of hard contact and boasts a stout.295/.362/.486 batting line in nearly 700 career plate appearances at the Triple-A level. There’s above-average raw power in Tena’s bat, but his penchant for whiffs has undercut his ability to drive the ball.

articles.title: Cardinals Promote Rob Cerfolio To General Manager
body: 9:40am: The Cardinals have formally announced Cerfolio’s promotion.

8:40am: The Cardinals are promoting assistant general manager Rob Cerfolio to the title of general manager, reports Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. He’ll serve as the No. 2 executive under president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom.

Cerfolio, 34, joined the Cardinals two offseasons ago. He’d previously been the Guardians’ director of player development and was given the title of AGM with a focus on player development and performance. He’s held that role for the past two seasons and now climbs another rung on the ladder.

It’s perhaps no coincidence that Cerfolio receives this title bump (and presumably pay increase) after his name emerged as a candidate in the Athletics’ GM search. He’s one of several known candidates that interviewed, joining Brewers assistant GM Matt Kleine and, of course, Red Sox assistant GM Taylor Smith, who ultimately landed the president of baseball operations title with the A’s. Cerfolio’s promotion to the GM post in St. Louis means that in order to be hired away by another organization in the future, he’d likely need to be offered a new team’s president of baseball ops title himself.

articles.title: Poll: Will Jake Bauers Accept The Qualifying Offer?
body: Earlier this week, eight players received a qualifying offer worth $23.15MM. Arguably, Jake Bauers was the most surprising name on the list. Whether he will accept that QO or not is one of the most interesting stories of the early offseason. Arguments can be made in either direction.

Two years ago, Bauers had one foot out the door of baseball. From 2018 to 2024, he bounced around the league, playing for the Rays, Guardians, Mariners, Yankees and Brewers. Teams clearly saw the talent but Bauers couldn’t put it all together. After the 2024 season, he had a career line of.208/.302/.361. That wasn’t in a small sample. He had stepped to the plate 1,744 times at that point.

Going into 2025, Bauers was projected by MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz for an arbitration salary of $2.3MM. The Brewers didn’t want to pay him that, so they put him on waivers. The other 29 clubs passed. Bauers became a free agent. He recently told Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that he was planning to retire at that time while his wife would return to teaching, but then she became pregnant, so Bauers decided to keep playing. He returned to the Brewers on a minor league deal.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal Rumors: Mets, Dodgers, Cubs
body: Free agency opened to all 30 teams on Monday evening, officially kicking off the bidding for Tarik Skubal. The first few days of the offseason have been characteristically slow throughout the entire market, but there’s been early speculation about the landing spot for the top free agent.

Much of the attention has unsurprisingly focused on the Mets and Dodgers, generally viewed as the two likeliest Skubal destinations. Jon Heyman of The New York Post wrote on Wednesday that the Mets are indeed interested in making a run, though he cautioned they haven’t yet determined how far they’re willing to go in the bidding two years into the record-setting Juan Soto contract.

New York also has needs at the back of the bullpen and around their infield. The Dodgers are more well set up for luxury buys. They’ll need to re-sign or replace a few leverage relievers (Evan Phillips, Alex Vesia, Blake Treinen and Kris Bubic) and could poke around the second base market for an upgrade on Tommy Edman and Alex Freeland. They’re much better positioned than the Mets in prioritizing a handful of targets rather than addressing various roster needs.

articles.title: Rays, Levi Stoudt Agree To Minor League Deal
body: The Rays are in agreement with right-hander Levi Stoudt on a minor league contract with a non-roster invite to Spring Training, reports Marc Topkin of The Tampa Bay Times. Topkin also reported this week that Tampa Bay was re-signing righty Kodi Whitley with a camp invite.

Stoudt, who’ll be 29 next month, has four games of major league experience. Those came with the 2023 Reds, for whom he tossed 10 1/3 innings of 11-run ball. Stoudt subsequently spent time in the Baltimore organization and was on a minor league contract with the Phillies for 2026. He was out to a great start to the season, combining for 22 2/3 frames without an earned run between the top two minor league levels. There’s a decent chance he’d have earned himself a look in the Philadelphia bullpen had he not suffered an elbow injury in June that ended his season.

A third-round pick by the Mariners in 2019, Stoudt got some prospect attention early in his career on the strength of a mid-90s fastball and good control. He averaged 96 mph on his fastball in Triple-A this year but threw his mid-80s slider at a massive 85% clip. The pre-injury results were encouraging, as Stoudt struck out 11 of 39 Triple-A opponents while allowing a total of six baserunners in 11 innings.

articles.title: Braves To Hire Perry Minasian As Senior Advisor
body: The Braves are bringing Perry Minasian back to their front office, reports Bob Nightengale of USA Today. Jesús Cano of The Athletic reports that Minasian will be a senior advisor in amateur scouting.

That’s the same role that Dana Brown took when he rejoined the Braves’ front office last week. Minasian and Brown were both high-ranking Atlanta staffers — Brown as vice president of scouting, Minasian as assistant general manager — before getting opportunities to run AL West rivals. The Angels hired Minasian as their GM over the 2020-21 offseason; Brown got the same job with the Astros three years later.

Both executives were dismissed by their former clubs within a couple months of one another over the summer. The Angels fired Minasian in late June and hired John Mozeliak on an interim basis. Houston moved on from Brown in August, and while the team technically announced it as a mutual parting of ways, owner Jim Crane has made clear it was essentially a unilateral decision.

Brown and Minasian are experienced talent evaluators who clearly still have the trust of longtime Atlanta president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos. Minasian also had scouting experience with the Blue Jays when Anthopoulos was running the Toronto front office.

articles.title: Mets To Hire Johnny Washington As Co-Hitting Coach
body: The Mets are hiring Johnny Washington as a co-hitting coach, reports Joel Sherman of The New York Post. He was working for Atlanta in 2026 as minor league hitting coordinator.

Washington, 42, was drafted by the Rangers in 2003. He played in that club’s minor league system through 2006 but never played in the majors. He bounced around for a bit, playing some independent and minor league ball, with his last official game action coming in 2009.

He pivoted to coaching after that. He worked in the minors for the Dodgers and Padres. The latter club promoted him to first base coach on the big league staff for the 2017 season. He was named hitting coach for the 2019 campaign. He spent the 2021 season as the hitting coach for the Hanwha Eagles in the KBO. He returned to MLB in 2022, working as assistant hitting coach for the Cubs. He then served as hitting coach for the Angels in 2024 and 2025 before joining Atlanta this year.

The Mets fired manager Carlos Mendoza during the 2026 season. Andy Green replaced him on an interim basis. In September, the Mets and Green announced an extension that would keep him around for the next three seasons. Washington and Green overlapped in San Diego for a time, as Green was the manager of the Padres from 2016 to 2019.

articles.title: MLBTR Podcast: Offseason Preview
body: The latest episode of the MLB Trade Rumors Podcast is now live on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and wherever you get your podcasts! Make sure you subscribe as well! You can also use the player at this link to listen, if you don’t use Spotify or Apple for podcasts.
This week, host Darragh McDonald is joined by Steve Adams and Anthony Franco of MLB Trade Rumors to discuss…

The Brewers winning the World Series (2:35) The Rays going into the offseason after winning the American League pennant (recorded prior to Erik Neader’s comments on Drew Rasmussen) (14:40) MLBTR’s list of the Top 50 Free Agents for the offseason (25:25) Jazz Chisholm Jr. (30:35) MLBTR’s list of the Top 40 Trade Candidates for the offseason (37:45) The Rangers potentially being active on the trade market (39:30) The Orioles potentially being active on the trade market (45:25) Rafael Devers of the Giants being a trade candidate (51:45) Tarik Skubal (57:40) Jake Bauers (1:16:00) Ryan Jeffers (1:28:25) Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips (1:41:30) Tyler Mahle (1:49:05) Check out our past episodes!

Angels’ Leadership In Flux, The Yankees Keep Boone And Cashman, And The Giants And Cardinals Offseasons – listen here Brewers vs. Rays, Dodgers and Guardians Post-Mortem, And The A’s New Front Office Boss – listen here Playoff Storylines And The State Of The White Sox, Yankees, Padres, And Braves – listen here The podcast intro and outro song “So Long” is provided courtesy of the band Showoff. Check out their Facebook page here!

articles.title: Marlins Open To Corner Infield/Outfield Addition
body: The Marlins have a wide array of potential targets as the offseason gets underway. Barry Jackson of The Miami Herald reports that the Fish are seeking at least one external addition to both the rotation and the bullpen. According to Jackson, they’re also open to bringing in an everyday position player at either a corner infield or outfield spot.

That leaves the front office with ample roster flexibility, a luxury of being well-positioned up the middle already. Miami has defensive stalwart Joe Mack behind the plate and a strong middle infield duo of Otto Lopez and Xavier Edwards. They’re well positioned long term in center field with Jakob Marsee as well, though they could look for a stopgap there because Marsee required postseason internal brace surgery. That came with a six-month recovery window that makes him doubtful for Opening Day if the season begins on time.

Miami was a league average offensive team in 2026. They ranked 18th in scoring, 23rd in home runs, and 16th in slugging percentage. They were in the top ten in batting average and on-base percentage but were a bit light in terms of true impact bats. It’s not surprising they’re open to an offensive acquisition in a corner, where most of their players have positional flexibility.

Kyle Stowers was a full-time first baseman in the second half. He has an outfield background and could move back there if the Fish brought in a first baseman. Javier Sanoja is the projected starter at third base. That looked like the offense’s biggest question mark for a while, but he finished the season on a tear.

articles.title: Angels Yet To Begin Interviewing GM Candidates While Awaiting Sale Approval
body: The Angels have yet to start interviewing candidates for their top position in baseball operations, interim general manager John Mozeliak tells reporters (including Jeff Fletcher of The Orange County Register). Mozeliak, who’s under contract through December, remains in charge of the front office as the offseason gets underway.

It’s a less than ideal spot that’s a product of the Angels’ pending sale. Arte Moreno agreed to sell the franchise to Stan Kroenke’s group (officially known as Kroenke Sports & Entertainment) on September 1 at a $4 billion franchise valuation. That’s awaiting official approval from the other 29 owners, however. The timing on that varies but frequently takes a few months. The most recently approved franchise sale (Padres) was agreed upon in mid-April and not finalized until August 17.

Moreno fired former GM Perry Minasian and tabbed Mozeliak on an interim basis on June 26. They gave Mozeliak the autonomy to trade controllable starter José Soriano to Toronto for a package led by shortstop prospect Arjun Nimmala. However, the ownership change seemingly ensured that Mozeliak would not hold the GM role for the long term. He told reporters a few weeks ago that he’s not a candidate for the full-time job and intended to step away once a new hire was in place. The Angels also moved on from skipper Kurt Suzuki.

articles.title: Reds Announce Joe Torres As Pitching Coach
body: The Reds announced that Joe Torres has been hired as their new pitching coach. He has previously been serving as the assistant pitching coach with the Guardians. He will replace Derek Johnson, who was the previous pitching coach in Cincinnati.

Cincinnati hired Johnson in October of 2018 and he was still officially on the job in 2026. However, he took a personal leave of absence in June and was away from the club for the final months of the season. The Reds announced last month that Johnson would not be returning.

Reds manager Terry Francona was hired in October of 2024 and inherited Johnson. To fill the vacancy, Francona has turned to his old staff. Francona was the skipper in Cleveland from 2013 to 2023. Torres was in the organization for much of that span. He joined the big league staff as assistant pitching coach in January of 2022, replacing Ruben Niebla, who left to become pitching coach in San Diego. Torres was working in Cleveland’s minor league system for five years prior to that, so he and Francona surely crossed paths often.

It always tough to connect a club’s on-field results to one specific coach but the Guardians organization is one with a strong reputation for pitching development. In 2026, Gavin Williams seemingly emerged as a true ace. Parker Messick is a Rookie of the Year finalist after his breakout season. Cade Smith’s first year as a full-time closer resulted in 41 saves and a 1.95 earned run average.

articles.title: Athletics Hire Brewers’ Cam Castro As General Manager
body: 12:03 pm CT: The A’s have officially announced the hiring of Castro.

10:31 am CT: The Athletics are hiring Brewers senior vice president of player development and performance Cam Castro as their new general manager, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. He’ll serve as the No. 2 executive under newly hired president of baseball operations Taylor Smith.

Castro, who’d been with the Brewers organization since 2019, has an extensive background in pitching development. He worked at Driveline more than a decade ago and was the head baseball coach for Division-II Lake Erie College before being hired by Milwaukee as a minor league pitching coach. He quickly climbed the ladder in the Brewers organization, ascending to minor league pitching coordinator, then director of pitching development and eventually vice president of player development, before being promoted to his most recent title following the 2024 season.

Pitching development has been an Achilles heel for the A’s for more than a decade. They’ve cultivated an impressive core of largely homegrown bats; Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, Jacob Wilson, Henry Bolte and Zack Gelof were all Athletics draftees. Catcher Shea Langeliers was a Braves pick but was traded to the A’s before ever making his big league debut. It’s a strong group of bats that give the soon-to-be Las Vegas A’s a nice foundation.

articles.title: Cardinals To Hire Joel McKeithan As Hitting Coach
body: The Cardinals are set to hire White Sox assistant hitting coach Joel McKeithan as their new hitting coach, Robert Murray of Fansided reports. He’ll take over for Brant Brown, who spent the past two seasons as hitting coach in St. Louis but was dismissed last month.

The 35-year-old McKeithan spent the past two seasons as an assistant hitting coach with the White Sox. He’d previously been both an assistant hitting coach and lead hitting coach with the Reds. McKeithan has also worked as a minor league hitting coach in both the Phillies and Tigers organizations.

White Sox hitters mashed 211 homers and walked at a 9.5% clip in 2026. Both marks were the fifth-best in baseball. On the whole, they posted a.236/.320/.406 batting line that was about 4% better than average, by measure of wRC+. The Cards hit.239/.313/.378 as a team, giving them the fifth-worst wRC+ (93) in the sport. They hit the seventh-fewest home runs in MLB (167) and tied with the Twins for the fifth-worst walk rate (8.3%). Obviously, any successes and failures of a team are attributable to far more than just one individual coach, but it’s still not a surprise to see the Cardinals draw their new top hitting instructor from an organization that had a more productive all-around year.

To this point, Brown has been the only coach dismissed from manager Oli Marmol’s staff. Third base coach Pop Warner and outfield/baserunning coach Jon Jay were on expiring contracts, but Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported last month that both are expected back for the 2027 season.

articles.title: Neander: Rays Have “Every Intention Right Now” Of Holding Drew Rasmussen
body: The Rays’ biggest question this offseason is whether to trade ace Drew Rasmussen. Tampa Bay had an easy call to exercise his $20MM option after what’ll almost certainly be the righty’s second straight top 10 finish in Cy Young balloting. That doesn’t preclude the possibility of a trade, as Rasmussen is set to make the largest salary for any player in team history.

Trading Rasmussen as he enters his final year under contract would be a typical Rays move. Tampa Bay’s run to the third AL title in club history may point to them operating differently in this case. President of baseball operations Erik Neander told reporters on Tuesday that the team’s early-offseason plan is keep Rasmussen as their #1 starter for 2027 (link via Marc Topkin of The Tampa Bay Times).

“(It’s) not a declarative this, that, whatever, but I can sit here very confidently and say that every intention right now is thinking about ‘Ras’ anchoring our rotation and how to make this team better going into next year,” Neander said. At a different point in the media scrum, he said the team “(wants) to have ‘Ras” back. We’re going into this offseason when you were that close to where we were, it’s hard to think we’ll be closer if ‘Ras’ isn’t part of the team.”

articles.title: Marlins Release Bradley Blalock
body: The Marlins released right-hander Bradley Blalock, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. Kevin Barral of Fish On First suggests that the 25-year-old is likely to pursue an overseas opportunity. Miami’s 40-man roster tally drops to 35.

Blalock spent one season in South Florida. The Marlins acquired him from the Rockies in January. Blalock made four MLB appearances in a mop-up role, allowing seven runs in 11 1/3 innings. He spent the rest of the season working as a starting pitcher with Triple-A Jacksonville. Blalock pitched 110 frames with a 5.56 ERA in the minors. He recorded roughly average strikeout (21.2%), walk (9.5%), and ground-ball (46.5%) marks.

A former 32nd round draft pick, Blalock has pitched parts of three seasons in MLB. He has allowed nearly eight earned runs per nine innings across 100 2/3 career frames. The 6’2″ righty also has an unimpressive 6.53 ERA at the Triple-A level, but some of that is driven by a nightmare season in the extremely hitter-friendly setting with the Rox’s affiliate in Albuquerque. Blalock throws seven pitches and averaged 96 mph with his fastball during his MLB work this year.

articles.title: Rays’ Edwin Uceta Undergoes Shoulder Surgery
body: Rays right-hander Edwin Uceta underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right shoulder last month, president of baseball operations Erik Neander revealed in a session with the media earlier today (link via Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times). Specifics aren’t clear, but Neander added that Uceta is expected to miss at least the first couple months of the 2027 season.

Uceta was a minor league pickup in the 2023-24 offseason who’d previously pitched with the Dodgers, D-backs, Mets and Cubs organizations. He came to the Rays with a career 5.80 ERA in 40 1/3 frames, but like so many other small-scale Rays pickups found a home in Tampa Bay. From 2024-25, Uceta pitched 117 2/3 innings with a 2.98 ERA. He fanned exactly one-third of his opponents, limited walks at a tidy 7.3% clip and induced some decidedly poor batted-ball metrics from opponents (88.1 mph average exit velocity, 34.8% hard-hit rate).

Before long, Uceta had found himself in a high-leverage role. He saved five games and tallied seven holds late in the’24 campaign, and he was one of manager Kevin Cash’s go-to setup arms in 2025 when he notched 21 holds (plus one rogue save). He looked locked into a setup role entering the 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Cardinals To Re-Sign Josh Fleming
body: Veteran lefty Josh Fleming is headed back to the Cardinals on a minor league deal, per Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. Fleming spent the final month of the season at Triple-A Memphis.

The Blue Jays brought Fleming in on a minor league deal last offseason. He didn’t break camp with the club, but was up by the second week of the season. Fleming was knocked around for four earned runs over three innings in his lone appearance with Toronto. He was designated for assignment, passed through waivers, and re-upped with the Blue Jays on a minor league deal.

Toronto cut Fleming in early July. He latched on with the Cubs, but that lasted just over a month. He finally found his way to the Cardinals organization for the final stretch of the season. After posting a low-3.00s ERA at Triple-A with the Blue Jays’ and Cubs’ affiliates, Fleming struggled with Memphis. He was tagged for 21 earned runs over 29 2/3 innings. Fleming gave up nine homers in six starts.

St. Louis didn’t have many proven options in the rotation entering the season, but the unit performed relatively well. It was also a remarkably durable group. Michael McGreevy, Kyle Leahy, Andre Pallante, and Matthew Liberatore each made 29+ starts. Dustin May also made 31 starts, but 10 of them came with Milwaukee after he was moved at the trade deadline. Quinn Mathews stepped into the rotation for the last two months of the year.

articles.title: Rockies Return RJ Petit To Tigers
body: The Rockies have returned 2025 Rule 5 pick RJ Petit to the Tigers, per a team announcement. The right-hander missed the entire 2026 campaign while recovering from Tommy John surgery.

Colorado took Petit with the top selection in last year’s Rule 5 draft. He was coming off a strong minor league season that saw him post a 2.44 ERA with a 29.5% strikeout rate between Double-A and Triple-A. Petit made three Spring Training appearances with the Rockies in 2026. He had TJ in March.

The 27-year-old Petit will head back to Detroit to continue recovering from the surgery. It’s unclear how much he’ll pitch this season, if at all. The injury came at a brutal time for a young arm seemingly on the brink of his MLB debut.

Petit sat in the mid-90s with his four-seamer and sinker during his stint in Toledo. He also threw a slider and changeup. Petit leaned heavily on the slider, throwing it more than 40% of the time. It averaged 83.7 mph with decent glove-side movement. FanGraphs has the slider as a 55-grade pitch.

articles.title: Red Sox Trade Eduardo Rivera To Cardinals
body: 11:17 am CT: The Red Sox have officially announced the trade.
10:34 am CT: The Red Sox are sending left-hander Eduardo Rivera to the Cardinals, reports Andrew Parker of SoxProspects.com. Boston will receive right-hander Juan Garcia in return.

Rivera was designated for assignment on Monday as part of Boston’s 40-man roster adjustments. He’s had multiple solid seasons in the minors, but struggled in his first taste of the big leagues this past year. The Red Sox ultimately ran out of space for him on the roster. Rivera will get a shot with a Cardinals squad that has less certainty in the bullpen, particularly from the left side.

Boston took Rivera in the 11th round of the 2021 draft. He operated as both a starter and reliever as he worked his way through the Red Sox system. The 23-year-old opened the 2026 campaign at Double-A. He allowed a run over two starts and earned the bump to Triple-A. Rivera compiled a 2.96 ERA across 45 2/3 frames at Worcester, with most of that work coming out of the bullpen.

Rivera was called upon in late April to eat some innings against the Yankees. He tossed 3 1/3 scoreless frames in his MLB debut. It wasn’t enough to keep him on the roster. Rivera wouldn’t get his next big-league chance until July. He fired 3 2/3 scoreless innings in his first start, a matchup against the Mets shortly before the All-Star break. Rivera was tagged for seven earned runs over three innings in his final two appearances. A lumbar strain ended his season in mid-August.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Outright Pavin Smith
body: The Diamondbacks sent first baseman Pavin Smith outright off the roster, according to the MiLB.com transaction tracker. That’ll drop their 40-man roster tally to 33.

Smith always seemed likely to lose his roster spot this offseason. Arizona already sent him through outright waivers around the All-Star Break. They called him back up in September in hope of finding a jolt against right-handed pitching. Smith managed a pinch-hit, walk-off home run to beat the Yankees on September 19 and had a big final two weeks. He had hit just.141/.236/.192 in 89 plate appearances before losing his MLB spot, though.

MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected Smith for a $2.5MM arbitration salary. This functions as an early non-tender of the former #7 overall pick. Smith will almost certainly file for free agency in the next day or two. He’ll take a league average.242/.325/.398 career slash line to the open market. Arizona will be in the market for left-handed bats and will need to acquire at least one player to slot at first base or designated hitter.

Jake Bauers is the top free agent first baseman but is attached to a qualifying offer and likely out of Arizona’s price range. Ty France, Alec Bohm, Josh Bell, Nathaniel Lowe, Joc Pederson, Eugenio Suárez and George Springer are available as free agent first base/DH types. The trade market could feature Andrew Vaughn (especially if Bauers accepts the QO to stay in Milwaukee), Spencer Torkelson, Royce Lewis and Jake Burger.

articles.title: Parker Messick Earns PPI Pick For Guardians
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced the finalists for all the major awards on Monday night. The award winners will be revealed next week, but the finalists are the players who finished top three in the voting in some order.

Guardians left-hander Parker Messick is listed alongside Cam Schlittler and Dylan Cease among the finalists for the AL Cy Young award. As MLBTR contributor Ethan Hullihen observes, that ensures that Cleveland will receive a bonus pick after the first round in the 2027 draft. Messick met the eligibility for the Prospect Promotion Incentive, which means a top three Cy Young finish within his first three seasons nets Cleveland a pick.

For those unfamiliar with the PPI intricacies, that only applies to rookie-eligible players who appeared on at least two of the preseason Top 100 prospect lists at Baseball America, ESPN and MLB Pipeline. Messick made his MLB debut last August and remained rookie-eligible going into 2026. He appeared on the ESPN and Baseball America lists. The Guardians carried him on their roster for the entire’26 season, so he could’ve earned them the pick either by winning Rookie of the Year or with a top three Cy Young finish in any season between 2026-28.

A team can only receive one PPI pick per player. Messick is unsurprisingly also a finalist for AL Rookie of the Year, but that’s no longer relevant to Cleveland’s PPI situation. They would not receive a second bonus pick if Messick wins ROY, nor would they receive any additional picks for a top three Cy Young finish in 2027 or’28.

articles.title: Rockies Hire Ethan Katz As Pitching Coach
body: The Rockies announced they’ve hired Ethan Katz as their new pitching coach. Thomas Harding of MLB.com reported the news shortly before it was official. Harding also reports that former MLB infielder Andre Lipcius is joining the staff as game-planning coach, where he’ll replace retiring assistant bench coach Ronnie Gideon. The team has not yet confirmed the Lipcius hire.

Katz takes over for Alon Leichman, who was dismissed after one year in the role. He’ll have his work cut out for him in taking on Coors Field with arguably the least talented pitching staff in the majors. Colorado was last in ERA (5.59) and strikeout rate (17.5%) for a fifth straight season. The ballpark certainly plays into that, but it’s far from the biggest problem. No team had a lower strikeout rate on the road this year, while only the Reds had a higher ERA away from home.

The 43-year-old Katz is a former minor league pitcher who was drafted by the Rockies in 2005. He never advanced beyond A-ball as a player but has carved out a strong coaching career. He spent five years as the top pitching coach with the White Sox and worked as an assistant under lead pitching voice Josh Miller with the Astros this year. Houston moved on from Katz — along with numerous other coaches and manager Joe Espada — after a season in which they ranked 24th in ERA and 12th in strikeout percentage.

articles.title: Rockies Outright Four Players
body: The Rockies announced they’ve dropped four players from their 40-man roster: infielder Chad Stevens and right-handers Blake Adams, Eiberson Castellano and TJ Shook. All four have already cleared outright waivers. Stevens, Castellano and Shook have elected free agency. Adams has been assigned to Triple-A Albuquerque. The club’s 40-man count is now at 37.

Adams, 26, will remain in the organization and could get a non-roster invite to Spring Training. He’s a 2022 draftee (13th round) who doesn’t have the previous career outright or seven years in the minors to elect free agency. The Kansas State product was called up on August 24 and tossed one inning against the Nationals in his MLB debut. It didn’t go as he hoped, as Washington tagged him for five runs, including a Daylen Lile homer. The 26-year-old had a 6.29 ERA and 16.5% strikeout rate as a multi-inning reliever in the minors this year.

Shook was acquired in the minor league portion of last year’s Rule 5 draft. He earned his first MLB call in June and made five total appearances, allowing seven runs over 7 2/3 innings. Shook managed a solid 3.45 ERA across 57 1/3 frames with Albuquerque but is a fly-ball pitcher whose fastball sits in the 92-93 mph range.

articles.title: Eight Players Receive Qualifying Offers
body: Eight players have received a $23.15MM qualifying offer, reports Joel Sherman of The New York Post. They are Randy Arozarena of the Mariners, Jake Bauers of the Brewers, David Bednar of the Yankees, Ryan Jeffers of the Twins, Brandon Lowe of the Pirates, Adrián Morejón of the Padres, Trevor Rogers of the Orioles and Seiya Suzuki of the Cubs.

As a refresher, teams are allowed to issue a one-year QO to an impending free agent as long as he spent the entire walk year with that club and has not previously received a QO in his career. The value is determined by averaging the salaries of the 125 top-paid players in the league. Players have until 3 pm Central on November 17 to decide whether to accept or reject. In the meantime, they are free to discuss contracts with other clubs, getting a sense of their market potential before making a decision.

If the player signs elsewhere, the club is then entitled to draft pick compensation. The player’s new club would be subject to penalties, certainly including draft pick forfeiture and potentially the forfeiture of international bonus pool space as well.

Most of the names are not surprising. Back in September, MLBTR took a look at the hitters and pitchers we expected to receive a QO. Rogers, Arozarena and Suzuki were characterized as locks. Jeffers and Lowe were also framed as likely recipients, with the slight hesitation due to the spending history of their respective clubs, rather than any lack of talent on the part of the players.

articles.title: Marlins Outright Patrick Monteverde
body: The Marlins announced that left-hander Patrick Monteverde has been sent outright to Triple-A Jacksonville. He has elected free agency, per Christina De Nicola of MLB.com.

Monteverde, a Marlin since they selected him in the eighth round of the 2021 draft, could be on the way to the second organization of his career this offseason. The 29-year-old made one appearance apiece with the Marlins in each of the past two seasons, but that is the extent of his major league experience. In 7 2/3 innings with the Fish, Monteverde was lit up for eight earned runs on 14 hits. He added six strikeouts against two walks.

While Monteverde hasn’t been much of a factor in the bigs, he has gotten extensive work at the minors’ highest level. He combined for 76 appearances and 49 starts with Triple-A Jacksonville over the past three years, but the soft-tossing Monteverde had trouble preventing runs during that stretch. He pitched to a 5.38 ERA with unspectacular strikeout and walk rates (18.9% and 8.6%, respectively) over 271 innings.

articles.title: Pirates Claim Akil Baddoo
body: The Pirates have claimed outfielder Akil Baddoo off waivers from the Brewers, according to announcements from both clubs. The Bucs have 40-man space and don’t need to make a corresponding move.

Baddoo, 28, didn’t play in the majors this year. He had a good rookie showing back in 2021 but struggled in subsequent seasons. The Brewers signed him to a major league deal ahead of the 2026 campaign. He suffered a left quad strain in spring training and began the season on the IL. When he was ready to come off the IL in May, he was optioned to Triple-A.

He ended up performing well in 64 games at that level. He hit 11 home runs and stole seven bases. His 23.3% strikeout rate was around average while his 12.2% walk rate was quite strong. He slashed.252/.342/.469 for a 113 wRC+ while spending time at all three outfield spots.

Baddoo exhausted his final option in 2026 and is now out of options. That will make it harder for him to hold a roster spot going forward. The Brewers bumped him off but the Bucs have scooped him up, at least for the moment.

The Pirates project to have Oneil Cruz and Bryan Reynolds in two outfield spots. Esmerlyn Valdéz, Jake Mangum, Jhostynxon García and others will be trying to earn playing time next to Cruz and Reynolds. Baddoo is now in that mix as well. If he holds his roster spot through the winter, he could compete for a role during spring training. If he is outrighted off the roster later in the offseason, he would have the right to elect free agency, both because he has a previous career outright and because he has at least three years of service time.

articles.title: Orioles Make Four Waiver Claims; Leody Taveras Elects Free Agency
body: The Orioles announced a dizzying slew of roster moves ahead of the deadline to get 40-man rosters down to 40 players. Baltimore claimed right-hander Josh White off waivers from the Marlins and southpaw Philip Abner off waivers from the Mets. The O’s also claimed catcher Zach Morgan from the Giants and righty Chase Hampton from the Cardinals.

Meanwhile, outfielder Leody Taveras cleared waivers and rejected an outright assignment, instead opting for free agency. Baltimore also confirmed its previously reported outright of former top prospect Heston Kjerstad, while adding that righty Yosver Zulueta and catcher Yohel Pozo were outrighted to Triple-A Norfolk. All of Kjerstad, Zulueta and Pozo can become minor league free agents. [UPDATE: Kjerstad, Zulueta, and Pozo indeed elected free agency, as per the MiLB.com transaction log.]

White, 25, is a 2022 fifth rounder. He’s only pitched two-thirds of an inning in the majors, during which he was shelled for five runs due primarily to issuing four walks. He posted a 2.41 ERA in 56 Triple-A frames, however, fanning 27% of his opponents there. His 13.5% walk rate in Jacksonville shows that the command struggles in his lone MLB appearance were more than just debut day jitters. White sits 94.4 mph on his four-seamer and mixes in a curveball and slider he uses with equal frequency. He has a pair of minor league option years remaining.

articles.title: Mets Claim Pierson Ohl
body: The Mets have claimed right-hander Pierson Ohl off waivers from the Rockies, reports Chelsea Janes of SNY. Colorado has announced the move.

The Rockies cut Ohl from their 40-man roster less than a year after acquiring him in a January 2026 trade with the Twins.
