They didn’t end up getting any contributions from Ohl, who underwent Tommy John surgery in late February and missed the entire season. He began throwing in August in hopes of returning in 2027. If he does, it could be as a member of the Mets.

Now 27 years old, Ohl has spent most of his pro career with the Twins organization. They drafted him in the 14th round in 2021 and helped him develop into a decent prospect. When they selected Ohl’s contract in July 2025, he owned a microscopic 3.6% walk rate in the minors. He continued limiting walks during a 14-appearance, 30-inning major league debut that year, as he issued free passes at a 5.3% clip. While that accompanied an unspectacular strikeout rate (20.3%) and a high ERA (5.10), Ohl posted more encouraging underlying numbers. ERA estimators such as SIERA (3.87), xFIP (3.99), FIP (4.20) and xERA (4.78) all suggested he deserved a better fate.

After a lost year with Colorado, Ohl will attempt to establish himself with his third organization. He is joining the Mets with a full slate of options and a good track record at the lower levels, where he has typically leaned on a low-90s fastball and an 81 mph changeup. Most of Ohl’s minor league work has come in Double-A ball, where he has logged a 3.47 ERA in 228 innings.

articles.title: Reds Claim Duncan Davitt, Paxton Schultz
body: The Reds announced a pair of waiver claims Monday. Cincinnati claimed right-hander Duncan Davitt off waivers from the Giants and fellow righty Paxton Schultz off waivers from the Nationals. They’ll both go right onto the Reds’ 40-man roster, which had five vacancies as of this morning.

Davitt entered the professional ranks as an 18th-round pick of the Rays in 2022. They wound up sending him (as well as Curtis Mead and Ben Peoples) to the White Sox in 2025 in a pre-deadline trade for righty Adrian Houser. Davitt made his major league debut this past April, but he only logged two appearances before the White Sox shipped him to the Braves for catcher Joey Bart in early August. He changed hands yet again when the Giants claimed him off waivers from the Braves in early September. Between the White Sox and Giants, he combined for eight innings of eight-run, 10-hit ball and recorded five strikeouts against four walks.

The 27-year-old Davitt still has two minor league options left, which is a plus for the Reds, though he had difficulty at the lower levels in 2026. While mostly leaning on a 93 mph fastball and an 84 mph slider, he registered a 6.04 ERA with an above-average 24.0% strikeout rate and slightly below-average 9.3% walk rate. He tossed 69 1/3 Triple-A innings and 6 2/3 in Double-A ball.

articles.title: White Sox Claim Graham Pauley
body: The White Sox announced that they have claimed infielder Graham Pauley off waivers from the Marlins. The Sox also outrighted left-hander Ky Bush and outfielder Junior Pérez to Triple-A Charlotte.

It’s a busy time of year for transactions, particularly those involving fringe players. The injured list goes away at 4 pm Central time today, meaning several players will be retaking roster spots. November 17 is the deadline for clubs to give roster spots to players who would otherwise be eligible for the Rule 5 draft. The roster squeeze will push many players to the waiver wire.

Pauley, now 26, was originally drafted by the Padres. He was sent to the Marlins in the 2024 deadline trade which sent Tanner Scott and Bryan Hoeing to San Diego. Pauley has received some big league chances with both the Padres and Marlins but hasn’t yet done much to prove himself. He exhausted his final option season in 2026 and is now slated to be out of options going forward. That will make it harder for him to hold a roster spot.

The Marlins have nudged him off but the White Sox have grabbed him, at least for now. It’s possible he will end up back on the waiver wire later in the offseason. As mention, Pauley hasn’t done much to establish himself at the big league level. That’s particularly true offensively. In 370 plate appearances, he has a.209/.272/.364 batting line.

articles.title: Braves Claim Mitchell Parker
body: The Braves announced that they have claimed left-hander Mitchell Parker off waivers from the Nationals.

Parker, 27, was a fifth-round pick by the Nats in 2020. He had a solid big league debut in 2024, making 29 starts and pitching 151 innings with a 4.29 ERA, a 20.6% strikeout rate and a 6.7% walk rate. He sat 92-93 mph that season, didn’t miss many bats and gave up a fair bit of loud contact in the air, but it was a solid enough season that gave him the look of an optionable fourth or fifth starter for Washington for the next few years.

The 2025 follow-up to that rookie effort was a disaster, however. Parker set a new career-high with 164 2/3 innings pitched, but his ERA skyrocketed to 5.68 while his strikeout and walk rates swung wildly in the wrong direction (14.2 K%, 8.0 BB%). Parker’s glut of fly-balls came back to bite him, too, as he was rocked for 25 round-trippers.

In 2026, Parker worked out of the bullpen with even shakier results: 34 2/3 innings and a 6.58 ERA. His strikeout and walk rates inched back in the right direction but were still worse than average. The lefty’s velocity ticked up to an average of 93.6 mph while working in relief, but that was at best a nominal silver lining.

articles.title: Marlins To Claim Cameron Weston
body: The Marlins claimed righty Cameron Weston off waivers from the division-rival Mets, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. New York had claimed Weston off waivers from the Orioles in early September. He spent the remainder of the season with the Mets’ top affiliate in Syracuse but didn’t pitch in a big league game as a Met.

Weston, whom the Orioles drafted in the eighth round in 2022, developed into a notable prospect with the organization. Both Baseball America (No. 13) and FanGraphs (14th) regarded him as one of the Orioles’ 15 best farmhands at the outset of the 2025 season. At that point, he owned a 3.09 ERA with a 28.3% strikeout rate and 7.2% walk rate in the minors. Weston ascended to the Triple-A level for the first time that year, but he posted a 4.59 ERA with far less impressive strikeout and walk numbers (22.0% and 11.7%, respectively) in 135 1/3 innings.

This past season went even worse for the 26-year-old Weston, who struggled to a 7.89 ERA with an 11.9% walk rate over 51 2/3 innings with Triple-A Norfolk. Weston made his major league debut with a scoreless inning against the Blue Jays on May 28, but that counts as his lone MLB appearance thus far. The Orioles cut him from their 40-man roster on Sept. 1. To Weston’s credit, he ended 2026 on a high note after the Mets claimed him. In 6 1/3 frames with Triple-A Syracuse, he gave up just one run on two hits and recorded 10 strikeouts against one walk.

articles.title: Mariners To Claim Isaac Mattson
body: The Mariners have claimed right-hander Isaac Mattson off waivers from the Pirates, MLBTR has learned. Pittsburgh hadn’t designated him for assignment, so it seems they instead quietly placed him on outright waivers at some point in the past couple days. Seattle’s 40-man roster is now four players over capacity, so they’ll need to subtract four players at some point prior to today’s deadline to get back down to 40.

Mattson, 31, has pitched in each of the past three seasons with the Pirates. He was a particularly solid arm for them in 2025, when he tallied a dozen holds and notched a spectacular 2.45 ERA with a 22.7% strikeout rate and 9.6% walk rate.

Mattson’s results went the wrong direction in 2026. Mattson was roughed up for a 5.35 ERA, although a weighty.347 average on balls in play and 68% strand rate were both well out of line with his career norms. Mattson did give up far too much hard contact (92.1 mph average exit velocity, 52.1% hard-hit rate), so the bloated ERA can’t be attributed solely to poor fortune on balls in play, but there’s still reason to forecast some positive/favorable regression for the righty.

In three seasons with the Bucs, Mattson logged a 3.83 ERA and 20 holds in 91 2/3 innings. He sits 94.2 mph on a four-seamer he uses at a nearly 75% clip, mixing in a relatively rare slider and changeup in a three-pitch repertoire. He also had a curveball early in his career, when he debuted with the 2021 Orioles, but he shelved that pitch back in 2024.

articles.title: Cardinals Decline Ryne Stanek’s Club Option
body: The Cardinals have declined their $6MM club option on right-hander Ryne Stanek for the 2027 season, the St. Louis Post-Dispatch’s Derrick Goold reports. Stanek will instead take the $1MM buyout and enter free agency.

Stanek inked a one-year, $2.5MM deal last winter, so the righty will walk away with $3.5MM from his lone season in the Gateway City. He delivered a 4.02 ERA, 24.3% strikeout rate, and 12% walk rate over 62 2/3 innings, and his 70 appearances tied George Soriano for second on the team.

It was almost exactly a standard season for Stanek, with his numbers coming very close to the 3.87 ERA, 26.8K%, and 11.9BB% he has posted over 521 MLB innings with six different teams over parts of 10 seasons. At least in bottom-line results, Stanek’s 2026 was a step up from his previous two seasons, when he had a 5.09 ERA over 111 1/3 innings with the Mets and Mariners.

Stanek remains a very hard thrower, as his fastball averaged 98mph. He also showed batters something new, as Stanek decreased usage of his fastball from 57.1% in 2025 to 51.5% in 2026, while bumping up the use of a very effective slider.

Since Stanek turned 35 in July, his age may limit him to just one-year offers this winter, even though he appears to have plenty left in the tank. The Cardinals and other teams figure to show interest in a durable veteran who can cover innings can still deliver the velocity to fool younger batters.

articles.title: Braves Sign Vidal Bruján To Minor League Deal
body: The Braves have brought in infielder Vidal Bruján on a minor league pact, according to his transactions log at MiLB.com. He will report to Triple-A Gwinnett as a depth option.

The 28-year-old Bruján has played in 271 big league games for six clubs since debuting in 2021. He’s never shown much at the plate, taking 658 plate appearances and batting.197/.266/.272 with a 53 wRC+. His biggest sample of work came in 2024 with the Marlins. Bruján had a 74 wRC+ in 278 plate appearances that year, striking out and walking at better than average rates but showing nothing in the way of power.

Bruján’s deal with Atlanta is technically a reunion. The Braves claimed him off waivers from the Orioles in August 2025 and gave him 47 plate appearances down the stretch in a lost season. Bruján was designated for assignment in January, claimed off waivers by the Twins, then quickly flipped to the Mets in a cash deal. He appeared in nine games for New York in May and June but spent most of the season at Triple-A, posting a 113 wRC+ and chipping in 16 stolen bases.

The Braves figure to invite Bruján to Spring Training (whenever it ends up happening) as a non-roster player. Ozzie Albies will return at second base after his $7MM club option was exercised. RosterResource currently has Jim Jarvis as Atlanta’s starting shortstop. The team could try to re-sign Mauricio Dubon as a stopgap given Jarvis’ meager 57 wRC+ in his debut campaign.

articles.title: Angels Outright Sebastián Rivero; Sammy Peralta Elects Free Agency
body: Nov. 1: Peralta has indeed elected free agency, as announced by the club.

Oct. 29: The Angels announced Thursday that left-hander Sammy Peralta and catcher Sebastián Rivero both went unclaimed on waivers and were assigned outright to Triple-A Salt Lake. Both are eligible to elect free agency and will presumably do so.

The 28-year-old Peralta split the 2026 season between the Rockies and Halos, combining for 23 innings with a 6.65 earned run average. He fanned a respectable 20.5% of opponents against a solid 8% walk rate, leading to better reviews from metrics like SIERA (3.96). However, Peralta was quite homer-prone, plunked four of the 112 batters he faced, and was dinged for a brutal.417 average on balls in play, which did him no favors. He’s now pitched in parts of four major league seasons and carries a 5.64 ERA in 68 2/3 frames. The soft-tossing southpaw has averaged 89.1 mph on his four-seamer and 88.8 mph on his sinker during his brief major league stints.

Rivero, 27, took only 57 plate appearances for the Angels, hitting.245/.286/.283. He’s had brief stints as a backup catcher both with Kansas City and Anaheim, totaling 164 major league plate appearances with a.197/.247/.237 slash. He’s never hit much in the minors either, but Rivero is a quality defender who has found himself occasionally pressed into big league action despite being the third or fourth catcher on the depth chart with multiple organizations. Assuming both players do indeed become free agents, they’ll look to catch on as minor league depth with a new team in free agency.

articles.title: Reds Decline Mutual Options For Eugenio Suárez, Pierce Johnson
body: The Reds have declined their 2027 mutual options for third baseman Eugenio Suárez and right-hander Pierce Johnson, the team announced. Both players are now free agents, leaving the Reds with five openings on their 40-man roster.

Neither decision comes as a surprise, especially considering it has been over a decade since both a team and a player triggered a mutual option. Suárez’s $16MM option did not come with a buyout. Meanwhile, the Reds chose to pay Johnson a $1MM buyout in lieu of the $8MM they would have owed him had both sides exercised the option.

Unless the 35-year-old Suárez sticks around on a new deal, this will wrap up his second stint in Cincinnati. The right-handed slugger previously played there from 2015-21, when he put together three seasons of at least 4.0 fWAR and two with 30-plus home runs. He also earned his first of two All-Star nods during that stretch.

The Reds first moved on from Suárez when they sent him (and outfielder Jesse Winker) to the Mariners in a blockbuster trade three weeks before the 2022 season opened. He then spent two seasons with Seattle before going to Arizona for one and a half. The Diamondbacks traded him back to the Mariners ahead of the 2025 deadline. Between the D-backs and pennant-contending Mariners last year, Suárez swatted 49 homers for the second time in his career and slashed.228/.298/.526. Despite a low batting average and on-base percentage, he put up a solidly above-average wRC+ of 125.

articles.title: Emilio Pagán Declines Player Option
body: Reliever Emilio Pagán has declined his $10MM player option with the Reds for 2027, Francys Romero of BeisbolFR reports. Unless he signs a new deal with the Reds by 4 p.m. CT on Nov. 2, the right-hander will head to the open market.

The 35-year-old Pagán, who has pitched for six teams since he debuted with the Mariners in 2017, spent the past three seasons in Cincinnati. He originally joined the club on a two-year, $16MM guarantee in December 2023, but the first season of the contract didn’t go particularly well. Pagán had separate stints on the injured list with triceps and lat issues, and he only delivered 38 innings of 4.50 ERA ball when healthy.

The past two years went far better for Pagán, who took over as the Reds’ closer in 2025. That year, he converted 32 of 38 save opportunities and recorded a stingy 2.88 ERA with quality strikeout and walk rates of 30.0% and 8.1%, respectively, over 68 2/3 frames. He was able to keep runs off the board despite inducing ground balls just 28.7% of the time. Pagán has walked that tightrope throughout his career, having logged a 29.3% ground-ball rate over 549 1/3 innings in the majors.

articles.title: Braves Hire Dana Brown For Scouting Advisor Role
body: The Braves are reuniting with Dana Brown as a senior advisor in their amateur scouting department, as per USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. It’s a homecoming for Brown, who worked as Atlanta’s VP of scouting from 2019-22 before he was hired as the Astros’ general manager.

Brown and Braves president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos have a long working relationship dating back to their days in Montreal, when Anthopoulos was Brown’s assistant when Brown was hired as the Expos’ director of amateur scouting in 2002. Brown continued in that role with the Expos/Nationals through the franchise’s move to Washington and until 2009, when Anthopoulos (now the Blue Jays’ GM) hired Brown for a special assistant’s role in Toronto. Once Anthopoulos was hired by the Braves following the 2017 season, Brown reunited with Anthopoulos once more within a couple of years.

The Astros’ hiring of Brown was a rare case of a team making a front office change right after a World Series title, as former GM James Click was let go after the playoff run due to clashes with owner Jim Crane (who is known for playing a direct role in baseball operations). While Brown didn’t capture a championship during his time in Houston, he also had a much better record than most GMs who are shown the door. Houston made the ALCS in 2023 and won two AL West titles in Brown’s three full seasons as GM, and the Astros even ended up winning the division again this year, albeit with an 81-81 record.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Los Angeles Angels
body: The Angels, amazingly, just had their first 100-loss season. That’s a low point for the franchise but there is optimism about the future because the 2027 club will have a new owner, a new front office leader and a new manager.
Mike Trout, OF: $141.8MM through 2030 Yusei Kikuchi, LHP: $21MM through 2027 Option Decisions
Robert Stephenson, RHP: $2.5MM club option was declined Additional Commitments
Anthony Rendon still owed $30.4MM in deferred salary 2027 financial commitments: $64.05MM Total future commitments: $193.2MM
Arbitration-Eligible Players (service time in parentheses; projected salaries courtesy of MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz)

Reid Detmers (4.159): $7.5MM Jose Siri (4.150): $2.3MM Josh Lowe (4.075): $3.6MM Tyler Heineman (4.066): $1.5MM Tayler Saucedo (4.043): $1.5MM Zach Neto (3.170): $9.8MM Grayson Rodriguez (3.129): $2.1MM Ben Joyce (3.075): $1.1MM Nolan Schanuel (3.045): $3MM Oswald Peraza (3.014): $1.4MM Sam Bachman (2.149): $1.1MM Non-tender candidates: Siri, Lowe, Heineman, Rodriguez, Peraza, Bachman

Anthony Rendon, Travis d’Arnaud, Yoán Moncada, Adam Frazier, Robert Stephenson It’s no secret that things haven’t been going well for the Angels lately. They haven’t made the postseason since 2014. They haven’t had a winning record since 2015. Despite that long run of poor results, they have resisted rebuilding and prioritized short-term contention.

articles.title: Luis Severino To Exercise Player Option, Remain With A’s
body: Athletics right-hander Luis Severino will exercise his $22MM player option and forgo a return to the open market, as first reported by Mike Rodriguez of Rompiendo Sports. Severino will remain with the A’s in their final season in Sacramento before becoming a free agent in the 2027-28 offseason.

Although Severino previously expressed dissatisfaction with the facilities at Sutter Health Park, it’s no surprise that the veteran will stick around for the third and final year of his contract. Severino posted a 4.16 ERA over 12 starts and 62 2/3 innings before going on the 15-day injured list at the end of May with a strain of his shoulder capsule and subscapularis muscle. The injury proved to be season-ending, as Severino was able to resume throwing but didn’t get deep enough into his recovery process to even begin a minor league rehab assignment.

Between this shortened season and his so-so performance in 2025, Severino wouldn’t have made anywhere close to $22MM in free agency. Opting out of his deal also would’ve meant hitting the open market in offseason that is bound to be interrupted by a lockout, so it makes plenty of sense for Severino to take his guaranteed payday and focus entirely on returning to the mound in 2027 (Severino’s age-33 season).

articles.title: Astros Hire Randy Flores As General Manager
body: The Astros have hired Cardinals assistant GM/scouting director Randy Flores as their new general manager. The team announced the move on Friday evening.

“Randy has had a huge impact on the Cardinals over the last 10 seasons,” Houston owner Jim Crane said in the press release. “Throughout the entire interview process, we’ve been thoroughly impressed with Randy and with his background in scouting and player acquisition. We’re happy to welcome Randy and his family to the Astros and we can’t wait to get to work on bringing another championship to Houston.” Flores and Crane will meet with the media during an introductory press conference on Monday morning.

It’s a surprise turn of events. The Athletic reported on Thursday that Brewers assistant GM Matt Kleine had emerged as the frontrunner for the position. Chandler Rome of The Athletic reports that Houston offered the GM job to Kleine on Wednesday evening, hours before Milwaukee won its first World Series.

Although it’s unclear precisely what changed, The Athletic suggests that Kleine had been seeking the title ‘president of baseball operations’ earlier in the week. They write that the Milwaukee AGM never pulled his name out of the running, though it’s possible there was some kind of hangup in negotiations on title and/or salary.

articles.title: Michael Soroka Declines Mutual Option With D-Backs
body: Michael Soroka has officially declined his end of a $10MM mutual option with the Diamondbacks, reports Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic. He’ll be paid a $1MM buyout and return to free agency.

This was inevitable, as Soroka has put himself in position to do pretty well financially. The Diamondbacks picked him up on a $7.5MM deal last offseason. (He earned an additional $1.35MM in performance bonuses by starting 20 games.) He was initially slated to open the season in a swing role, but an Opening Day injured list stint for Merrill Kelly drew him into the starting five.

Soroka was one of Torey Lovullo’s more reliable starters and held a rotation spot all season. He pitched to a 3.41 earned run average across 116 innings. He led Arizona starters with a 24.1% strikeout rate while limiting his free passes to a 6% clip. Soroka tailed off a bit in the second half as he navigated injured list stints for a left glute strain and arm inflammation, yet it was mid-rotation production on a rate basis. This was also his highest workload since 2019.

The innings questions are going to keep Soroka from commanding a massive contract, but he’s very likely to secure a multi-year deal. He’s entering his age-29 season and has one of the better strikeout and walk profiles of the group of mid-tier free agent starters. Soroka has a chance at three years, with a two-year pact in the $10-12MM range feeling like a floor.

articles.title: Guardians Select Milan Tolentino
body: The Guardians announced that they have selected the contract of infielder Milan Tolentino. They also declined a club option on right-hander Trevor Stephan as well as their end of a mutual option with righty Shawn Armstrong.

Tolentino, 25 next month, was a fourth-round pick in the 2020 draft. The fact that the Guardians are adding him to the roster now suggests he was about to qualify for minor league free agency. By giving him a roster spot, they prevent him from getting away.

He has never really been a top prospect in the system but he clearly has some tools. He has spent the past two years at the Triple-A level. He has stepped to the plate 957 times in that span, hitting 42 home runs and drawing walks at a strong 12.5% clip. The flipside is that he has also struck out as a massive 32.9% pace. That has led to a lopsided.221/.321/.445 batting line and 100 wRC+, indicating his offense works out to league average on the whole.

Defensively, Tolentino has spent most of his time at shortstop while also getting lots of action at second and third base. He very briefly dabbled in the outfield this year. The Guards have Travis Bazzana at second and José Ramírez at third. Shortstop could be covered by either Brayan Rocchio or Ángel Genao. Daniel Schneemann is on the roster and could be in a bench/utility role.

Tolentino will try to push into that mix but he has a full slate of options and could be in line for more time at Triple-A. He already has a couple of seasons at that level but it wouldn’t hurt to get some more seasoning in an attempt to cut down on the punchouts.

articles.title: Diamondbacks To Hire Ben Fritz As Pitching Coach
body: The Diamondbacks have a new pitching coach. Dennis Lin of The Athletic reports that Arizona has snaked Ben Fritz away from the Padres. He has been working as the bullpen coach in San Diego. The Snakes parted ways with pitching coach Brian Kaplan earlier this month.

Fritz, 45, was a first-round pick of the Athletics back in 2002. He pitched in the minors through 2008 but never made it to the big leagues. He kept pitching in indy ball through 2010. The Padres gave him a minor league coaching job in 2015. He got the bullpen coach job at the big league level ahead of the 2020 season. He was briefly the pitching coach in 2021. Larry Rothschild was fired from that job in August of that year. Fritz held the job the rest of the way and then Ruben Niebla was hired in October.

For what it’s worth, the Padres have had good results in the pitching department in recent years. From 2020 to 2026, San Diego pitchers posted a collective 3.86 earned run average, behind just six other clubs. The Diamondbacks had a 4.55 ERA in that same time frame, better than just three teams.

It’s always tough to determine how much credit or blame to give to an individual coach, since he can only work with the players on the roster and is also just one member of a larger staff. But it seems Fritz has a good reputation in the league. He reportedly drew some interest from other clubs last year. Lin’s report from today notes that the Rockies were interested in him for their pitching coach vacancy but the Diamondbacks have managed to bring him aboard.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Seeking Controllable Starting Pitching
body: After deciding whether or not to trade Ketel Marte, a secondary item on the Diamondbacks’ to-do list will be adding to the rotation. General manager Mike Hazen tells Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic that he would like to acquire a controllable starter. That is more likely to happen via trade, as Hazen is unlikely to push hard for a starter in free agency given the team is planning to reduce payroll.

The D-backs had a middling 4.28 ERA out of their rotation this year. The group’s 9.6% K-BB rate bested only the lowly Rockies, as Arizona’s starters showed good control but struggled to strike opponents out. Eduardo Rodriguez was better than expected. He posted a 2.89 ERA over 32 starts despite middling peripherals and led the staff with 3.2 fWAR. Michael Soroka and Brandon Pfaadt were the next best performers after him. Both had ERAs below 3.40, with Soroka riding an above-average 24.1% strikeout rate and Pfaadt relying on ground balls and control.

The trouble is that Soroka will become a free agent once he declines his end of a $10MM mutual option. Both sides have expressed interest in a reunion, though it remains unclear how far Arizona will go to retain Soroka while also addressing the rest of their roster. The bullpen, first base, and left-handed hitting all need to be addressed, as MLBTR’s Anthony Franco wrote in our Offseason Outlook series.

articles.title: Marlins Exercise Club Option On Sandy Alcantara
body: One of the most straightforward option decisions for any team this offseason is now official. The Marlins announced Friday that they’ve exercised their $21MM club option on right-hander Sandy Alcantara. It’s a net $19MM decision, as the Marlins would have owed Alcantara a $2MM buyout even if they’d preferred to move on and let the face of their franchise test free agency. The 2027 campaign will be the last year he’s under contract. He’s slated to become a free agent next winter.

There was never a doubt that this option would be picked up. Alcantara had a strong rebound in his second season back from Tommy John surgery. Major League Baseball’s consummate workhorse tossed 214 innings — tops in either league — and notched a 3.87 earned run average. Alcantara’s 17.1% strikeout rate was well below average, but his 6.6% walk rate was strong and his 41.9% ground-ball rate was about average.

Because of the Marlins’ perennially small payroll and frequent rebuilds, Alcantara’s name has come up in trade chatter at seemingly every turn over the years. That’s far less likely to be the case this winter, even as he heads into his final year of contractual control.

The Marlins reportedly have no interest in trading Alcantara and have every intent of keeping him and starting him on Opening Day once again next season. President of baseball operations Peter Bendix has spoken of Alcantara’s importance to the club on multiple occasions, and he’s unsurprisingly said to be a personal favorite of owner Bruce Sherman.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Expected To Field Interest On Ketel Marte
body: The Diamondbacks’ biggest offseason question is whether they’ll line up a Ketel Marte trade. Arizona fielded interest in the star second baseman early last offseason, though it seemed mostly a matter of due diligence as they explored ways to add controllable starting pitching.

There’s a good chance the team will more aggressively shop Marte this offseason — albeit with various reasons why it may be more difficult to actually make a deal. Most notably, Marte can veto any trade after securing 10-and-5 rights (10 years of service time, the last five with one club) in April.

Reports from both John Gambadoro/Alex Weiner of Arizona Sports and Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic indicate that the Snakes will explore Marte trades yet again. Piecoro writes that they’ve received preliminary interest from other clubs, though it’s obviously very early in the process with the trade market just reopening this morning.

Marte features prominently on MLBTR’s list of the game’s top offseason trade candidates, slotting in at #6. That’s driven in large part by comments from team officials who’ve become increasingly frustrated with Marte no-showing for certain games over the years.

articles.title: Braves Exercise Options On Ronald Acuña Jr., Ozzie Albies
body: The Braves announced they’ve picked up their options on Ronald Acuña Jr. and Ozzie Albies. Acuña will make $17MM next season, while Albies will match this year’s $7MM salary. Those were Atlanta’s only option decisions this year.

There wasn’t much suspense with either decision. The Braves weren’t going to cut either member of their core for what would’ve amounted to $7MM in savings. Acuña’s option came with a $10MM buyout that meant he’d only have been bought out had he suffered some kind of career-altering injury. Albies’ deal didn’t have a buyout but comes with a base salary akin to what solid utility infielders (e.g. Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Willi Castro) make as free agents.

The Braves have Acuña until team control for two seasons, as there’s another $17MM option on his deal for the 2028 campaign. That one doesn’t have a buyout, so it’d be a costlier decision, but it’s still highly likely to be exercised. Acuña hit 20 homers with a.255/.345/.451 slash line in a relative down year. He’s one season removed from a monster.290/.417/.518 showing after coming back from the second ACL tear of his career.

This will be the final season of the $35MM extension that Albies signed early in his career. Atlanta has tacked on $10MM by picking up two club options along the way — a $4MM buyout on his first option was already factored into that $35MM guarantee — so he made a total of $45MM over a nine-year stretch. Albies handily outperformed those salaries, though he’s been more serviceable than great going back to the start of the 2024 season.

articles.title: The Braves’ Other Middle Infield Question
body: The Braves have the most glaring shortstop need in MLB. Mauricio Dubón and Ha-Seong Kim are impending free agents, leaving Jim Jarvis as the top in-house option. There’s a decent chance they’ll re-sign Dubón on a two-year deal, but he’s ideally suited as a super-utility player.

If the Astros make Jeremy Peña available before his year of club control, the Braves should be heavily involved. They’ll also surely look into younger shortstops who might be expendable on their current team (e.g. Anthony Volpe, Brayan Rocchio). The focus on shortstop has potentially overshadowed that the Braves’ other middle infield position might also need a shakeup.

Ozzie Albies has started 1117 games at the keystone for the Braves over the past nine seasons. No one else has started more than 44. Albies has been a steady, durable lineup fixture for years. He has handily outperformed the $35MM contract extension he signed in April 2019 and was a legitimate star through the’23 campaign.

articles.title: Pirates Notes: Keller, Valdez, Buchanan
body: Mitch Keller’s season ended the day before the trade deadline, when the Pirates placed him on the 60-day injured list due to a teres major strain in his right shoulder. The team didn’t provide major specifics at the time, but Aiden Stepansky of MLB.com writes that Keller is believed to have suffered a Grade 3 strain — a gruesome injury that saw his teres major muscle detach from the bone.

Keller somewhat remarkably didn’t require surgery. Doctors recommended a lengthy down period and rehab. The plan has been for him to resume throwing late this month, and he’s expected to have a normal offseason.

The injury didn’t occur on one specific pitch, it seems. Keller told Stepansky he couldn’t pinpoint the exact moment at which it occurred. That suggests he was pitching through discomfort for some time, and the results bear that out. The typically steady Keller was dinged for a 5.29 ERA in 22 starts. His 17.7% strikeout rate was a career-worst, and his 8.3% walk rate — while still solid — was his highest since 2022. He posted a sub-7% mark each year from 2023-25. Keller’s 93.3 mph average fastball was also a career-low mark. He sat at a season-low 91.9 mph in his final start before hitting the injured list.

articles.title: Astros Hire Conner Watson As Director Of Hitting
body: The Astros have hired Conner Watson as their new director of hitting, The Athletic’s Chandler Rome reports. Watson heads to Houston after spending the last two seasons as the Guardians’ assistant director of hitting development.

The new hire continues an offseason of change for an Astros team that is looking for both a new GM and manager. In this case, Watson fills a role that has been open since August, when former director of hitting Dan Hennigan departed for a coaching job on the Wake Forest staff.

Spencer Medick was hired as Houston’s director of pitching earlier this week, so the Astros now have two division heads in place overseeing the entire organization’s pitching and hitting approaches. It is perhaps a little unusual that Medick and Watson were hired in advance of a general manager taking the wheel of baseball operations, though it perhaps tracks given how Astros owner Jim Crane is known for his active role in front office decisions.

Before joining the Guardians, Watson spent three years as a lead instructor at Driveline’s Arizona branch. He’ll now look to shake up and perhaps modernize the Astros’ hitting practices at both the major and minor league levels. While many of Houston’s coaches and manager Joe Espada won’t be returning in 2027, hitting coach Victor Rodriguez was expected to be retained, though this could potentially change depending on Watson’s plans.

articles.title: Guardians Notes: Kwan, Velazquez, Rotation
body: The Guardians won the American League Central for the third straight year and reached the doorstep of the World Series in 2026, but their season ended with a six-game loss to the Rays in the ALCS. With their championship hopes dashed again, Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti, general manager Mike Chernoff and assistant GM Matt Forman met with the media on Thursday to wrap up 2026 and discuss the upcoming offseason.
[RELATED: Guardians Offseason Outlook]

The Guardians aren’t at risk of losing outfielder Steven Kwan to free agency this winter, but the two-time All-Star only has one year of control left. MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projects an $11.3MM salary for Kwan in his third and final trip through arbitration. That’s an eminently reasonable salary for a player of his caliber, though it’s a pricey figure for a team that had the lowest payroll in baseball (around $75MM). The Guardians have a history of trading away productive veterans with dwindling team control, evidenced by deals in which they shipped out Josh Naylor, Francisco Lindor, Corey Kluber, Carlos Carrasco, Trevor Bauer and Mike Clevinger. With that in mind, Kwan could be an offseason trade candidate. However, if we’re to believe Guardians brass, he isn’t going anywhere.
“As we sit here today, we’re expecting Steven Kwan to be a big part of a contending team next year,” Antonetti said (link via Paul Hoynes of cleveland.com).

articles.title: Todd Benzinger Passes Away
body: Former big leaguer Todd Benzinger passed away on Wednesday at age 63, according to a statement released by the Reds earlier this week. Three of Benzinger’s nine MLB seasons (from 1987-95) were spent in Cincinnati, with the switch-hitter playing a memorable role in the Reds’ World Series-winning squad in 1990.

A fourth-round pick for the Red Sox in the 1981 draft, Benzinger spent his first two Major League seasons with Boston before he was dealt to the Reds as part of a five-player swap in December 1988. It was a virtual homecoming for Benzinger, whose birthplace of Dayton, Kentucky is right across the Ohio River from Cincinnati. Benzinger made a bit of history in his very first at-bat as a Red, as his RBI single in the first inning on Opening Day 1989 officially ended Orel Hershiser’s regular-season scoreless-inning streak at a record 59 innings.

Acting as the Reds’ everyday first baseman in 1989, Benzinger moved into more of a platoon role the next season as both a first baseman and occasional left fielder. Benzinger did get the start at first in Game 4 of the 1990 World Series, and he’ll forever be remembered in Cincinnati for recording the final out (a Carney Lansford pop-up in foul territory) that sealed the Reds’ sweep of the Athletics.

“[Benzinger] was a super nice guy,” former Reds teammate and Hall-of-Famer Barry Larkin told MLB.com’s Mark Sheldon. “He was always a hard worker, not real loud. Just about doing his business. He was just a steady, consistent contributor. There was no craziness about him. He fit in well with the team. Just a really good, solid guy.”

articles.title: Poll: Does Paul Skenes Just Need To Fix His Changeup?
body: It’s obvious that Paul Skenes did not have the follow-up campaign one would have expected of a Cy Young winner. After holding opponents to a 1.97 ERA last year, that figure nearly doubled to 3.82 in 2026. Skenes still came out above average by strikeout rate (28.1%) and walk rate (6.9%), and ERA estimators like xERA (3.28) and SIERA (3.34) were a bit kinder to him than the surface-level ERA. For what it’s worth, FanGraphs valued Skenes at 4.2 wins above replacement, ranking 12th-highest among qualified starters this year. Nonetheless, it was a clear drop-off for Skenes by his lofty standards.

As MLBTR’s Charlie Wright wrote in August, Skenes’ stuff looked mostly the same this year. Apart from ditching his cutter, the righty’s four-seam fastball, splitter, sinker, slider, and changeup usage were all within 3.5% of their 2025 levels. The four-seamer remained his most common offering and averaged 96.8 mph – a 1.4 mph decrease from last year, but still well above league average. Curiously, the most drastic change in Skenes’ pitch mix was a sharp decline in the effectiveness of his changeup.

articles.title: Pirates Re-Sign Kyler Fedko To Minors Deal
body: The Pirates have agreed to re-sign outfielder Kyler Fedko to a two-year minor league deal, per Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. Fedko underwent knee surgery in August to repair a torn ACL, MCL, and LCL, so he’ll be rehabbing for a good portion of the 2027 season.

The 27-year-old Fedko debuted with the Twins this year after spending parts of six seasons working through the minor leagues. He spent about a month in the Majors starting in mid-June, appearing in 14 games and taking 19 trips to the plate. Fedko walked twice and got his first RBI on a sacrifice fly, though he did not record his first big league hit. The Twins optioned him to Triple-A St. Paul on July 10th. He batted.274/.362/.545 at that level with a 128 wRC+ until the aforementioned triple knee injury ended Fedko’s season in early August. Minnesota released him on September 1st, and the Pirates picked him up three days later.

The two-year deal gives Fedko some continuity as he continues his rehab. Meanwhile, the Pirates get a no-risk depth outfielder to stash in the minors for the 2028 season (late 2027 if Fedko progresses quickly). This year was Fedko’s second at the Triple-A level. In 2025, he took 187 plate appearances for St. Paul after being promoted from Double-A in August. He batted.268/.353/.476 with a 115 wRC+, striking out at around average rates and showing penchants for power, speed, and getting on base. The latter three remained on display this year. Fedko knocked 17 home runs, stole ten bases, and walked at an 11.1% clip in 75 games for St. Paul before the injury.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Pittsburgh Pirates
body: The Pirates took a step forward in 2026 but still missed the playoffs for an 11th consecutive season. They’re now set for a notable set of salary increases in arbitration and could lose one of the best bats available this winter to free agency.
